locations.name: Golden Krone Hotel, Bistritz
locations.desc: Harker's last stop of civilisation. The landlord's wife presses a crucifix on him.

locations.name: Borgo Pass
locations.desc: A moonlit mountain road. Wolves howl; blue flames flicker where treasure lies.

locations.name: Castle Dracula, courtyard
locations.desc: A vast ruined courtyard under the moon. One great door, no light.

locations.name: Castle Dracula, the hall
locations.desc: A lamp-lit hall where the Count bids him welcome.

locations.name: Harker's bedroom
locations.desc: A comfortable room with a mirror. There is no reflection of the Count in it.

locations.name: The library
locations.desc: Books in English on every subject; the Count has studied England thoroughly.

locations.name: The forbidden wing
locations.desc: A dim chamber on the unexplored side of the castle, where he is forbidden to sleep.

locations.name: The ruined chapel and crypt
locations.desc: Fifty boxes of earth lie in the old chapel. In one, the Count lies as if dead.

locations.name: Whitby churchyard
locations.desc: Windswept graves above the harbour. Mina's seat overlooks the sea.

locations.name: The Crescent, Whitby
locations.desc: Our lodgings on the West Cliff: a sitting-room with a view of the sea, and Lucy's mother fussing over her tea-things.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study, the asylum
locations.desc: A cutaway to Dr. Seward's study at the asylum, where the phonograph waits and Renfield is always near.

locations.name: East Cliff churchyard
locations.desc: The churchyard above the harbour. From the seat on the old tomb one sees the whole of Whitby, the Abbey and the grey sea.

locations.name: Tate Hill Pier and the harbour
locations.desc: Fishing boats, nets and the smell of tar. The coastguard hut stands under the cliff, its door padlocked.

locations.name: The coastguard hut
locations.desc: A snug hut of stove, charts and ropes, smelling of tobacco and paraffin.

locations.name: Whitby Abbey
locations.desc: Broken arches against the sky. The sexton says the White Lady shows herself in the great window at sunset.

locations.name: East Cliff, in the storm
locations.desc: The whole town stands on the cliff in the howling dark, watching the sea come in.

locations.name: Deck of the Demeter
locations.desc: The Russian schooner lies broken on the sand, her sails in rags, her helm still manned by a dead man.

locations.name: The Demeter's cabin and hold
locations.desc: Below decks it is dark and stinks of damp earth. Great boxes fill the hold.

locations.name: Lucy's bedroom
locations.desc: Two beds side by side, the window looking out on the sea. Lucy sleeps with a faint smile.

locations.name: The steps and lanes, by night
locations.desc: The fog lamps burn dull orange. Somewhere above, the clock of St. Mary's strikes one.

locations.name: East Cliff, by moonlight
locations.desc: Moonlight on the tombs. On the seat, something white, and something black bending over it.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study, Purfleet
locations.desc: My own room in the asylum: the desk, the phonograph, the case-books. Somewhere below, a patient is counting flies.

locations.name: The asylum ward and dispensary
locations.desc: A whitewashed passage of locked doors. At the end hangs the dispensary cabinet, and at the head of the passage a cell I would rather not open.

locations.name: Renfield's cell
locations.desc: A bare room with a barred window facing the old house of Carfax. It smells of sugar, dust and something small and dead.

locations.name: The asylum grounds
locations.desc: Elms, a high wall, and beyond it the ruinous chimneys of Carfax. Sparrows quarrel on the gravel.

locations.name: The Zoological Gardens
locations.desc: Keepers' cottages behind the elephant-house. Far off, a wolf is howling in the afternoon.

locations.name: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth
locations.desc: A long, clean ward of white beds and quiet nuns. In the corner bed lies a thin, grey-haired man I cannot recognise, and cannot mistake.

locations.name: The hospital chapel
locations.desc: A small chapel, candles, a plain altar. Sister Agatha has said it may be done here, at once.

locations.name: Hillingham, the hall
locations.desc: Mrs Westenra's house at Hampstead, quiet as a held breath. A clock ticks too loudly. Upstairs, Lucy sleeps.

locations.name: Lucy's bedroom, Hillingham
locations.desc: A girlish room: a white bed, a deep window-seat, curtains stirring where no one has touched them.

locations.name: The Hillingham garden
locations.desc: Lawn, shrubbery, a tool-shed, and the night coming down. Something flaps against the lit windows above.

locations.name: Kingstead churchyard
locations.desc: The Westenra vault under the yews. A thin rain. Four men, a Professor, and a very small coffin of silence.

locations.name: Hampstead Heath
locations.desc: Furze, bracken and open sky. The Westminster Gazette speaks of a 'bloofer lady' who walks here after dark and leads small children away.

locations.name: The North Hospital, children's ward
locations.desc: White beds in a long ward. In one of them lies a small child with a bandaged throat.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study, Purfleet
locations.desc: My own study at the asylum: the phonograph, the locked cabinet, and a workbench where I have mended many a lock for the sake of the patients.

locations.name: Mina Harker's sitting-room, Paddington
locations.desc: A modest hotel parlour, a typewriter on a writing-table, a basket of sewing, and two people who have lately been very near to ruin.

locations.name: Hillingham, the Westenra house
locations.desc: The house is quiet. White flowers have not yet been cleared from the room where Lucy lay, and the smell of wild garlic still clings to the curtains.

locations.name: Jack Straw's Castle
locations.desc: A roadside inn on the top of the Heath. A fire, a long table, a landlord who has seen worse doctors than us.

locations.name: Heath lane by night
locations.desc: A dark lane between hedges. Lamps stand far apart. Somewhere beyond the trees the church of Kingstead keeps its watch.

locations.name: Kingstead churchyard, the lych-gate
locations.desc: A low stone wall, a lych-gate, a notice board with the plan of the graves, and a sexton's lodge that smells of onions.

locations.name: Kingstead churchyard, by night
locations.desc: An avenue of yews, junipers marking the church path, a clump of alders, railed-off tombs ghastly white in the moonlight.

locations.name: The Westenra tomb
locations.desc: A marble vault, damp and sordid. Coffins on shelves, withered flowers, iron gone to rust. Lucy's lead-cased coffin rests at the far end.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's library, Purfleet
locations.desc: The doctor's book-lined library at the asylum. The phonograph stands on the desk, and the long table is already set for counsel.

locations.name: Mrs. Harker's typewriting room
locations.desc: A small sunny room off the library. Mina has borrowed a typewriter and pinned the whole sad history to the wall.

locations.name: Renfield's room, the asylum
locations.desc: A bare padded room with one barred window upon the park. Sugar-smears on the sill, a sealed jar of flies on the table.

locations.name: The asylum grounds
locations.desc: Lawns, a yew-tree and a high stone wall. Beyond the wall, the dark roofs of Carfax.

locations.name: Carfax: the overgrown park
locations.desc: Neglected grounds behind the high wall. The great square house stares with shuttered eyes; the chapel stands apart among the weeds.

locations.name: Carfax chapel
locations.desc: A damp, ancient chapel. The air is thick with foul earth. Dozens of great boxes lie stacked in the nave.

locations.name: A London street by the cab-stand
locations.desc: The noise of the City. Hansoms, drays and clerks. Somewhere among these streets the Count has left his trail.

locations.name: Carter, Paterson & Co., the carriers' office
locations.desc: A smoky counting-room smelling of horse and ink. A dog-eared ledger lies open on the counter.

locations.name: Potter's Court, Walworth
locations.desc: A cramped court of carts, barrels and washing. The man I seek is said to lodge at Corcoran's.

locations.name: Mitchell, Sons & Candy, house agents
locations.desc: A respectable office with a polished counter and a locked safe. Everything here is discretion and cash.

locations.name: The Harkers' bedroom
locations.desc: A bedroom behind a thick yellow blind. Gaslight, a locked door, and a cold that does not belong to October.

locations.name: 347 Piccadilly
locations.desc: A stone-fronted house, high steps, a bow window, a torn 'To Let' board. Within: dust, damp and the smell of old earth.

locations.name: 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End
locations.desc: A tumbledown house in a poor street. The windows are boarded; the cellar smells of the grave.

locations.name: Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey
locations.desc: A damp, empty house near the river. The last of the boxes lies here.

locations.name: The quay, Varna
locations.desc: Grey water, tarred hulls and a forest of masts. Somewhere out on the Black Sea a ship called the Czarina Catherine is long overdue.

locations.name: Hotel Odessus, Varna
locations.desc: A stuffy private sitting room with a sofa for Mina, a table of telegrams, and a window on the harbour.

locations.name: Lloyd's agency, Varna
locations.desc: Ledgers, brass rails and a clerk who has not yet been told why four Englishmen are so anxious about one ship.

locations.name: The harbour, Galatz
locations.desc: A river harbour in the early mist. The Czarina Catherine lies at her moorings, unaccountably arrived.

locations.name: Aboard the Czarina Catherine
locations.desc: A wet deck, a silent crew and a hold that smells of old earth.

locations.name: Hildesheim's office, Burgen-strasse
locations.desc: A cramped back office, all ledgers and locked boxes. Its owner counts coins with his eyes before his hands.

locations.name: St. Peter's churchyard, Galatz
locations.desc: A walled yard in the grey morning. By the wall lies the man who carried the box.

locations.name: Hotel at Galatz
locations.desc: The men are asleep. In the sitting room Mina's typewriter clicks softly in the lamplight.

locations.name: The steam launch Mina, the Sereth
locations.desc: Night on the river. The little launch throbs against the current, her electric lamp throwing a white road on the water.

locations.name: The rapids on the Bistritza
locations.desc: Brown water, white spray and a broken keel. The river will carry us no further.

locations.name: The bank road to Fundu
locations.desc: A mud road along the right bank, a sky of low snow-cloud, and a long way still to the mountains.

locations.name: Inn at Veresti
locations.desc: A village inn with a fat landlady, a stove, and a great basket being packed with provisions.

locations.name: The road to the Borgo Pass
locations.desc: The road climbs into the pine and the snow. Peasants make the sign against the evil eye as we pass.

locations.name: Below Castle Dracula
locations.desc: A fire in the snow, a ring of crumbled Host, and a ruined castle black against the stars.

locations.name: Castle Dracula, the courtyard
locations.desc: By daylight the castle is only a ruin. The great chapel door has rusted shut.

locations.name: The old chapel
locations.desc: Cold, dusty, and silent. Fifty boxes once stood here. Now only the tombs remain.

locations.name: The sisters' vault
locations.desc: Three tombs. In one lies a woman more radiant than any living, and the room is thick with her will.

locations.name: A hollow among the rocks
locations.desc: Two great boulders and a pocket of shelter. From here the whole plain can be seen through the glasses.

locations.name: The plain below the castle
locations.desc: A white plain, a low red sun, and the leiter-wagon racing the dusk toward the castle.

locations.name: The snowfield at sunset
locations.desc: The wind has dropped. Where the Count stood, there is nothing but dust.

locations.name: Exeter, a study
locations.desc: A book-lined room, a boy at play, and a thick bundle of typescript tied with ribbon.

locations.name: The Lord's chamber, The Ring
locations.desc: The great bed with its faded hangings. The fire is kept high, and the whole room smells of camphor and old paper.

locations.name: The hall, The Ring
locations.desc: Black oak, stag's heads and portraits of Holmwoods who all look as if they had been told bad news.

locations.name: The grounds of The Ring
locations.desc: Lawn, limes and the grey flank of the house. The chapel roof shows above the yews, and the Home Wood darkens the hill.

locations.name: The garden at Hillingham
locations.desc: Lucy's mother's garden: roses, a lawn that has never seen a weed, and Lucy herself under the arbour.

locations.name: The summer-house, Hillingham
locations.desc: A little octagon of white wood and glass at the garden's end. We have taken our tea here for three weeks.

locations.name: The estate office
locations.desc: Ledgers to the ceiling, and a stove which has not been lit since my father last came down these stairs.

locations.name: The village green
locations.desc: Cottages of old brick round a pond. The tenants wait outside the Holmwood Arms and do not take off their hats.

locations.name: The Home Wood, by night
locations.desc: Black oaks and bracken. Somewhere ahead, a lantern is shuttered, and a wire snare sings in the wind.

locations.name: The family chapel
locations.desc: Cold stone, a worn altar and the brasses of my ancestors in the floor. A single bell hangs in the little tower.

locations.name: The Holmwood vault
locations.desc: Steps down into the earth. The air is dry, the lamp-flames lean away from the farther dark.

locations.name: The muniment room
locations.desc: Iron-bound chests of deeds and a desk with a green lamp. The window has been bricked up for a century.

locations.name: The quay, Varna
locations.desc: The Black Sea port on a bright July morning. Gulls, tar, tarred rope, and a long line of Slovak carriers walking fifty boxes up a gangway as if they were carrying their own coffins.

locations.name: Deck of the Demeter
locations.desc: A Russian schooner of no great size, well found and well kept. The boards have been scrubbed white; by the end of the voyage no one will scrub them.

locations.name: The Captain's cabin
locations.desc: A bunk, a chart table, a sea-chest and a lamp that swings. Home, for twenty years of voyages, and the only door on board that locks.

locations.name: The hold
locations.desc: Dark, close and smelling of damp earth and silver sand. Fifty boxes stand lashed in their rows, each the length of a coffin.

locations.name: The galley
locations.desc: A black stove, a rack of pans and the cook's whole kingdom in eight square feet. It is the one warm place aboard.

locations.name: The forecastle
locations.desc: Bunks in two tiers, sea-chests, damp oilskins, and holy pictures nailed over every pillow.

locations.name: The bows
locations.desc: The foredeck and the bowsprit, wet and narrow, with the anchor cable coiled like a sleeping snake. The fog begins here.

locations.name: The wheel
locations.desc: The quarterdeck, the binnacle, the barometer in its brass case, and the wheel itself with its worn spokes. A man could stand here forever.

locations.name: The great hall, the castle in the Carpathians
locations.desc: Black rafters, a hearth like a cave mouth and a council that has not slept. The banners hang as though the wind outside had tired of them.

locations.name: The Voivode's chamber
locations.desc: My father's room, now mine. The bed is too large, the books too many, and the portrait does not like me.

locations.name: The watch-tower
locations.desc: Open battlements above the pass. Far off to the east a ridge keeps its own dark, and on it a beacon that should burn does not.

locations.name: The mountain road
locations.desc: Pines, rock and the sound of cartwheels going the wrong way: the hungry are coming up the road as the levy goes down it.

locations.name: The army's camp
locations.desc: A hundred fires in a bowl of the hills. Men are cleaning mail, and none of them are talking about home.

locations.name: The Reed Ford
locations.desc: A broad brown river and reeds as tall as a rider. Water sleeps, the Turks say, and the enemy is sleepless.

locations.name: The shore of Lake Hermannstadt
locations.desc: Black water under a low sky. A ferry-post, a ring of leaning stones and a mountain that seems to have its door open.

locations.name: The Scholomance, the lecture hall
locations.desc: A stone school under the mountain. The benches are worn, the torches never smoke and nobody here has ever been seen to laugh.

locations.name: The forbidden library
locations.desc: Shelves to the vault, chained books and a smell of cold iron and wet paper.

locations.name: The tithe chamber
locations.desc: Ten seats in a ring, a fire without smoke, and below the floor a sound like a great beast breathing.
locations.date: The last night of the term

locations.name: The family crypt
locations.desc: Cold stone, old wax, and no light at all but what the eyes themselves seem to give.

locations.name: The castle chapel, by night
locations.desc: The little chapel above the crypt. The doors have been left unbarred and the altar candles have burned to stubs.

locations.name: Cathedral Close, Exeter
locations.desc: A fine May morning under the cathedral towers. Rooks, cabs, and a flower-seller with the whole of Devon in her basket.

locations.name: Hawkins & Harker, Solicitors
locations.desc: Mr. Hawkins's office: deed-boxes to the ceiling, a fire kept up in all weathers, and a quill that has signed more conveyances than the Archbishop.

locations.name: The muniment room
locations.desc: A cool vault under the office where the firm keeps what it cannot bear to throw away.

locations.name: The schoolroom
locations.desc: Slates, a globe, a blackboard with a chalk drawing of the Exe, and the faint smell of ink and apples.

locations.name: Jonathan's lodgings
locations.desc: Two rooms above Mrs. Dunmore's linen-draper's. His father's trunk stands under the window, locked these many years.

locations.name: St. Petroc's churchyard
locations.desc: Where the Harkers lie, in the corner by the yew where the sun comes last.

locations.name: The Reading Room, British Museum
locations.desc: Under the great dome, a hundred readers rustle like a wood in autumn. Somewhere in these catalogues is the whole of Transylvania.

locations.name: The castle wall, by night
locations.desc: Hundreds of feet of sheer stone under the moon, and a window left open on the Count's side. Below, the whole country lies bright and silent.

locations.name: The Count's room
locations.desc: An empty room that is not empty. It smells of old earth, and a heap of gold lies in the corner like rubbish.

locations.name: The ruined chapel and its vault
locations.desc: Down a winding stair, the dead air of an old burial-place. Fifty great boxes of earth stand in the gloom.

locations.name: The mountain path
locations.desc: A goat-track under the stars. Far below, a river; somewhere nearer, wolves and a Szgany fire.

locations.name: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth
locations.desc: A long white ward where the Sisters go about in silence. A bed by the window, and a nun who does not leave it.

locations.name: The hospital garden
locations.desc: Lime trees, gravel walks and a few patient convalescents in chairs.

locations.name: The hospital chapel
locations.desc: Small, whitewashed, bright with candles and with a wreath of white roses over the altar.

locations.name: Lucy's room, Hillingham
locations.desc: A white bedroom on the first floor, window open on the lawn. It smells of lavender and of a morning that has not yet decided to be anything but happy.

locations.name: The parlour, Hillingham
locations.desc: Chintz, a piano nobody plays well, and a vase that is not equal to the occasion. Mamma's workbasket sits where a cat would, if she permitted a cat.

locations.name: The garden, Hillingham
locations.desc: A long lawn, a rose arbour and a bench in the shade. Every window of the house is open, and there is a smell of cut grass.

locations.name: Crescent lodgings, Whitby
locations.desc: Two narrow beds under a sloping ceiling, a window full of sea and a landlady who believes in draughts. We have the best rooms in the Crescent, Mamma says, and the worst stairs.

locations.name: East Cliff, Whitby
locations.desc: Grass, wind and gulls. The Abbey stands over the town, and below it the old churchyard hangs on to the edge of the cliff by its fingernails.

locations.name: East Cliff, by night
locations.desc: The same cliff, the same seat, and no one else on the whole headland but me and the moon. And a bell somewhere, tolling slowly, that has no business ringing at this hour.

locations.name: The Abbey steps, by night
locations.desc: A hundred steps down, then a hundred more, between graves and the black water. I do not know how I came to be halfway down.

locations.name: Lucy's room, Hillingham
locations.desc: My own room again, with the window open and a smell in it that is not lavender. Someone is always in the chair beside the bed. Tonight it is Dr. Seward, asleep with two fingers on my wrist.

locations.name: The schoolroom, Exeter
locations.desc: Rows of ink-stained desks, a stove, a smell of chalk and wet wool. Somebody has stolen the speech-day prize.

locations.name: The typewriting room
locations.desc: A narrow room under the eaves that Miss Hallam lets me use after lessons. One Remington stands under a dust-sheet, and it has not spoken for a year.

locations.name: My rooms, Exeter
locations.desc: Two small rooms over a draper's, a gas-ring, a window on the cathedral close and a table piled with shorthand exercises.

locations.name: St. David's station, Exeter
locations.desc: Steam, porters and the clatter of milk-churns. Everything here runs by the minute, and it is the only place in Exeter where I am entirely at ease.

locations.name: The Crescent, Whitby
locations.desc: Our lodgings on the West Cliff. Lucy's mother has the best chair and Lucy has the best view; I have the writing table.

locations.name: East Cliff churchyard, dusk
locations.desc: The seat on the cliff above the harbour, the Abbey black against a red sky, and the gravestones that tell such confident lies.

locations.name: The coastguard hut
locations.desc: Charts, a brass telescope and a stove that smells of tarred rope.

locations.name: Our bedroom, Whitby, at night
locations.desc: Two beds, one sleeping girl, a curtain that breathes, and the sea saying one long word under the window.

locations.name: The dark hold
locations.desc: Water laps somewhere. Timber creaks. I know this place and I have never been here.

locations.name: The Morris ranch, Brazos country, Texas
locations.desc: Dawn on the home corral. The rail is cut clean through, the remuda is gone, and an old hand sits on an upturned bucket holding his head.

locations.name: The stable
locations.desc: Warm, dim and smelling of hay and saddle-soap. One stall stands empty, with a name painted on a board above it.

locations.name: The open range
locations.desc: Grass to the sky in every direction, a water-hole, and a trail that wants reading before it rains.

locations.name: The cottonwood bottoms
locations.desc: Slow brown water under leaning trees. Somewhere in the reeds, something is breathing.

locations.name: Dunning's camp
locations.desc: A fire in a hollow, horses on a picket-line, and one white-socked paint mare pulling at her rope.

locations.name: Camp on the Pampas
locations.desc: Grass to the horizon, one supply-wagon, and a fire of dung and thistle-stalk. Arthur is cleaning his gun, Seward is writing, and the gaucho is looking at the sky.

locations.name: The horse lines
locations.desc: A moon without a cloud, tall silent grass, and the picketed horses stamping uneasily at nothing.

locations.name: The grass at dawn
locations.desc: The wind has dropped. The grass is bright, and everything wrong lies in it.

locations.name: Room 12, Purfleet
locations.desc: Padded in grey ticking where the plaster has been mended. A barred window, a cot, a tin tray. Home, of a kind.

locations.name: The day-room, Purfleet
locations.desc: Seven iron beds, three barred windows, nine lamps and a clock that is wrong in the hour. Everything here is counted by somebody.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study
locations.desc: Carbolic, cigar smoke and a phonograph under a cloth. Somewhere in these case-books I am a column of figures.

locations.name: The scullery
locations.desc: A black range, a stone sink and the good smell of a kitchen that has no idea what is kept upstairs.

locations.name: The asylum garden, by night
locations.desc: Wet gravel under a thin moon, the high old wall and a water-butt. Beyond the wall, the dark mass of Carfax.

locations.name: The chapel at Carfax
locations.desc: Cold stone, a broken window and the smell of old earth. Someone has been bringing boxes into a holy place.

locations.name: Dr. Seward's study, Purfleet
locations.desc: Carbolic, cigar smoke and the faint sweetness of chloral. The phonograph waits on the desk, and the house is quiet in the particular way of a house full of the sleepless.

locations.name: The patients' ward
locations.desc: A long day-room with iron beds along the wall, a stopped clock, and the soft, continual sounds of people who talk to themselves.

locations.name: Room 12
locations.desc: Renfield's room. Sugar on the table, a jar on the window-sill, and a stillness that is never quite restful.

locations.name: The dispensary
locations.desc: Jars, scales and a locked poison-cupboard. Everything here can cure or kill, depending on a grain.

locations.name: The records room
locations.desc: Case-books in rows, copying-presses and a bundle of foreign letters tied with tape.

locations.name: The asylum garden
locations.desc: Gravel, a water-butt and a high old wall. Beyond it, the dark mass of Carfax.

locations.name: Van Helsing's study, Amsterdam
locations.desc: Books to the ceiling, a skull on the globe, and a lamp that has burned late every night for twenty years.

locations.name: The house on the Herengracht
locations.desc: Upstairs, where the stove is kept high and the voices are lowered. The kitchen smells of cloves and onions.

locations.name: The Herengracht, Amsterdam
locations.desc: Gabled houses lean over the black canal. Skaters on the ice, a barrel-organ, and the bells of the Oude Kerk.

locations.name: The lecture-room
locations.desc: Tiered benches, a long blackboard and the smell of chalk and wet wool. The students are early. The Dean is earlier.

locations.name: The University library
locations.desc: Alcoves of calf and vellum under green lamps. At the end of the hall, a press of oak with a brass lock: the rare books.

locations.name: The chapel of St. Nicholas
locations.desc: Cold stone and thin candlelight. Father Pieter keeps the altar plain and the sacristy tidy.

locations.name: Kirchdorf, Styria
locations.desc: A mountain village under snow: low roofs, one inn, a church with an onion-spire. The peasants stop talking as the stranger passes.

locations.name: The inn at Kirchdorf
locations.desc: Black beams, a tiled stove, and a long table where nobody wants to sit with their back to the door.

locations.name: The churchyard, by night
locations.desc: Leaning crosses in the snow. The moon shows three old stones at the north wall, and a fourth shadow that is not a stone.

crucifix.name: Crucifix
crucifix.desc: The old woman's gift. 'For your mother's sake.' I did not like it, but I took it.

garlic.name: Garlic flowers
garlic.desc: Garlic. The peasants ward off evil with it. They must know something.

diary.name: Journal
diary.desc: My shorthand journal. The only thing in this place I can still call my own.

razor.name: Shaving glass
razor.desc: A small shaving mirror. I saw no reflection of the Count behind me.

key.name: Iron key
key.desc: A key from the Count's own coat. It is heavier than it looks.

lantern.name: Lantern
lantern.desc: A good lamp. The castle is dark in places even by day.

stake.name: Wooden stake
stake.desc: Sharpened oak. A thing I should not know the use of.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.desc: A mason's hammer from the chapel.

vault_key.name: Count's keys
vault_key.desc: Taken from the Count's own belt. I can hardly believe he did not wake.

wine.name: Tokay
wine.desc: Golden Tokay. 'Excellent wine', I wrote in my journal.

brass_key.name: Brass key
brass_key.desc: A small brass key. It belongs to some inner door.

a2_lucy_letter.name: Lucy's letter
a2_lucy_letter.desc: Lucy's account of the three proposals: a girl in bliss and despair.

a2_pin.name: Safety-pin
a2_pin.desc: A large safety-pin. It will fasten a shawl at a throat.

a2_shawl.name: Warm shawl
a2_shawl.desc: The warmest shawl we own. Lucy will need it.

a2_lucy_door_key.name: Key to Lucy's door
a2_lucy_door_key.desc: The key to the door of the room Lucy and I share.

a2_hut_key.name: Coastguard's spare key
a2_hut_key.desc: A small iron key on tarred twine.

a2_lantern.name: Storm lantern
a2_lantern.desc: A stout lantern that will not blow out.

a2_cabin_key.name: Cabin key
a2_cabin_key.desc: A key of dull brass, from the captain's pocket.

a2_log_p1.name: Log leaf: Varna to Matapan
a2_log_p1.desc: First leaf of the log, dated from 6 July to 16 July. Varna, the Bosphorus, the Dardanelles.

a2_log_p2.name: Log leaf: the stranger
a2_log_p2.desc: A leaf dated from 17 July to 28 July. A stranger on deck, the search, the Bay of Biscay.

a2_log_p3.name: Log leaf: the mate
a2_log_p3.desc: A leaf dated from 29 July to 3 August. Men missing, the mate, the box.

a2_log_p4.name: Log leaf: the last entry
a2_log_p4.desc: The last entry, 4 August, from a bottle in the captain's pocket.

a2_bill.name: Consignment note
a2_bill.desc: Fifty boxes of earth for Mr. S. F. Billington of 7 The Crescent, forwarded by Hawkins's agents.

a2_rosary.name: Captain's rosary
a2_rosary.desc: A string of beads and a small cross, still stiff from the cords that held them to the wheel.

a2_agatha_letter.name: Letter from Sister Agatha
a2_agatha_letter.desc: From the Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth: 'Mr. Harker has had a sharp attack of brain fever...'

a3_dispensary_key.name: Dispensary key
a3_dispensary_key.desc: A small brass key marked D. It opens the poison cabinet in the ward. Only I, and Hennessey, carry one.

a3_chloral_crystals.name: Chloral crystals
a3_chloral_crystals.desc: Chloral hydrate, in clean white crystal. Dissolved in water it sends a man to sleep. In the wrong dose it sends him a good deal further.

a3_sugar_lumps.name: Hoarded sugar
a3_sugar_lumps.desc: Sugar lumps, hidden in a patient's pillow. Sugar attracts flies. Flies are his stock-in-trade.

a3_fly_jar.name: Jar of flies
a3_fly_jar.desc: A jam-jar with a muslin lid and forty bluebottles. He counts them aloud every evening.

a3_spider_box.name: Box of spiders
a3_spider_box.desc: A matchbox in which large spiders have been kept like cattle. He feeds them flies and they grow fat.

a3_renfield_notebook.name: Renfield's notebook
a3_renfield_notebook.desc: Columns of figures: so many flies, so many spiders, so many sparrows, in a small, neat, terrible hand.

a3_orderly_key.name: Orderly's key
a3_orderly_key.desc: A ring-key on a loop of tarred string. It hung under the night orderly's saucer, where a man hides a key he is not supposed to have. It fits the old cell doors in the cellar.

a3_arthur_telegram.name: Arthur's telegram
a3_arthur_telegram.desc: 'Lucy is not well. Come to Hillingham at once. - Arthur.' It was written, I think, by someone who had not slept.

a3_telegram_form.name: Telegram form
a3_telegram_form.desc: A blank post-office telegram form. Every word costs a halfpenny, and an hour may cost a great deal more.

a3_transfusion_kit.name: Transfusion kit
a3_transfusion_kit.desc: My black bag: silver tubing, lancets, a small syringe, carbolic. Everything a transfusion needs but the blood.

a3_door_key.name: Bedroom key
a3_door_key.desc: The housekeeper's key to Lucy's room. A locked door is the one ward that cannot be argued with.

a3_window_pin.name: Iron window-pin
a3_window_pin.desc: A stout iron pin from the potting-shed. Dropped through the sash-staples it holds a window against anything but a saw.

a3_harker_diary.name: Jonathan's journal
a3_harker_diary.desc: The shorthand journal from the Castle. Jonathan will not look at it and will not part from it.

a3_sealing_wax.name: Sealing wax
a3_sealing_wax.desc: A stick of red wax from Sister Agatha's desk.

a3_ribbon.name: Black ribbon
a3_ribbon.desc: A length of black ribbon from the sisters' sewing basket.

a3_wedding_ring.name: Wedding ring
a3_wedding_ring.desc: A plain gold ring, found in Jonathan's waistcoat pocket among a few coins. I think it was meant for this.

a3_sister_letter.name: Sister Agatha's letter
a3_sister_letter.desc: 'He has had a brain fever. He wishes you to know he loves you, and that he is afraid.' - Agatha, Sister of St Joseph.

a3_lucy_memo.name: Lucy's memorandum
a3_lucy_memo.desc: A crumpled paper found against her heart. Her handwriting is neat to the last line, and then it is not.

a3_gazette_cutting.name: Gazette cutting
a3_gazette_cutting.desc: 'An Escaped Wolf': the keeper's tale, cut from the Pall Mall Gazette. A tall, thin man with a beaky nose was admiring the wolf before it escaped.

a3_smelling_salts.name: Smelling salts
a3_smelling_salts.desc: Mrs Westenra's own salts. They will bring round a faint, but not a drugged girl.

a4_gazette.name: Westminster Gazette
a4_gazette.desc: 'A Hampstead Mystery': children lured by a beautiful lady, found with small wounds on the throat.

a4_wound_notes.name: Notes on the wound
a4_wound_notes.desc: My notes on the child's throat: two punctures, a finger-breadth apart, edges white and ragged.

a4_shorthand_diary.name: Jonathan's shorthand journal
a4_shorthand_diary.desc: Harker's Transylvanian journal in Pitman's shorthand. Few can read it.

a4_ribbon.name: Typewriter ribbon
a4_ribbon.desc: A new ribbon, still in its blue paper.

a4_typed_journal.name: Mina's typed journal
a4_typed_journal.desc: Jonathan's journal and Mina's own, typed in clean black letters.

a4_lock_invoice.name: Undertaker's invoice
a4_lock_invoice.desc: A bill from Messrs. Chubb for 'one four-lever falling-bolt lock for the Westenra vault, with two keys'.

a4_lucy_note.name: Lucy's note
a4_lucy_note.desc: A note in Lucy's hand about sleep-walking and a sore throat.

a4_pawn_ticket.name: Pawn ticket
a4_pawn_ticket.desc: A pawnbroker's ticket: 'One small gold crucifix, 5 shillings'.

a4_key_blank.name: Key blank
a4_key_blank.desc: A blank key of good brass, uncut.

a4_tomb_key.name: Key of the vault
a4_tomb_key.desc: A four-lever key cut to the vault's falling lock.

a4_turnscrew.name: Turnscrew
a4_turnscrew.desc: A heavy turnscrew for coffin screws, and for punching into lead.

a4_fretsaw.name: Fret-saw
a4_fretsaw.desc: A tiny fret-saw with a blade fine enough for lead.

a4_candle_stub.name: Candle-end
a4_candle_stub.desc: A short candle-end of sperm wax.

a4_matches.name: Box of matches
a4_matches.desc: Lucifer matches in a tin box.

a4_oil_lamp.name: Dark lantern
a4_oil_lamp.desc: A lantern with a slide for hiding or showing the light.

a4_putty.name: Glazier's putty
a4_putty.desc: A ball of grey putty, soft as clay.

a4_host_putty.name: Host-putty
a4_host_putty.desc: Putty kneaded with the crumbled Host: a seal against the Un-Dead.

a4_soldering_iron.name: Soldering iron
a4_soldering_iron.desc: A plumber's iron, black with use.

a4_hot_iron.name: Hot iron
a4_hot_iron.desc: The soldering iron, heated cherry-red in the blue flame.

a4_solder.name: Stick of solder
a4_solder.desc: A stick of dull grey plumber's solder.

a4_surgical_knives.name: Post-mortem knives
a4_surgical_knives.desc: My case of surgical knives. The Professor asked for them.

a4_missal.name: Missal
a4_missal.desc: Van Helsing's missal, with the prayers for the dead.

a5_cylinders.name: Phonograph cylinders
a5_cylinders.desc: Dr. Seward's spoken diary, wax cylinders in a stained box. Mina begs to hear them.

a5_harker_journal.name: Jonathan's journal
a5_harker_journal.desc: My husband's shorthand journal from Transylvania, held together by a strap.

a5_whitby_cutting.name: Mina's Whitby papers
a5_whitby_cutting.desc: My own diary and the Dailygraph cuttings about the wreck of the Demeter.

a5_vh_memorandum.name: Van Helsing's memorandum
a5_vh_memorandum.desc: Van Helsing's closely written notes on Lucy's death and on the Un-Dead.

a5_renfield_notebook.name: Renfield's notebook
a5_renfield_notebook.desc: Rows of tiny figures, pages of flies, spiders and sparrows tallied day by day.

a5_typed_transcript.name: The typescript
a5_typed_transcript.desc: Every paper copied in order, in triplicate. The whole case in one pile.

a5_cabinet_key.name: Small cabinet key
a5_cabinet_key.desc: A small key, the sort a doctor hides from his own patients.

a5_carfax_keys.name: Carfax keys
a5_carfax_keys.desc: Heavy keys to the gate, the house and the chapel of Carfax, from Mr. Hawkins' papers.

a5_chapel_key.name: Chapel key
a5_chapel_key.desc: A rusty iron key. The chapel lock is old and stubborn.

a5_sovereign.name: Gold sovereign
a5_sovereign.desc: A bright sovereign. In London, a sovereign opens more mouths than a magistrate.

a5_hawkins_letter.name: Letter of authority
a5_hawkins_letter.desc: A letter over Jonathan's hand and Lord Godalming's seal, pleading our authority.

a5_ledger_copy.name: Carriers' ledger copy
a5_ledger_copy.desc: A copy of the carriers' ledger: six boxes to Mile End, six to Bermondsey, nine to Piccadilly.

a5_agent_keys.name: Keys of 347 Piccadilly
a5_agent_keys.desc: The keys of the Piccadilly house, handed over by the agents with a good deal of reluctance.

a5_counts_keys.name: The Count's keys
a5_counts_keys.desc: A bunch of keys dropped as the Count tore through us. Each is labelled in a neat hand.

a5_counts_money.name: The Count's gold and notes
a5_counts_money.desc: Gold and Bank of England notes, dropped from his torn coat. He paid in cash for everything.

a5_lloyds_telegram.name: Lloyd's telegram
a5_lloyds_telegram.desc: A telegram from Lloyd's: the Czarina Catherine cleared the Thames this morning for Varna.

a5_ship_notes.name: Notes on the Czarina Catherine
a5_ship_notes.desc: Mina's notes, in the Professor's hand: darkness, water lapping, creaking wood. A ship. Varna.

a6_purse.name: Lord Godalming's purse
a6_purse.desc: Arthur's purse. Money, he says, is the only language every port understands.

a6_field_glasses.name: Field glasses
a6_field_glasses.desc: Van Helsing's field glasses, brass and leather, good for a mile of open ground.

a6_whetstone.name: Whetstone
a6_whetstone.desc: A flat grey whetstone from a chandler's stall. Jonathan's kukri has not seen one in a week.

a6_sharp_kukri.name: Whetted kukri
a6_sharp_kukri.desc: Jonathan's Ghoorka knife, edged till it takes a hair from the air.

a6_telegram.name: Lloyd's telegram
a6_telegram.desc: 'Czarina Catherine reported entering Galatz at one o'clock to-day.'

a6_bradshaw.name: Continental timetable
a6_bradshaw.desc: A thumbed railway guide. Mina has marked the Varna line in pencil.

a6_permit.name: Shippers' letter
a6_permit.desc: A paper from the Varna shippers to the Captain and the Galatz agent: they may look in the box.

a6_bill_of_lading.name: Bill of lading
a6_bill_of_lading.desc: Fifty pounds' worth of earth, consigned to one Immanuel Hildesheim, Burgen-strasse 16, Galatz.

a6_ms_letter.name: Letter of introduction
a6_ms_letter.desc: A note from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff asking Hildesheim to be helpful. It carries weight.

a6_receipt.name: Hildesheim's receipt
a6_receipt.desc: The box was handed over to one Petrof Skinsky, a Slovak. Signed, with a thumbprint.

a6_skinsky_slip.name: Boat-hire slip
a6_skinsky_slip.desc: A slip of rough paper found by Skinsky's wall: a boat, a crew of Slovaks, 'up the river by night'.

a6_map.name: Map of the Sereth and Bistritza
a6_map.desc: Mina's map, pencilled with the Count's likely road through Fundu to the Borgo Pass.

a6_typescript.name: Typescript of the journals
a6_typescript.desc: Mina's fair copy of every diary and letter. A thick bundle, still smelling of ink.

a6_roumanian_flag.name: Roumanian flag
a6_roumanian_flag.desc: A small flag. Fly it at Fundu and the villagers will take us for officials.

a6_lamp.name: Electric lamp
a6_lamp.desc: A bright electric lamp for the launch. The boatmen fall to their knees when it shines on them.

a6_provisions.name: Provision basket
a6_provisions.desc: A basket of bread, cold meat and a flask of soup, packed by a landlady who says nothing about why.

a6_furs.name: Furs and rugs
a6_furs.desc: Heavy furs. It is a long way to the pass and the snow is coming.

arthur_burden_spectacles.name: Father's spectacles
arthur_burden_spectacles.desc: Gold-rimmed, folded in the dying Lord's own hand-writing.

arthur_burden_telegram.name: Telegram from Hillingham
arthur_burden_telegram.desc: 'Do not stay away for fear of us.'

arthur_burden_desk_key.name: The Lord's desk-key
arthur_burden_desk_key.desc: Brass, small, worn by a thumb. It opens the writing-desk.

arthur_burden_ring.name: My mother's ring
arthur_burden_ring.desc: A small old ring with a pale stone, in a velvet box.

arthur_burden_intro_letter.name: The Lord's letter to Mrs. Westenra
arthur_burden_intro_letter.desc: A letter of introduction in my father's handwriting.

arthur_burden_ribbon.name: Lucy's blue ribbon
arthur_burden_ribbon.desc: Blue silk, still faintly smelling of lavender.

arthur_burden_ledger.name: Estate ledger
arthur_burden_ledger.desc: Arrears, interest, and the name Crowle & Aske.

arthur_burden_muniment_key.name: Muniment-room key
arthur_burden_muniment_key.desc: Three wards, heavy as a hymn-book.

arthur_burden_signet.name: Godalming's signet ring
arthur_burden_signet.desc: Heavy, worn smooth. Three rings on a field of grey: the Holmwood arms.

arthur_burden_mortgage.name: Deed of mortgage
arthur_burden_mortgage.desc: Three red seals. The whole estate, pledged.

arthur_burden_terms.name: Mr. Crowle's terms
arthur_burden_terms.desc: A neat sheet: sell the Wood, sell the Green, and say nothing.

arthur_burden_petition.name: The tenants' petition
arthur_burden_petition.desc: Thirty names, some of them only crosses.

demeter_voyage_manifest.name: Bill of lading
demeter_voyage_manifest.desc: '50 boxes of earth and silver sand, Varna to Whitby, consigned to Mr. S. F. Billington.'

demeter_voyage_clearance.name: Customs clearance
demeter_voyage_clearance.desc: A stamped clearance for the Demeter. The stamp is crooked, which is the best a bribe can do.

demeter_voyage_candle.name: Blessed candle
demeter_voyage_candle.desc: A beeswax candle from the widow on the quay.

demeter_voyage_hold_key.name: Hold key
demeter_voyage_hold_key.desc: The big brass key to the main hatch.

demeter_voyage_cabin_key.name: Cabin key
demeter_voyage_cabin_key.desc: The key to my cabin. The only lock on the ship that has never been picked.

demeter_voyage_rosary.name: Mother's rosary
demeter_voyage_rosary.desc: A string of black beads, worn smooth by a lifetime of prayer.

demeter_voyage_bottle.name: Corked bottle
demeter_voyage_bottle.desc: A strong bottle with a stout cork.

demeter_voyage_bottle_log.name: Sealed bottle with the log
demeter_voyage_bottle_log.desc: The last pages of the log of the Demeter, sealed in wax.

demeter_voyage_robin.name: Round robin
demeter_voyage_robin.desc: The men's petition for a double watch, signed in a ring so that no one signs first.

demeter_voyage_keepsake.name: The Captain's crucifix and rosary
demeter_voyage_keepsake.desc: A small silver crucifix and a string of worn black beads, carried by the Captain of the Demeter to the last.

dracula_voivode_signet.name: The Voivode's dragon signet
dracula_voivode_signet.desc: A dragon coiled round a cross, worn smooth by three generations of princes.

dracula_voivode_medal.name: Order of the Dragon medal
dracula_voivode_medal.desc: My father's medal, silver-gilt. 'O quam misericors est Deus', and on the reverse the dragon biting its own tail.

dracula_voivode_charm.name: Wolf-tooth charm
dracula_voivode_charm.desc: A grey wolf's fang, set in iron and hung on a thong. It does not keep wolves off. It tells them who you are.

dracula_voivode_warhammer.name: My father's war-hammer
dracula_voivode_warhammer.desc: Iron-headed, ash-hafted, notched on the left. It has killed men on the Danube and it can break a lead seal.

dracula_voivode_draft_order.name: Draft order to the levy
dracula_voivode_draft_order.desc: The captains of the levy are to assemble at the camp. Unsealed, it is only a clerk's handwriting.

dracula_voivode_sealed_order.name: Sealed order to the levy
dracula_voivode_sealed_order.desc: A dragon stands up in green wax. The order is the Voivode's now.

dracula_voivode_radu_letter.name: Radu's letter
dracula_voivode_radu_letter.desc: 'The ford at the new moon. The boyars are divided. The Voivode is young.' Signed with a Turkish cipher and, below, in a hand I know, an R.

dracula_voivode_ribbon.name: Ileana's grey ribbon
dracula_voivode_ribbon.desc: A length of grey silk, still faintly perfumed with rosemary.

dracula_voivode_token.name: Scholar's token
dracula_voivode_token.desc: A disc of black iron stamped with a wolf's mouth. Open to those who carry it.

dracula_voivode_library_key.name: The library key
dracula_voivode_library_key.desc: Black iron, shaped like a wolf's head. The lock it opens is shaped like a mouth.

dracula_voivode_ink.name: Pot of black ink
dracula_voivode_ink.desc: Ink that dries at once and looks a year old.

dracula_voivode_black_book.name: The Master's black book
dracula_voivode_black_book.desc: Lessons in the speech of beasts and the calling of weather, in a hand like barbed wire.

dracula_voivode_ring.name: Ileana's silver ring
dracula_voivode_ring.desc: A small silver ring, cut for a hand that never wore it.

dracula_voivode_standard.name: Broken Akinji standard
dracula_voivode_standard.desc: A green horse-tail on a snapped spear, with a tin crescent.

harker_road_counts_letters.name: The Count's letters
harker_road_counts_letters.desc: Nine letters in a small upright hand: a large, old, secluded house, with a chapel and a high wall, no neighbours who can overlook it. The Count would also like a pond or well.

harker_road_archive_key.name: Muniment-room key
harker_road_archive_key.desc: Mr. Pell's own key to the firm's basement vault.

harker_road_box_key.name: Deed-box key
harker_road_box_key.desc: A small japanned key for the black deed-box.

harker_road_surveys.name: Three surveys
harker_road_surveys.desc: Hampstead: a villa among a dozen others, a bandstand in the road. Whitby: a villa on the cliff, overlooked from the church. Purfleet (Carfax): old, walled, with a chapel, a pond like a well, and the lunatic asylum as sole neighbour.

harker_road_commission.name: Letter of credit and particulars
harker_road_commission.desc: Mr. Hawkins's letter of introduction to the Count's agents, with the draft of the deed.

harker_road_pen.name: Steel pen and ink
harker_road_pen.desc: A pen and a small bottle of ink from Mr. Hawkins's desk.

harker_road_museum_notes.name: Museum notes
harker_road_museum_notes.desc: Notes on the Carpathians: Saxon, Wallach, Magyar and Szekely; the Szgany; the Evil Eye; the name Dracula.

harker_road_ring.name: Mother's ring
harker_road_ring.desc: A thin gold ring, worn at the back. My mother's. She wore it for nineteen years.

harker_road_trunk_letter.name: Father's last letter
harker_road_trunk_letter.desc: 'Jonathan, if you read this I will have been gone a long while. Be a decent man. Be kind to your mother's memory. Write things down.'

harker_road_mina_ribbon.name: Mina's ribbon
harker_road_mina_ribbon.desc: A ribbon from Mina's hair, red, slightly crumpled, still smelling of her soap.

harker_road_diary.name: Travelling diary
harker_road_diary.desc: A small black diary bound for the journey; the shorthand pages are still blank.

harker_road_gold.name: Handful of old gold
harker_road_gold.desc: Old coin of five reigns, from the Count's heap.

harker_road_vault_key.name: The Count's key
harker_road_vault_key.desc: A heavy iron key on a ring, worn at the bow.

harker_road_spade.name: Rusty spade
harker_road_spade.desc: A gravedigger's spade, with a splintered haft.

harker_road_wolf_tooth.name: Wolf's tooth
harker_road_wolf_tooth.desc: A yellowed tooth, picked from the ground where the wolves fell back.

harker_road_ward_pen.name: Doctor's pen
harker_road_ward_pen.desc: A pen lent by the hospital physician.

harker_road_paper.name: Hospital paper
harker_road_paper.desc: A sheet of the Sisters' writing-paper, thin and cream.

harker_road_pocket_diary.name: My diary (torn)
harker_road_pocket_diary.desc: My journal, salvaged from the lining of my coat. I do not wish to read it.

harker_road_sealed_diary.name: Sealed diary
harker_road_sealed_diary.desc: The torn diary, tied with Mina's ribbon and sealed with the chapel's wax.

harker_road_parents_letter.name: Letter to my parents
harker_road_parents_letter.desc: A single sheet, folded small, addressed 'To my Father and Mother'.

harker_road_sealed_journal.name: Jonathan's sealed journal
harker_road_sealed_journal.desc: A torn black diary bound with a red ribbon and sealed in wax: the account of his captivity, which he vowed never to open 'unless some solemn duty come upon me'.

lucy_summer_ink.name: Inkwell
lucy_summer_ink.desc: A squat bottle of black ink. Mamma says it is the Admiralty's, borrowed.

lucy_summer_paper.name: Pad of letter-paper
lucy_summer_paper.desc: Good cream paper from Mamma's escritoire. Rather too good for my writing.

lucy_summer_escritoire_key.name: Escritoire key
lucy_summer_escritoire_key.desc: A tiny brass key. It opens the walnut escritoire in the parlour.

lucy_summer_mina_letter.name: Mina's last letter
lucy_summer_mina_letter.desc: 'Begin with what you see out of the window; then the people in the house; then what you cannot tell anyone else; and last, your love.'

lucy_summer_lilies.name: White lilies
lucy_summer_lilies.desc: Three tall white lilies. The back of the vase.

lucy_summer_forget_me_nots.name: Forget-me-nots
lucy_summer_forget_me_nots.desc: A fistful of small blue flowers. The front of the vase.

lucy_summer_bouquet.name: Hillingham bouquet
lucy_summer_bouquet.desc: Lilies behind, the rose between, and a fringe of forget-me-nots in front. It is exactly right.

lucy_summer_arthur_letter.name: Arthur's letter
lucy_summer_arthur_letter.desc: 'I am no hand at speeches. I only want to know whether I might hope, and I shall not mind a plain answer.'

lucy_summer_seward_note.name: Dr. Seward's note
lucy_summer_seward_note.desc: 'If I am to be refused, let it be plainly done. I could not bear to be managed, or kept dangling, or laughed at kindly.'

lucy_summer_quincey_card.name: Mr. Morris's card
lucy_summer_quincey_card.desc: 'Say it short, Miss Lucy, and say it to my face. I won't mind either, but I'd mind being talked round.'

lucy_summer_ring.name: Arthur's ring
lucy_summer_ring.desc: His mother's ring: a small old band with a pale stone, a little too loose.

lucy_summer_pressed_letter.name: Lucy's pressed-flower letter
lucy_summer_pressed_letter.desc: My father's last letter, written when I was ten, with forget-me-nots pressed in every fold. It still smells faintly of summer.

mina_records_notebook.name: Shorthand notebook
mina_records_notebook.desc: Mina's shorthand notebook: tides, timetables, dreams, and the unanswered questions about Jonathan.

mina_records_hairpin.name: Steel hairpin
mina_records_hairpin.desc: A stout steel hairpin that frees jammed type-bars.

mina_records_ribbon.name: Typewriter ribbon
mina_records_ribbon.desc: A fresh, glossy black ribbon for the Remington.

mina_records_prize_book.name: Tennyson prize book
mina_records_prize_book.desc: The Speech Day Tennyson in green morocco, gilt-edged and recovered.

mina_records_typing_key.name: Typewriting-room key
mina_records_typing_key.desc: A small iron key from Miss Hallam's chatelaine.

mina_records_typed_page.name: Typed page
mina_records_typed_page.desc: A beautifully typed letter, eleven lines with no errors.

mina_records_hawkins_reply.name: Mr. Hawkins's reply
mina_records_hawkins_reply.desc: A typed note from Mr. Hawkins's office: a registered letter for Miss Murray has gone astray on the Bristol line.

mina_records_lost_letter.name: Jonathan's lost letter
mina_records_lost_letter.desc: Jonathan's letter from Bistritz, twelve days late, soft at the corners.

mina_records_almanac.name: Swales' almanac
mina_records_almanac.desc: A dog-eared almanac. The margin notes: 'Tides run fifty minutes later each day.'

mina_records_plumb.name: Brass plumb-bob
mina_records_plumb.desc: A brass plumb-bob on a knotted cord, from the coastguard's lead-line.

mina_records_candle.name: Candle
mina_records_candle.desc: A tall white candle for the bedside table.

mina_records_keepsake.name: Typewriter ribbon and shorthand book
mina_records_keepsake.desc: The Remington's ribbon wound round Mina's Whitby notebook: the two instruments of her gift.

quincey_hunt_sugar.name: Sugar lump
quincey_hunt_sugar.desc: A lump of sugar from Maria's tin. Santa Fe would follow me to Mexico for one.

quincey_hunt_powder.name: Powder horn
quincey_hunt_powder.desc: A horn of black powder, kept dry.

quincey_hunt_lead.name: Lump of lead
quincey_hunt_lead.desc: Spent slugs dug out of Wash's target post and tapped into a lump. Good for ten cartridges.

quincey_hunt_spur.name: Silver spur
quincey_hunt_spur.desc: A big Mexican spur engraved with a P, lost at the ford by one of Dunning's men.

quincey_hunt_running_iron.name: Running-iron
quincey_hunt_running_iron.desc: A rustler's brand-changing iron, taken from Dunning's loot chest.

quincey_hunt_blanket.name: Santa Fe's blanket
quincey_hunt_blanket.desc: Her worn saddle-blanket, soft with years, smelling of her.

quincey_hunt_letter.name: Arthur's letter
quincey_hunt_letter.desc: 'Dear Quincey, Seward and I are sailing for Buenos Aires in the spring to hunt on the Pampas. We shall want a man who can shoot. Come, and bring the mare. Your friend, Art.'

quincey_hunt_lantern.name: Hurricane lantern
quincey_hunt_lantern.desc: A stout lantern, dry as a bone. It needs oil.

quincey_hunt_slugs.name: Cast slugs
quincey_hunt_slugs.desc: Ten bullet-slugs, freshly cast, still smelling of hot lead.

quincey_hunt_bat_wing.name: Bat's wing
quincey_hunt_bat_wing.desc: A broad leathery wing, cut from the creature at the lines. Proof for Seward.

quincey_hunt_sheath.name: Quincey's bowie sheath
quincey_hunt_sheath.desc: Tooled Texas leather, bitten once by a spiteful mare on the Brazos. It has carried the great bowie knife through the whole of this story.

renfield_mercy_spoon.name: Tin spoon
renfield_mercy_spoon.desc: A bent tin spoon that has seen better dinners. A lever for a loose board.

renfield_mercy_ledger.name: Notebook of lives
renfield_mercy_ledger.desc: Renfield's ledger: every fly, spider and sparrow, in a clerk's hand. A sane document about an insane account.

renfield_mercy_sugar.name: Lump of sugar
renfield_mercy_sugar.desc: A white lump, blue-papered. The bait for the smallest and most numerous of lives.

renfield_mercy_jar.name: Jam jar
renfield_mercy_jar.desc: An empty glass jar with a ring of old jam at the lip.

renfield_mercy_flies_jar.name: Jar of flies
renfield_mercy_flies_jar.desc: A jar of eleven small furious lives, held in a palm.

renfield_mercy_garden_key.name: Garden key
renfield_mercy_garden_key.desc: An iron key on a loop of tape marked 'GARDEN'. The spider's, or Hodge's.

renfield_mercy_sparrow.name: Injured sparrow
renfield_mercy_sparrow.desc: A small brown bird with a hurt wing, warm in the hand. It weighs nothing, and it weighs everything.

renfield_mercy_transfer_note.name: Dr. Seward's note
renfield_mercy_transfer_note.desc: A note in Seward's hand: 'Move R. to the quiet wing on Monday. Be gentle.'

renfield_mercy_pencil.name: Stub of pencil
renfield_mercy_pencil.desc: Dr. Seward's pencil stub. It was meant for case-notes and will do for confessions.

renfield_mercy_keepsake.name: Renfield's notebook of lives
renfield_mercy_keepsake.desc: A cloth-bound notebook with a faded crest. The last entry is a sparrow, crossed out.

seward_asylum_ward_key.name: Ward key
seward_asylum_ward_key.desc: The small iron key to the patients' ward.

seward_asylum_clock_key.name: Clock-winding key
seward_asylum_clock_key.desc: Mr. Pym's winding key. He wants it back.

seward_asylum_dispensary_key.name: Dispensary key
seward_asylum_dispensary_key.desc: Kept by Hennessey in the one place nobody would look.

seward_asylum_spare_key.name: Spare dispensary key
seward_asylum_spare_key.desc: Hennessey's spare, hidden where a patient would not look.

seward_asylum_blank_cylinder.name: Blank wax cylinder
seward_asylum_blank_cylinder.desc: A smooth cylinder of wax for the phonograph.

seward_asylum_cylinder.name: Seward's phonograph cylinder
seward_asylum_cylinder.desc: A wax cylinder: the doctor's voice on the night that Purfleet went wrong.

seward_asylum_wet_blanket.name: Sodden blanket
seward_asylum_wet_blanket.desc: Soaked, heavy, ready to smother a fire.

seward_asylum_draught.name: Measured draught
seward_asylum_draught.desc: Twenty grains of chloral in a glass of water. Neither too weak nor too strong.

seward_asylum_forged_slip.name: Forged prescription
seward_asylum_forged_slip.desc: A slip for sixty grains of morphia, in a forged hand, in violet ink.

vanhelsing_lore_casebook.name: Van Helsing's casebook
vanhelsing_lore_casebook.desc: Two columns on every page: what I saw, and what I was told.

vanhelsing_lore_cabinet_key.name: Cabinet key
vanhelsing_lore_cabinet_key.desc: A small brass key, for the cabinet where Arminius's letters are kept.

vanhelsing_lore_letters.name: Arminius's letters
vanhelsing_lore_letters.desc: Three Hungarian letters on the Voivode, the Scholomance and a Styrian village.

vanhelsing_lore_library_key.name: The Dean's brass key
vanhelsing_lore_library_key.desc: Cold brass, warm only where the Dean's thumb has held it. Opens the rare-book press.

vanhelsing_lore_rituale.name: Old Dutch Ordo
vanhelsing_lore_rituale.desc: 'Before the bread is blessed the hands must be washed; before the hands are washed the priest must be shriven; the Collect is said over the bread, and the pyx is sealed last.'

vanhelsing_lore_wafers.name: Tin of unblessed wafers
vanhelsing_lore_wafers.desc: Flour and water, cut thin. Not yet a sacrament.

vanhelsing_lore_child_cross.name: A child's silver cross
vanhelsing_lore_child_cross.desc: Small, bright and made for a christening. It was not made to be put away.

vanhelsing_lore_ward.name: The ward
vanhelsing_lore_ward.desc: A linen square holding a consecrated Wafer, a child's silver cross and a braid of garlic, bound in red thread.

vanhelsing_lore_bag.name: Van Helsing's black medical bag
vanhelsing_lore_bag.desc: Scarred black leather, brass clasps. Lancets, a stethoscope, a bottle of brandy, and in the lid a pyx of consecrated wafers.

interact.take_text: I pulled out a half-burnt stick of ash wood.
interact.look: A smoky fire. The landlord's family keep it burning all night. A half-burnt stick of ash wood lies in the hearth.
The remains of my paprika hendl. Excellent, if thirsty work.

interact.take_text: I took the scrap of homespun cloth. It may bind or wrap something.
interact.look: A rough chair with a scrap of homespun cloth over the back.

interact.take_text: I took the coil of rope.
interact.look: A coil of rope hangs over the back.

interact.take_text: I filled a flask from the barrel. Slivovitz: it will steady the nerves.
interact.look: Plum brandy, by the smell.

interact.take_text: I pocketed the bottle. It gives courage for the road ahead.
interact.look: Golden Tokay, left by the hostess.

interact.go_fail: The hostess has not yet finished with me. I should hear what she has to say first.
interact.look: The door to the yard, where the coach waits.
The Golden Krone Hotel. 'Mittel Land' - the Middle Land, as Bistritz calls itself.

interact.take_text: I decanted a little lamp oil into a flask.
interact.look: An oil lamp, nearly full.

interact.take_text: I slipped the table knife into my pocket.
interact.look: A plain table knife lies by the plates.
The landlord's wife. She wrings her hands, and weeps for me.
A broad man, anxious to speak and unable to.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. The hostess's warning still rings in my ears.
interact.look: A black calèche with four black horses' worth of harness and no horses. The driver waits, tall and silent.
The Borgo Pass. A track climbing toward the Carpathian night.

interact.take_text: I mark the spot, and pull up a sharpened stake that someone left nearby. It may serve.
interact.look: A faint blue flame flickers over the grass. They say gold is buried where it burns.
Bare against the clouds.
A tall driver with a long brown beard, a black hat, and eyes that shine red in the lamp.
Yellow eyes in the dark. The howling is close.
The pack grows bold. Near the driver, they cower.

interact.set_text: I knocked. After a moment, the sound of a heavy step behind the door. A key turns, chains rattle. I wait.
interact.look: A great door, old and studded with large iron nails. No light, no sound.
Stagnant water. A bat flits across the surface.
A rusted lantern, long burned dry.

interact.go_fail: A rusted iron lock bars the way. Something heavy might break it.
interact.look: A path leads toward the ruined chapel at the edge of the castle.
A fire the size of a man burns in the grate. It is the only warmth in the castle.
Laid for one. The Count says he has already dined, and does not drink... wine.
Set for me.
Empty. He does not eat in my presence.

interact.take_text: I took the bottle.
interact.look: Golden Tokay, old and rich.

interact.take_text: I took a handful of garlic flowers.
interact.look: A bowl of garlic flowers, set out unaccountably on the Count's table.
Golden candlesticks, long past polishing.
My bedroom. The Count showed me there himself.
The library.
The door to the courtyard.
A carved face of some forgotten ancestor, scarred with age.
A tall old man, clean shaven save for a long white moustache, clad in black from head to foot. His hand is cold as ice.
A four-poster. I sleep here, though not easily.

interact.take_text: I unhooked the little glass. Whatever he is, he cannot be seen in it.
interact.look: Cutting myself shaving, the Count's hand seized my throat... and in the glass there was no reflection of him at all.
Paper, ink, and no one to write to.

interact.take_text: I will not be parted from my journal.
interact.look: My journal, kept in shorthand.

key.say: The iron key turns. Inside, a mason's hammer and a fistful of garlic bulbs.

interact.use_fail: It will not open.
interact.look: A locked chest. Forced from within? Or from without?
Four candles. A fifth would not hurt.
The hall.
English books on every subject - law, history, geography... and 'Bradshaw's Guide'. The Count has studied England thoroughly.
More English books, thick and well-thumbed.
Magazines, newspapers, and a London directory.
The Count's favourite chair, I think.
It burns day and night.
The hall.

interact.go_fail: Too dark. I need a light before I go beyond that door.
interact.look: 'Whatever you do, do not sleep in any other part of the castle.' This door leads there.
Here, in the moonlight, I let myself fall asleep. I should not have.
A lady's embroidery frame, dusty with years.

interact.take_text: I took the garlic flowers. A superstition? Maybe not.
interact.look: Dried garlic flowers, left on the table. They are old.
Back to the library.
Black with age. Nothing stares back.
One was dark, and had great aquiline nose, like the Count; the other fair, with great masses of golden hair and eyes like pale sapphires.
They whispered together and laughed - a silvery, musical laugh, as hard as glass.
'He is young and strong; there are kisses for us all.'
One of fifty boxes of earth, newly dug, I think.

interact.take_text: With shaking hands I take the keys from his belt. He does not stir.

stake.say: I raise the stake... and my arm will not obey me. Alone, with only this, I am no match for him. Not yet.

interact.look: The lid is open. The Count lies within, eyes open, stony and without colour. Not breathing. A key hangs at his belt.
Worn letters. 'Dracula'. The rest is lost.
Even here, the cross endures. The Count would flinch from it.
Its flames lean toward the coffin.
Back to the night air.
A narrow stair beneath the chapel. Perhaps the road to freedom - perhaps worse.
Cold in August, with a vase of sea-pinks in the grate. Mrs. Westenra says the chimney draws better empty.
Guide-books, a Bible and three novels with their pages uncut. Lucy reads only the ends.
My shorthand notebook, the blotter, and a place where I have written 'Jonathan' and nothing after it.

interact.take_text: I put Lucy's letter in my pocket. It is the only complete account of that wild afternoon.
interact.look: Lucy's long letter, three pages crossed. I have read it twice and shall read it again.
My notebook of Whitby: tides, the price of tea, and the unanswered questions about Jonathan.
My own chair, with the cushion Lucy embroidered badly.
Lucy's favourite. She says the springs are exactly right for novel-reading.

interact.take_text: I take the largest safety-pin. One never knows.
interact.look: Cottons, a thimble, a card of buttons and a paper of safety-pins, which Lucy borrows daily.
Lucy gathers them on the cliff every morning.
The door to the room Lucy and I share.
The way down to the town and the East Cliff.
The way down to the town and the East Cliff.
Ajar, and the night air coming in. She has gone out into the fog.
Lucy, pretty and fair, smiling over her tea. She has the colour of a girl who sleeps well.
Lucy, pretty and fair, smiling over her tea. She has the colour of a girl who sleeps well.
Lucy's mother, in grey silk and a lace cap, with a weak heart and a strong opinion on draughts.
Lucy's mother, in grey silk and a lace cap, with a weak heart and a strong opinion on draughts.
A plain, quick girl from the town. She knows everything the fishwives know.
A plain, quick girl from the town. She knows everything the fishwives know.
A postman in a sea-damp coat, holding a foreign envelope with a convent seal.
Papers in rows, a blotter, and the case-book of the asylum, open at a name I cannot read from here.
'R. M. Renfield, aetat 59. Sanguine temperament; great physical strength; morbidly excitable; periods of gloom ending in some fixed idea.'
Maudsley, Esquirol, Pinel, and a row of bottles with tight stoppers and tighter labels.

interact.take_text: Seward waves a hand: 'Take one dose, Miss Murray, in case Miss Lucy cannot sleep.' I bottle it carefully.
interact.look: Chloral, morphia and brandy, all measured, all locked. The key is left in because Seward trusts himself.
A sugar-smeared jar of flies, confiscated from the patient in Room 12. They buzz without hope.
Well sat in. Many a mad man has told his story here.
Banked low. The room smells of carbolic and cigar smoke.
A large, kind man in a white coat who has been bitten twice and bears no grudge.
A thin, pale man of nearly sixty, quite calm, with a little line of sugar on the table before him and an eye on the window.
A seat fixed on the flat tomb of the suicide's grave. Lucy and I come here every fine afternoon, and the sea breathes up at us.

interact.take_text: Pressed into the moss at the stone's foot, a small iron key on a loop of tarred twine. The coastguard's spare, if Mr. Swales is to be believed.
interact.look: 'HERE LYETH THE BODY OF GEORGE CANON, WHO DIED, IN HOPE OF A GLORIOUS RESURRECTION, ON JULY 29, 1873, FALLING FROM THE ROCKS AT KETTLENESS. THIS TOMB WAS ERECTED BY HIS SORROWING MOTHER TO HER DEARLY BELOVED SON. HE WAS THE ONLY SON OF HIS MOTHER, AND SHE WAS A WIDOW.' Lichen at the foot has been disturbed.
'Sacred to the memory of Thomas Wilson, mariner, lost with all hands in the Providence, 1859. His wife and five children mourn.' Fresh flowers lie at the base.
'Mary Jonas, widow, aged 91 years. She was beloved of many.' She had, the stone suggests, several sons.
Worn smooth. A carved anchor and a ship. The inscription began 'In loving memory' and then lost patience.
A plain cross for a child. Someone has set a shell on it.
Square, grey and enduring, with the hundred and ninety-nine steps going down beside it.
Mr. Swales's bench, black with sea-wet and tobacco.
Unlit by day. It has a lovely view and no flame.
The steep way down to the harbour.
A grass path, and the broken Abbey beyond.
'West Cliff and the Crescent.' Under it, in pencil: 'Mind the steps.'
A very old man, weather-beaten like a sea-wall, leaning on a stick and clearly enjoying a young lady's company.
He lies on the seat, his neck broken, his face frozen in fear and horror. The coastguard says he fell. I do not think he fell.
A stout lady in a bonnet, a guide-book in one hand and a parasol in the other, pleased with everything.

interact.go_fail: Padlocked. The coastguard is out on the pier, and nobody else holds the key. There might be a spare hidden somewhere.
interact.look: A tarred door under a tarred lintel. A padlock that has seen more of the sea than of oil.
The cliff drops straight into the harbour here, black and dripping.
Gulls nest on every ledge.
The same wet black rock, down to the waterline.

props.name: Steps up to the East Cliff

interact.look: Hundreds of years of feet have worn the steps hollow. The iron rail is cold and wet.
Twine, tar, tallow and lamp-glass, and a bunch of garlic hung up by the sailors for luck.

interact.take_text: The chandler waves me on: 'Take it, miss, it's no use to me. Lucy'd not like the smell.'
interact.look: Sailors hang garlic to keep off fever and the evil eye.
Salt and scales and the afternoon's catch.
Empty and smelling it.
The lighthouse lanthorn keeps better time than the town clocks.
Tate Hill Pier gathers sand and gravel at its foot. A ship driven here would stick fast.
Tarred planks and a pair of oars. The coastguard's, by the number on her bow.
Cork floats, coils of net and a dead gull somebody swept in.

interact.go_fail: A constable bars the gangway: 'No one aboard till the Board of Trade man comes, miss. Someone must speak for you.'
interact.look: A schooner of Varna, aground on the sand with her sails in tatters. A cordon of ropes keeps the crowd back.
A broad woman with arms like rope. She has sold twine to three generations of drowned men.
Mending a net with fingers like knots of tarred rope. His eyes never leave the sky.
Helmeted, stout, and fully aware of the importance of his rope.
A tidy, worried solicitor with a pencil behind his ear and fifty boxes he did not order on his conscience.
A great grey brute, cowering under the pier. It sprang from the ship and none can say whose it is.
Back out to the harbour.
A black stove with a kettle that never quite boils.
Blankets that smell of tobacco and wet dog. No dog.

interact.take_text: A knife is no weapon against what is coming, but it cuts rope and ash wood and I take it.
interact.look: A good steel splicing knife with a horn handle, left on the desk.
The coastguard's chair, worn to his shape.

interact.take_text: I take the crowbar. A lid that will not open will open to this.
interact.look: Marline-spikes, a sail-needle, a short iron crowbar for stubborn lids.

interact.take_text: I take the storm lantern. A hold is a dark place.
interact.look: A stout storm lantern, wick trimmed.

interact.take_text: I fill a flask from the keg.
interact.look: Paraffin, topped up that morning.

interact.take_text: I fill a little flask with clean water.
interact.look: Rain water, cold and clean.
A square, patient man whose eyes are always on the weather even indoors.
Where the White Lady shows herself at sunset, in the legend, in the same pose as a woman at a high window. The glass is gone, and the light is lovely.
Half an arch against the sky. The other half is the sea's now.
Cut off at the knee by seven centuries.
The slab of some forgotten abbot. A single line of Latin is left: 'Dominus custodiat introitum tuum.' May the Lord guard thy coming in.

interact.take_text: I pick one sprig, careful of the thorns. Wild rose is a good flower for a grave.
interact.look: Pale wild roses growing out of the broken stones. The sexton says they bloom here in defiance of the wind.

interact.take_text: I break off a straight piece. Ash is good, hard wood.
interact.look: A bough of ash, broken in some gale, clean and straight.

interact.take_text: I fill my flask. Rain-water from the Abbey is as pure as any.
interact.look: A hollow stone full of rain, collected for nobody.
No name left. Lucy says its owner dislikes visitors.
The way back up to the churchyard.
An elderly man with a spade, who talks to the stones as if they were shy parishioners.
The new searchlight on the summit of the East Cliff, untried until tonight. It sweeps the sea like a white finger.
Wet, empty and humming in the wind.
Swinging so wildly it throws two shadows at once.
Shouting orders into the wind that the wind sends back unfinished.
Soaked and delighted. He has predicted this and is not displeased to be right.
A fishwife in a shawl, knuckles white on the railing.
A boatman, praying aloud and quite without shame.
A landlady in a nightcap and her husband's coat.
The mast is intact, but its canvas has been ripped into long grey ribbons.
The helm. Cords bind the spokes. Whoever stood here meant to keep this course whatever came for him.

interact.take_text: Clean canvas, torn from the spare sail. Good for bandages or wicks.
interact.look: Mildewed sailcloth and rope-ends. The lock has been burst.

interact.take_text: I take the handspike. A straight length of ash is worth more than its wooden weight.
interact.look: A handspike of ash, for keeping men in order, which the mate swore would suffice. The crew thought otherwise.
Smashed. The glass lies outward as though something inside wanted out.
Pitch. The deck-house door is bolted with it.
Back to the pier.

interact.go_fail: Locked. The captain must have kept the key by him.
interact.look: The way below. A padlock holds it, rusty and obstinate.
Lashed to the helm, his hands bound over a crucifix and a string of beads, his head fallen forward. Two days dead, they say, and no man in the crowd would touch him.

knife.say: The knots are tied tightly, fastened with his teeth. I cut the cords and lay him down with the greatest reverence I can find. A bottle is in his pocket, and I take it, and the cabin key with it.

interact.use_fail: I need something sharp to cut the cords without tearing him.

interact.look: Back up to the deck and the grey light.

interact.take_text: Under the straw tick, a damp roll of paper in a seaman's hand: the second leaf of the log.
interact.look: A straw tick, a Russian Bible and a crucifix-sized empty nail. Under the tick, damp pages.

interact.take_text: Rolled inside the chart, a third leaf of the log, smeared with something rust-coloured.
interact.look: Charts of the Black Sea and the Channel, with a course pencilled to Gibraltar and a cross where nothing should have been.

interact.take_text: Wrapped in oilskin at the bottom: the first leaf of the log, headed Varna.
interact.look: Oilskins, a pipe and a ledger. The lid has been forced.
A great box, sealed with nails. Stencilled: 'Clay. For Mr. S. F. Billington, 7 The Crescent, Whitby.' It stinks of old earth, and something else.

interact.take_text: Pinned under the lid, the consignment note in two languages: fifty boxes of earth, for Billington, by Hawkins's agents.
interact.look: The lid is off. Earth, black and dry, fills it. In the earth, a hollow the shape of a man's back.
Sealed. The nails are bent outward. It has been opened and closed again from the inside.

interact.take_text: A heavy hammer. If I ever need to drive in a stake...
interact.look: Hammer, chisel, a screwdriver. The mate used it only once.

interact.take_text: A clean length of canvas from the sail-bag.
interact.look: Canvas bag stuffed with old sailcloth and twine.
Out of oil. The wick is black.
A four-poster with Lucy's nightgown thrown across the foot.

interact.set_text: I draw the sash down and shoot the bolt. The sea will have to speak to Lucy through glass.
interact.look: The sash is open to the sea air; Lucy likes it so.
Dresses, hats and a very large muff.
A chair with a shawl thrown over its back.

interact.take_text: I lay the shawl ready by my pillow. If the worst came, she should not be cold.
interact.look: A thick white shawl, the warmest we own.
Brushes, a silver mirror and Lucy's whole hair-ribbon collection.

interact.take_text: I take the flask. Emergencies, as Mrs. Westenra says.
interact.look: A flask of brandy that Mrs. Westenra says is only for emergencies.

a2_lucy_door_key.say: I turn the key. The bolt shoots home with a satisfying noise.

interact.use_fail: I have nothing to lock it with.
interact.look: The door to the landing, with a good lock and, as yet, no key.

interact.go_fail: I cannot leave without the key, and a warm shawl and a pin to fasten it. Lucy will be cold; the night is wet.
interact.look: The door is still locked from the inside. How did she get out?
Lucy sleeps with one hand under her cheek and the sea-wind stirring her hair.

interact.go_fail: Three ways lead on from the lamps, and I have nothing to tell me which. I need some sign: a footprint, a scrap, someone who saw her.
interact.look: Stone steps up toward St. Mary's, vanishing into fog.
The door I came out of.

interact.set_text: Bare feet, a woman's, heading for the foot of the steps. Bare feet! On these stones.
interact.look: Small bare footprints in the wet, going up and to the left. Lucy has gone without her slippers.

interact.set_text: A strip of her nightgown, torn on the railing. She passed this way.
interact.look: Caught on a rusted spike, a scrap of white cambric the colour of Lucy's nightgown.
A dull orange in the thick air.
Another, equally helpless.
A tired night watchman with a lantern and a bad chest.
An urchin of eleven, sitting up long past any bedtime, in a coat that was a man's.
The seat where we sit by day. By night it is a different place altogether.
Black against the moon, with one lit window. The clock has stopped.
The arch stands out with the moon behind it, and something pale seems to hang in the broken window.
The way I came.
She sits upright on the seat, perfectly still, her head thrown back and her lips parted. Her nightgown is wet to the knee.
A tall, thin, black shape bending over her. In the moonlight, something white, and two small points of red like eyes.
Case-books, a blotter, a green-shaded lamp. A drawer that has seen better locks.
Edison's wax-cylinder phonograph. My diary speaks aloud now, and sometimes disagrees with me.
My chair. The leather is worn to the shape of long nights.
A small table under the window, piled with ledgers.
The asylum case-ledger. Dosages, weights, observations.
Where I sort what I have found, before I let myself conclude anything.
My working notes on Renfield. I will set down what I have gathered, and decide.
Lombroso, Esquirol, Maudsley, Bucknill and Tuke. A row of sensible men who did not meet Renfield.
A banked fire, a mantel clock, a photograph of Lucy I should not have kept so near.
