An old campaign chest of instruments I rarely need.
Hippocrates, chipped on the nose. He has heard everything I have said into the phonograph, and has not judged.
Three candles, for the nights the gas gives out.
Laudanum, labelled, locked up in spirit if not in fact. I keep it on the sill so I will not forget the danger.
The passage to the ward and the dispensary.
My assistant, brisk and tired, with a stethoscope round his neck and a rumpled Irish smile.

do.say: 2 September. Renfield has been loud all night, Lucy's name is in every letter, and I have not eaten. The phonograph, at least, never asks how I feel.

interact.look: My study, where the phonograph waits.

interact.go_fail: I should speak to Hennessey before I go in alone to a man like that.
interact.look: A heavy oak door with a barred grille at the height of a face. Something moves behind it, and counts.
The garden door, with a little daylight under it.

a3_dispensary_key.say: The key turns. I take the stock bottle of chloral crystals and a flask of brandy, leaving the morphia where it is.

interact.use_fail: That will not open it. It wants the little brass key marked D.
interact.look: The poison cabinet: chloral, morphia, laudanum, and my one decent brandy. It is locked, and I am the guard.
Hennessey weighs the patients here. A strip of chalk reads: 'R. - 9 st. 4 lb. (down 11 lb.)'. He eats nothing at table.
Scales, a graduated glass and a brass measure. Here I weigh out what sends men to sleep.
Clean rainwater from the roof, with a tin dipper. Good enough for a draught.
Clean sheets for the beds. The lid does not sit quite flat.
A bench no one sits on for long.
An oil lamp, trimmed and lit, with a wire guard.
Some patients ask for it and some are quieter without it. We keep it.
A square, patient attendant in a white coat, with keys at his belt and his hat in his hand.
The cell door, with a grille on the corridor side only.
Iron bars, painted so often they are fat with paint. Through them, Carfax's chimneys show black against the sky.

interact.take_text: Inside the pillow, wrapped in a handkerchief: a dozen lumps of sugar, hoarded from his tea.
interact.look: A cot, a blanket, a neatly folded sheet. The pillow is lumpy: it has been slit and sewn up again with fishing-twine.
A deal table scrubbed white. On it the evidence of an industry.

interact.take_text: I lift the jar. Forty flies, and every one of them counted.
interact.look: Forty bluebottles in a jam-jar, bumbling against the muslin.

interact.take_text: Flies; spiders; sparrows. Each total is added with a flourish. I take the notebook.
interact.look: A school exercise book filled with rows of figures and little crosses.

interact.take_text: A box of fat spiders, each in its own cardboard cell like a lodger. I take it.
interact.look: A shallow deal box with a sliding lid. Something dry rustles inside.
A sparrow hops on the flagstones, quite unafraid of a man who has been feeding it spiders.
A bolted-down stool.
A bucket. The least interesting thing in the room.
He crouches by the wall, muttering numbers, his eyes fixed on a point just behind my head. He is thin as a rake and awake as a lamp.

chloral.say: I speak quietly, hold out the glass, and he drinks it as a child drinks medicine. In ten minutes he is sitting on the cot, calm, and ready to talk.

interact.use_fail: That will not calm him.

interact.look: Renfield, sitting quietly on the cot with his hands between his knees. He looks like a clerk, which he once was.

do.say: He has heard me in the corridor. The counting stops. Then it begins again, much faster.

interact.look: The ward door, painted the grey of institutions.
Carfax: the old house next door, shut up, tumbledown, sold lately to a foreigner by Mr Hawkins's firm. It is nearer than I should like.
The gardener's shed. A row of hooks, a smell of earth and creosote.

interact.take_text: A good claw hammer. I take it, and leave the nails.
interact.look: Pocock's toolbox, with the lid propped by a trowel.

interact.set_text: A man could squeeze through here, if he were thin and determined.

hammer.say: Three nails, and the slat is as firm as the wall. Whatever walked this track will have to find another door.

interact.use_fail: A hammer would do it, if I had one.
interact.look: One slat of the boundary fence swings on a single nail. Through the gap, long grass, a worn track leading to the garden of Carfax.
A bench in the sun, facing the high wall. Convalescent patients sit here when they are well enough to be bored.
Sparrows on the gravel, plump as aldermen. One of them hops closer, as if it had been fed by a gentleman.

interact.go_fail: I cannot leave while Renfield is a puzzle I have not worked out, and while Arthur's message has not come.
interact.look: A hansom with a tired grey horse. The driver wants to know which road.
A four-wheeler hired for the afternoon. 'The Zoo, sir? Regent's Park, an hour or so.'
A gas lamp on an iron standard.
The head gardener, with hands like roots and a face that has seen weather and patients alike.
A boy in a pillbox cap, red from running, with a buff envelope held out in front of him like a tray.
'Zoological Gardens. Carnivora: left. Pachyderms: right. Visitors are requested not to tease the animals.'
Two bars of the wolves' cage are bent outward, like grass in a flood. A wolf did not do this alone.
A plain table outside Mr Bilder's cottage. Tea, a mug, and a folded newspaper.

interact.take_text: Mr Bilder says I may have the cutting. 'Better you than the Missus, who reads it aloud.'
interact.look: 'An Escaped Wolf'. The paper is already soft from the keeper's thumb.
A bench with a view of the wolves and no wolves in it.
Straw for the cages.
A gas lamp not yet lit.
My cab, waiting for the return to the asylum.
A stout keeper in a flat cap, smelling of straw and wintergreen. He has the manner of a man much interviewed.
The keeper's wife on her step, with her arms folded and her opinions plain.
A great grey wolf paces his cage, back and forth, back and forth, with his eyes on the north.

do.say: A great grey wolf is pacing a cage in the afternoon sun, and the keepers look like men who have not slept.

interact.look: A plain door, and beyond it the sound of someone setting out candles.
A made-up cot, white as a bandage.
A sleeping patient, an old man with a rosary round his wrist.
The corner bed. A blanket is drawn up to the chin of the thinnest, whitest man I have ever loved.
Empty. The sister has put a sprig of box on the pillow.
A small desk with a lamp, a ledger and a rosary. The ledger records every patient's fever to the quarter-degree.

interact.take_text: I take the wax. Sister Agatha nods; it is for a good cause.
interact.look: A stick of red sealing wax and a taper beside it.

interact.take_text: I fold Sister Agatha's letter into my bag. I shall want it, one day, to show him how it was.
interact.look: The letter that brought me here, left under the lamp.

interact.take_text: I take a length of black ribbon from the basket.
interact.look: A sister's sewing-basket: thread, thimbles, scraps of black ribbon for shrouds.

a3_harker_diary.say: I lay Jonathan's journal on the table. A little black book, held shut with an elastic band.

a3_ribbon.say: I lay the black ribbon beside the book.

a3_sealing_wax.say: I set the wax and taper beside the ribbon.

interact.use_fail: That is not what I need for this table.
interact.look: A clean little table near the window, ink, paper, and room enough for a decision.

interact.take_text: In the waistcoat pocket, a few coins, a ticket and a plain gold ring wrapped in a handkerchief. He bought it before the Castle. I take it.
interact.look: A man's threadbare coat is over the chair-back, with a waistcoat folded beneath it. The waistcoat pocket is lumpy.
My travelling trunk, still strapped. I have brought one good dress, in case.
A crucifix over the sister's desk. The ward is quiet beneath it.
Three candles for the night nurse.
A basin of cool water and a folded cloth.
A tall, quiet Sister of St Joseph, with a calm face, an English that is better than mine is German, and a hand like a bird's.
Jonathan, in a hospital shirt, his hair gone white. He is sitting up, which is more than the doctors promised.
A young Hungarian sister folding sheets with great severity.

do.say: 24 August. Buda-Pesth. I am Mina Murray no longer in my own mind; I am just the girl who came across Europe after a letter.

interact.look: Back to the ward and the corner bed.
A plain altar-table with a white cloth, two candles, and a missal open to the marriage service.
A small silver crucifix. It is Hungarian and old and the face on it is kind.
Candles for a wedding in the afternoon.
Candles for a wedding in the afternoon.
A worn pew.
A worn pew.
A worn pew.
A worn pew.
A stone stoup of holy water.
An English-speaking priest in a worn white surplice, with ink on his thumb. He has agreed to this at two hours' notice.
Jonathan, steadied between two orderlies' chairs. He has combed what is left of his hair.
Sister Agatha, who has agreed to be the witness for the sake of two strangers and a miracle.

interact.go_fail: Mrs Westenra expects me to speak to her first. It would be a rudeness to go up like a tradesman.
interact.look: The stairs up to Lucy's room. A faint smell of lavender, and of something older.
The garden door, ajar, with the hum of evening bees behind it.
A tall clock that ticks like a pulse. It says a quarter to seven, and the post-office closes at eight.
Mrs Westenra's writing desk: crested paper, pen and ink, a bundle of Lucy's old Whitby postcards.

interact.take_text: I take a form. I should compose the message with care; every word is a halfpenny and an hour.
interact.look: A packet of post-office telegram forms, each with a printed line: 'Sender's name below, address above'.
A table for papers and magazines. A railway timetable lies open.
Bradshaw's Railway Guide, open to the Continental pages.

interact.take_text: I take the brandy. I rather suspect I shall need it.
interact.look: Mrs Westenra's sideboard: sherry, port, and one decent bottle of brandy for emergencies.
A small table by the wall.

interact.set_text: Laudanum, and a great deal of it. The servants were drugged. This was not drink; it was a plan.
interact.look: The port decanter, half empty. It does not smell like port.

interact.take_text: I take the key to Lucy's room. It may be the only ward that cannot be argued with.
interact.look: The housekeeper's key-board, labelled in copperplate. 'Miss L.'s room' hangs by itself.
A fire kept alight in all weathers. The room is warm and the house is cold.
An easy chair by the fire. One could wait for morning in it.
A deal box with Dutch stamps, full of garlic flowers. The scent is enormous.
Umbrellas, a cane or two, and an iron bar someone has stood among them.
A branch of candles.
A kitchen chair, brought in for the insensible maid.
A bust of someone's grandfather, looking disapproving.
Lucy's mother: small, silvered, gentle, with a cardiac flush she thinks no one notices and a heart the doctors will not name.
A young maid with a duster in her pocket and a way of looking over her shoulder at the stairs.
One of the maids, slumped and breathing like an engine, as if she would never wake.

a3_smelling_salts.say: The salts take. She coughs, sits up, and begins to weep. Behind her the others stir. Quincey's cab is crunching up the drive.

interact.use_fail: That will not wake her.

interact.look: Arthur, a big fair man who looks as if he had been struck. He holds his hat in both hands.
Quincey Morris, mud to the knees and a wide hat, standing as if he had ridden in. His voice is the softest thing about him.

do.say: 7 September, morning. The door bell. A small, solid, grey-bearded man with a leather case on the step: Van Helsing, who must have come by the night boat. 'Where is she?' he says, in place of any greeting.
6 September. Hillingham. The garden is full of flowers and the house is full of fear.

interact.look: A white bed with a blue counterpane. The pillow is a perfect, slightly sunken oval.
A chair set where a watcher would sit. A rug, a cushion, a book unopened.
A girl's dressing-table: brushes, a hand-glass, a faded Whitby postcard.
A mirror in which a pale girl, if she stood there, would still look like herself.
Dresses of a summer that ended in Whitby.

interact.take_text: Smelling salts. They will not wake a drugged girl who is truly gone, but they may wake a servant who is only dosed.
interact.look: Her mother's dressing-case, dropped in the night. Powder, hairpins, and a little bottle of sal volatile.
A water jug, a glass, a candle, and a medicine bottle three-quarters empty.

interact.set_text: A trail of petals: from the bed-head, across the carpet, to the window-seat.
interact.look: Garlic flowers scattered between the bed and the window, as though dropped by someone walking away.

interact.set_text: Dew on the soles. She walked on the grass. In her sleep? Or at some other bidding?
interact.look: Her white slippers, beside the window-seat. The soles are wet with dew.
The east window is gone: a ragged hole, glass across the carpet, the curtains snapping in the night air.
We have covered her with a sheet, and with the last decency we had. Her hand has slipped out from under it, and Van Helsing has put it back.

garlic.say: I rub garlic flowers into the door as the Professor showed me.

interact.use_fail: That will do nothing to a door.
interact.look: The door to the landing. A bolt on the inside, a lock outside.

garlic.say: I rub garlic flowers into the window as the Professor showed me.

interact.use_fail: That is no use on a window.
interact.look: A deep window-seat under the east window. In the evenings she sits here and counts the stars. The sash is painted so it will not open. Except that it has opened.

garlic.say: I rub garlic flowers into the chimney as the Professor showed me.

interact.use_fail: Not for a chimney.
interact.look: A small grate, swept and empty. A chimney is a door, if one is thin enough.

garlic.say: I rub garlic flowers into the door as the Professor showed me.

interact.use_fail: That will do nothing to a door.
interact.look: The door to the landing. A bolt on the inside, a lock outside.

garlic.say: I rub garlic flowers into the window as the Professor showed me.

a3_window_pin.say: I drop the iron pin through the sash-staples. The window is now a wall.

interact.use_fail: That is no use on a window.

interact.look: A small grate, swept and empty. A chimney is a door, if one is thin enough.
Lucy, as if asleep. There is more colour in her cheeks than in life, and I am more afraid of it than of any pallor.
The Professor, in his shirt-sleeves, washing his hands in the basin as he thinks.
Lucy, propped on pillows: a white-lipped, still beautiful girl with blue-veined eyelids and a pulse like a bird's.

garlic.say: A garland of garlic flowers around her neck, tied with white ribbon, as the Professor taught me.

interact.use_fail: I do not think that will help her.

interact.look: Lucy, propped on pillows: a white-lipped, still beautiful girl with blue-veined eyelids and a pulse like a bird's.

garlic.say: A garland of garlic flowers around her neck, tied with white ribbon, as the Professor taught me.

interact.use_fail: I do not think that will help her.

interact.look: Lucy, propped on pillows: a white-lipped, still beautiful girl with blue-veined eyelids and a pulse like a bird's.

garlic.say: A garland of garlic flowers around her neck, tied with white ribbon, as the Professor taught me.

interact.use_fail: I do not think that will help her.

interact.look: Back to the house.
A lean-to of tarred boards against the wall. It smells of earth, twine and old mats.
A slatted work-bench strewn with pots, twine and bulbs.
A bed of kitchen herbs. The cook's garlic is green and rank and entirely ordinary, nothing like the white flowers the Professor wants.
A bat circles the lit upper window again, and again. It does not fly like an English bat.
A cab waiting for a fare back to the asylum.
A black-plumed hearse with a black-plumed horse. The undertaker's men take their hats off, one at a time.
Rainwater, and a drowned moth.
A lantern hung on the wall by the door.
A boy from the post-office, perched on the bench with a pad and pencil. He is eating a bun and does not intend to be hurried.

garlic.say: Under the Professor's eye I lay garlic flowers on the coffin-lid and across the lintel. 'It is the old custom of the country where I was born,' he says, and says no more.

interact.use_fail: Not that. Garlic flowers, as he asked.
interact.look: A marble vault at the end of the yew walk. A cross, a name, a date. The door is bronze, and not yet closed.
'Beloved wife'. The lichen has finished the rest.
A weathered stone, a skull and an hour-glass.
'Thomas Holloway, of this parish.'
A small stone cross with a wreath of dead lilies.
A cross leaning at ten degrees to the world.
A wet bench. No one is sitting on it.
A lantern, for the late burials.
Wreaths of white lilies and white roses. Arthur's is the largest, and the Professor's is the only one that smells of anything.
The Professor, bare-headed in the rain, with his hat in his hands and a bag at his feet.
Arthur, motionless as a post. Quincey has an arm round his shoulders.
Quincey, his hat pulled down against the rain and, I think, against my eyes.
The sexton, a leathery man, leaning on a spade and waiting, with the immense patience of his trade.

do.say: 22 September. Rain on the yews. The coffin was lowered an hour ago; the clergyman has gone, and the Professor has not.

interact.look: Van Helsing sits here with his chin on his stick, studying the grass as other men study a text.
A lamp-post standing alone on the Heath, unlit by day, as useful to a child as a church to a heathen.

interact.set_text: A child's red shoe, the strap torn through. It is smaller than my hand. I mark the place.
interact.look: A hollow where bracken is flattened. Something small and red shows under the furze: a child's shoe, with its strap torn.

interact.set_text: White lawn, fine and old, no peasant's cloth. A winding-sheet might look so. I do not like where my thoughts go.
interact.look: A thorn bush by the path. A thread of white lawn cloth has caught on it, fine as a gentlewoman's linen.

interact.set_text: Bare footprints, a woman's, pointing toward the church at Kingstead. They stop at the road; she walked on the grass.
interact.look: A line of broken bracken crossing the slope, and in the soft earth the prints of bare, narrow feet heading north.

interact.go_fail: I should first buy the Gazette and read it, and Van Helsing wants to settle where this trail leads.
interact.look: A hansom waits at the roadside to carry us to the North Hospital, where the child lies.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. I must see the child's wound with my own eyes before I let the Professor's theory rest.
interact.look: The long road back to my asylum at Purfleet.

interact.go_fail: There is nothing to be done at the inn until the Professor and I are of one mind.
interact.look: The door of the inn on the crown of the Heath.

interact.go_fail: It is too early. We must first dine and make our plans.
interact.look: The narrow path that runs north over the Heath toward the church of Kingstead.
A thin lad with a satchel of papers and a loud voice.
A woman in a grey shawl, one eye always on the children, the other on a policeman.
Two small children playing at being the 'bloofer lady' and the baby she takes away.
A tall constable with a notebook, leaning against a rail and tired of questions.

do.say: 26 September. The Westminster Gazette tells of children lured away on the Heath by a 'bloofer lady' and found with small wounds on the throat. Van Helsing read it on the platform and turned white. He will not say why.

interact.look: A neatly made cot. Its small occupant went home this morning.
A small child lies here, white as the sheet, a bandage at the throat.
A sleeping boy with a bandaged hand. He knocked over a lamp, they say.
Bottles of carbolic, lint and linseed. Nothing here for a wound that will not heal.
A table with the ward register open upon it.
Admitted Tuesday, 4 a.m., found on the Heath near Shooter's Hill, laid on the grass 'as one lays a doll'. The same hour as the last two cases.
A brass lamp turned low for the night nurse.
A stove warmed against the autumn. The ward smells of carbolic and boiled milk.
A chair for the mother who has not come.
The way back to the Heath.
The house surgeon, a young man with ink on his cuffs and no patience for fools or professors.
A small girl propped on pillows, watching me with solemn eyes.
A sister in starched cap, carrying linen as if it were a standard.
The door to the hall, and the cab that will carry us back to the Heath.

interact.go_fail: Hillingham can wait; first I must be of one mind with the Professor.
interact.look: The cab for Hillingham, where Lucy's papers still lie.

interact.go_fail: There is no reason yet to go to Paddington.
interact.look: The cab for the railway station and Mrs Harker's hotel.
The Professor stands with his hands to the blaze, watching me as one watches a patient who refuses a draught.
My desk: the diary on the phonograph cylinders, a half-written case note, and a cold cup of tea.
Worn to the shape of an anxious man.

interact.set_text: Chubb's catalogue. A falling-bolt lock drops its bolt by its own weight and can be opened from within; a spring latch shuts itself and cannot. Tombs in the old style are fitted with the first. Four levers or six, according to the price.
interact.look: Medical texts and, between Gray and Bucknill, a trade catalogue: 'Chubb's Locks'. A page is turned down: falling-bolt locks, four and six levers, against spring latches.
My bench. I learned to cut keys as a student to help a locked-up uncle; the asylum has since put the skill to many uses.
A drawer of key blanks, odd wards, and a rusty file.
An old biscuit tin of keys that belong to nothing I own.
The blotter, full of ink and half-formed doubts.
The Professor's bag: it clinks in a way that has nothing to do with surgery.

interact.take_text: I took the case of knives. I pray God I never put them to the use I fear.
interact.look: My own case of post-mortem knives. He asked for it at Hillingham, and I did not ask why.

interact.take_text: I took the heavy hammer. It will drive a stake or a nail equally.
interact.look: The asylum's tool chest: saws, a mallet, a hammer for the loose boards.

do.say: Back at Purfleet with Mrs Harker's typed pages and Harker's own word that he did not dream. The Professor wants me to read them now.
Evening at Purfleet. The Professor has said nothing the whole way home, and I have said nothing back.

a4_ribbon.say: I wound the fresh ribbon onto the spools. The keys strike black and clean.

interact.use_fail: That will not mend the typewriter.
interact.look: Mina's typewriter stands here, its ribbon worn grey and faint. A folded shawl lies next to it.

a4_shorthand_diary.say: Mina's fingers fly where mine stumble. In an hour the shorthand lies in clean black type: the whole of the foreign journal.

interact.use_fail: There is nothing here to type.
interact.look: The machine is ready, the paper rolled in. Mina's shorthand diary would go well on it.

interact.take_text: A spare ribbon, still in its paper. Mina would not mind.
interact.look: Thread, a thimble, a half-darned stocking, and a spare typewriter ribbon in blue paper.
A sofa where Jonathan sits when he is not walking up and down.
Mina has marked the Exeter trains in pencil. 'Quick 3.34, change at Reading.'
A small coal fire, politely lit.
A plain hotel chair.
An oil lamp, wick trimmed.

interact.go_fail: I have not finished here. I must hear Harker and Mrs Harker, and carry back the typed pages.
interact.look: The hotel corridor, and the cab back to Purfleet.
Mina, pale and composed, has the look of a woman who has lately been very frightened and has decided to be useful.
Jonathan's hair is white at the temples. He looks twenty years older than the photograph on Mina's table.

do.say: The Exeter note found me out, and so has the Paddington hotel. A young woman who has typed out a dead man's journals and a living man's nightmares: I take off my hat to her.

interact.look: The way to the front door and the cab for Purfleet.
A cab waits for the road to Kingstead.
The bed where Lucy lay, now stripped, with a tarnished outline of lilies still on the pillow.
Four tall candles, burnt to stubs. Nobody has dared to remove them.

interact.take_text: I took a handful of the white flowers. The smell makes my eyes run.
interact.look: The box that came from Haarlem, addressed by the Professor: a mass of wild garlic flowers, heavy as sin.

interact.take_text: I took the sprigs.
interact.look: Sprigs of garlic stuck into a vase beside the window.

interact.take_text: I untied the bunch.
interact.look: A bunch tied with ribbon to the window latch.
A pretty desk with papers in neat stacks: Mrs Westenra's accounts, Lucy's letters, bills from the undertaker.
A thick Turkey rug, one corner turned up as if someone stepped on it in haste.
Novels, a Book of Common Prayer, the Peerage. Nothing that would help us.

interact.take_text: I took a good length of ash kindling. A carpenter could make something of it.
interact.look: A basket of ash kindling beside the cold grate, from the garden pruning.

interact.take_text: I pocketed the paper knife.
interact.look: A bone-handled paper knife, keen enough to trim a quill or a vein.
The undertaker left a pattern coffin in the hall. Lead lining, oak outer, brass handles.
The Professor's case. Inside lies the tin that came from Amsterdam.
A young maid with red eyes who dusts the same shelf again and again.
The family solicitor, in a black coat and an air of professional sorrow, with his hat held like a shield.
Arthur sits with his face in his hands. He has not shaved in three days.
Quincey leans on the mantel, slowly rolling a cigarette he does not light.

do.say: 29 September. Hillingham again. Arthur has come up from Ring and will not let the Professor out of his sight.

interact.look: The inn door, with a bell that rings once when it opens.
A long table with a cold joint, bread and a stone jug of ale. The Professor is already carving.
A fire where a whole sheep could be roasted. It throws shadows like the wings of bats.

interact.take_text: Behind the barrel hangs a coil of good hemp rope. I take it.
interact.look: A cask of the landlord's best. A coil of good hemp rope hangs behind it.
A rack of pewter pots, a ledger and a jar of loose change.

interact.take_text: The landlord nods: a silver coin is mine to borrow.
interact.look: A pewter cup holding a few coins.

interact.take_text: The landlord sells me the lamp for a florin.
interact.look: A good oil lantern with a slide that opens and closes the light.

interact.take_text: I pocketed the matches.
interact.look: A box of lucifer matches and a handful of candle-ends.

interact.take_text: I filled a flask.
interact.look: A stone jug of spring water.

interact.set_text: The map marks the patrol on the high road. The Heath path by Hampstead Lane is shown unpatrolled, if dark.
interact.look: An Ordnance sheet: the lanes, the Spaniards, Hampstead Lane, Kingstead church. A pencil line marks a horse patrol on the high road at half-past ten.
A square man in a leather apron who has served nightmen, resurrection men and doctors without a change of expression.
A carter nursing a mug of ale and a grievance.
Back to the Heath and Jack Straw's.
The lane toward the lych-gate of Kingstead.
A lamp that gives light to itself and little else.
The patrol's lamp on the corner; the policeman stands under it on his round.
A bench under the lamp where the policeman's beat comes round. A child laid here would be found within minutes.
'Kingstead, 1 mile.'
The constable finds the child by the lantern's beam and bends to it, fumbling for his whistle.

do.say: Midnight is long gone. The child in my arms is breathing, and its throat bears two tiny marks. The patrol lamp is just ahead.

interact.go_fail: The wicket is locked, and the sexton has the key on his belt. I should speak to him, or find another way in.
interact.look: A small iron wicket let into the churchyard wall. The sexton locks it at dusk.

interact.set_text: I trace the plan with a finger: wicket, yew avenue, vault at the head; the alder clump near the north wall would hide four men. The sexton locks the main gate but the wicket opens from inside.
interact.look: A board with the plan of Kingstead churchyard: the church path flanked by junipers, an avenue of yews going north, an alder clump in the north-west corner, railed tombs along the east. The Westenra vault stands at the head of the avenue. A hand has written beneath: 'Gate locked at dusk.'

interact.take_text: I took a ball of the glazier's putty. It has many uses.
interact.look: A glazier's box left by the church repairs, with a tub of soft putty.

interact.take_text: I took the soldering iron.
interact.look: A plumber's bag, left for the vestry roof: a soldering iron, a stick of solder and a pot of flux.

interact.take_text: I took the solder.
interact.look: A stick of plumber's solder, dull grey, forgotten on a stone.
A seat for mourners. Its arm is carved with initials.
The Hollis family tomb: weather-stained, mean-looking in the failing sun.
The lane back toward the Heath.

interact.go_fail: There is nothing for me at Hillingham until I know what we are to tell Arthur.
interact.look: A hansom waits, the driver dozing.
A stooped man with a heavy ring of keys and a long nose reddened by weather and gin.
A sleepy cabman with a muffler over his chin.

do.say: 30 September. The funeral is over, and the sexton will lock up at dusk. In the dusk we shall not be alone: Arthur, Quincey, the Professor and I.

interact.look: The way out, unlatched from within.
A pale marble vault at the head of the yew avenue. 'Lucy Westenra' on the plate, the marble gleaming like a pale ghost.

interact.set_text: A falling lock, four levers. Not a spring latch: it will not shut and trap us inside. The Professor nods, satisfied.
interact.look: Beneath a brass plaque, an iron lock-plate with four lever-slots. The bolt drops by its own weight: a falling lock, not a spring one. We could not be shut in.

a4_tomb_key.say: The key I cut turns on the fourth lever. The bolt falls, and the door gives with a groan that must be heard in Hampstead.

interact.use_fail: That will not open the lock.
interact.go_fail: Locked. I need a key that fits a four-lever falling lock, and the Professor wants me to look at the lock before we trust it.
interact.look: A creaky iron-banded door. The keyhole is rust-stained brass.

a4_host_putty.say: Van Helsing rolls the putty in thin strips and presses them along every crack. The white of the Host shows in the grey like frost.

interact.use_fail: That will not seal the crevices.
interact.look: Where the door meets the frame there are crevices wide enough for a knife-blade. A spirit could pass where an arm could not.

interact.set_text: We crouch under the yew, the Professor's lantern shuttered. A clock somewhere chimes the half-hour. Then something white moves between the tombs.
interact.look: A great yew with a hollow at its foot, where two men could crouch unseen.

interact.set_text: The four of us crouch in the alder clump: the Professor with his crucifix, Arthur with his white face, myself, and Quincey with a drawn bowie. The Professor whispers, 'Do not move until I say.'
interact.look: A clump of alders against the north wall, perfect cover for four men. Moonlight reaches them hardly at all.
The old church, its tower black against the sky. Its clock is slow.
A juniper marking the church path.
Another juniper on the path.
'Ann Foulkes, aged 61. Asleep in Jesus.'
A pointed stone, lichen-eaten.
A stone cross leaning toward the path.
A tomb with iron railing, white against the dark.
The strips of consecrated putty along the door-crack gleam like frost. Lucy cannot pass them, but she must go home to her coffin before dawn.
A white figure drifting between the tombs, with something small in its arms.
A small child, sleeping heavily, two red marks at its throat.
A figure in white, golden-haired, carrying a child. Her lips are red as a wound.
The creaking door. It lets in a little of the night.

a4_turnscrew.say: The Professor and I unscrew the coffin lid, one screw at a time. Each squeak rings through the vault.

interact.use_fail: That is not what opens a coffin.
interact.look: Oak, with a brass plate: 'Lucy Westenra. Died 17 September 1897.' Inside, we know, a lead case.

a4_fretsaw.say: A tiny hole with the turnscrew, then the fret-saw: two feet down one side, across, and the flap is bent back. The candle shows the satin and the frilled shroud, and nothing else. The coffin is empty.

interact.use_fail: The lead is too thick for that.
interact.look: The lid lies against the wall. The lead is dull, soldered along every seam, with a faint smell of sourness leaking out.
The lead casing, cut back like a tin. The satin is faintly crushed where someone lay, and quite empty now.
The lead casing, cut back like a tin. She lies within.

a4_candle_stub.say: I melt the foot of the candle onto the coffin lid so that it stands upright.

interact.use_fail: Nothing to do with that.
interact.look: A coffin with clouded silver plate, a good shelf for a candle.

a4_matches.say: The match rasps, and the little flame stands up in the stale air. The vault leaps into being: spiders, beetles, dust, brown flowers.

interact.use_fail: I need a light.
interact.look: A candle stub on the coffin lid, waiting for a light.
The candle burns with a steady yellow flame. Wax drips on the coffin plate.
Another coffin, plate eaten black by the damp air.
Funeral flowers, brown paper to the touch, and the smell of a drain.

props.name: Oil lamp with a blue flame

a4_soldering_iron.say: I lay the iron in the blue flame until it glows dull cherry. It will bite the lead.

interact.use_fail: That will not do for the lamp.
interact.look: A small lamp with a blue-edged flame, set on the shelf: hot enough to heat an iron.
A web the size of a dinner-plate, a fat spider in the middle of it.
Van Helsing stands with the missal open, his lips moving. He wishes us to be of one mind about what must be done.

stake.say: Arthur takes the stake. Its point rests where the heart lies beneath the pale throat. 'Now, friend Arthur,' says the Professor, 'in God's name, strike.'

interact.use_fail: That is not the instrument.
interact.look: She lies on her back, helpless, in a trance the sun cannot break. The stake must be set above the heart.

hammer.say: Arthur drives the stake home with three blows, his face set like marble. A hideous, blood-curdling screech, the body shakes and twists in wild contortions, white sharp teeth champing, lips cut and foam-flecked. And then it is quiet.

interact.use_fail: I need the hammer.
interact.look: The stake stands over her heart. All that remains is the hammer.
The Professor reads the prayers for the dead while the body settles.

a4_surgical_knives.say: The Professor and I do what must be done, with the steadiest hands we have. The knife is quick; I will not write more of it.

interact.use_fail: That cannot do it.
interact.look: The face is wholly at rest. All that remains is what the Professor calls the old, hard duty.

props.name: Lucy, the mouth to be filled

garlic.say: I fill the mouth with the white flowers. The tomb is thick with their smell.

interact.use_fail: Only garlic will serve.
interact.look: The final rite: the mouth filled, as the Professor prescribes.

a4_solder.say: I lay the solder along the cut and bend the flap of lead back down.

interact.use_fail: I need the solder.
interact.look: The lead casing, opened and laid back. The seam is waiting.

a4_hot_iron.say: The iron bites and the solder runs. We lay the oak lid over the lead and screw it down. The coffin lies as if no one had ever touched it.

interact.use_fail: The iron must be hot.
interact.look: A seam of grey lead and solder waiting for heat.
Van Helsing stands at the door with his hat in his hand, and one more thing to ask of us.
Lucy lies as in life but redder, her mouth full of dark blood, her teeth long and sharp. She does not stir.
Dusk. The sun has set. She rises, as one who wakes from a long sleep, and the smile on her face is not hers.
She lies back in the coffin, eyes open and staring, the red fading from her lips. She cannot move.
The sweetness and purity have come back to her face. She is no longer a thing of terror but only Lucy.
Arthur stands with his head bowed and his eyes dry, the weight of a month taken off his chest.

do.say: Nearly dusk. Lucy's coffin is open before us, and Van Helsing has asked that Arthur, who loved her, strike the blow.
Day. The sun cuts a bar through the door. The Professor lifts the lid, and I see her.

interact.look: A long table, strewn with maps, ink and the remains of a cold supper. Here a company of strangers will become a council.
Candles enough to read by, if not to hope by.
Rows of lunacy and physiology. I once thought they explained the world.
Case-books of the asylum, with Renfield's more voluminous than most.
A modest fire. On the mantel, a stopped carriage-clock and a small stone bust.
A bust of Hippocrates, rather the worse for dust. Hollow, I am told, though I never tested the claim.

a5_cabinet_key.say: The little key turns. Within lie the wax cylinders of my phonograph diary, in their stained box.

interact.use_fail: That does not open it. The keyhole is small and brass-rimmed.
interact.look: A tall locked cabinet where I keep the more private records. A small keyhole, brass-rimmed.
My desk. Ink, blotter, and a pile of letters I cannot bring myself to answer.
My phonograph, the Edison I use for my diary. Its horn is turned to the wall.
A heavy glass inkstand with a stopper.
A small table for the decanter, the one comfort of long nights.

interact.take_text: I took the decanter. It has revived better men than I.
interact.look: Good brandy. Many a night it has served as supper.

interact.take_text: I took the carafe of water.
interact.look: A carafe of fresh water on the floor beside the side-table.
The post tray. Nothing yet.

interact.take_text: I opened the telegram. It is from Lloyd's.
interact.look: A fresh telegram lies on the tray, still sealed with the office's blue wax.
The tall clock in the corner. When it strikes, the house goes to bed, and the nightmares wake.
The door to Mina's typewriting room; the click of keys comes through it.
The corridor to the wards, and Renfield's room.
The garden door.
The stair to the guest rooms, where the Harkers are lodged.
Jonathan, hair gone white at the temples, a man who has seen the mountains' other side.
Mrs. Harker, small and straight, with a printer's patience about her. Her eyes are very bright.
Mina, pale and resolute. Her hands are never still: she folds, unfolds, touches the typescript.
Mina, with a linen band across her brow. She meets my eye bravely.
Mina sits in the high-backed chair, like one expecting to be questioned by a dream.
Mina, very still. She has understood before any of us that she will not be taken.
A broad, keen-eyed Dutchman with a pointed beard. He carries a heavy bag as though it held sleeping children.
The Professor, standing at the head of the table like a physician before a hard case.
Van Helsing, at ease for once, but never idle. His bag is open.
The Professor, with the Host at his breast and grief behind his eyes.
Van Helsing, turning a gold coin over and over: the old hypnotist's trick, made grim.
The Professor with timetables spread before him, already half in Varna.
Lord Godalming, calm in a way he did not use to be. Grief has given him a quiet edge.
The Texan, lounging with a cigar he does not light. He has already counted the doors.

do.say: The Harkers have come. Jonathan, aged by a month in the castle. Mina, small and valiant. The Professor beams at them, like a man seeing hope at last.

interact.look: A sturdy desk, with carbon paper in neat stacks.

a5_cylinders.say: I played each cylinder through, and typed it. Lucy, the wasting, the sick nights. And Renfield's fits...

a5_harker_journal.say: Jonathan's shorthand, page after page, into clean type. The castle, the Count, the boxes.

a5_whitby_cutting.say: My own diary, the Dailygraph cuttings, the wreck of the Demeter. Typed and cross-referenced.

a5_vh_memorandum.say: The Professor's memorandum, in his careful foreign English. I corrected nothing and understood a great deal.

a5_renfield_notebook.say: Renfield's tallies, copied exactly. Columns, dates, a pattern that is not quite coincidence.

interact.use_fail: I cannot type that. It is not a record.
interact.look: A Remington, borrowed from the village. I feed it papers and it gives back order.
Mina has pinned notes, cuttings and tickets in order. Threads of cotton link them. A wall of knowledge.
A good lamp, trimmed bright.
Three copies of everything. 'Never trust one copy,' Jonathan says.
Overflowing with spoiled sheets.
Back to the library.

do.say: Sunlight, a borrowed typewriter, and the whole of a terrible story to set in order. Jonathan's shorthand, Seward's cylinders, my Whitby papers, the Professor's memorandum: each must be typed, and then I will see what they say together.

interact.look: A narrow bed with a grey blanket. The sheets are ripped in strips for some purpose of his own.
Sugar spilled in a careful ring. Dead flies lie in rows like soldiers.
A jar full of flies, kept for the spiders. 'Life,' Renfield calls it. 'Life, Doctor.'
Sugar for the flies. The attendants say he saves it from his tea.

interact.take_text: I took the notebook. Mina may find the pattern I cannot.
interact.look: Pages of figures, dates, little tallies of flies, spiders, sparrows. Each day is a ledger of lives. It might be that the figures themselves mean something.
The sash opens only an inch, and there is a bar across it. The park beyond is grey with fog.
A lamp turned low, the nearest thing to company he allows.
My chair. I have sat here more nights than my own bed.
The corridor and the library beyond.
Renfield, pale and sweating, hands twisting at his waistcoat. For once there is terror in him, not cunning.
Renfield on the floor, back broken, face bruised past knowing. He lives, but only just.
He is at peace at last. His hands are open.
Simmons, a decent, stolid man who has seen nothing, and would rather not say so.

do.say: A scream in the night, then silence. Simmons ran for me. Renfield lies in a glittering pool of blood. Something has been here that was not a man.

interact.look: The garden door of the asylum.

interact.go_fail: The gate is locked, and we have no authority yet to break into Count's own land. Mr. Harker has Mr. Hawkins' keys, and the Professor wants counsel first.
interact.look: A heavy oak gate, bolted on the Carfax side. Beyond lie the neglected grounds.
A great yew with a view over Carfax. Quincey says a man could sit there all night and see the chapel door.
A bench the patients use on fine days.

interact.take_text: I filled a flask with lamp oil. Fire is a thing the Un-Dead respect.
interact.look: Lamp oil for the asylum, kept in a barrel by the shed.

interact.take_text: I chose a straight billet of ash.
interact.look: Stacked ash for the asylum stoves. One could make a stake of it.

interact.take_text: I took a strip of clean linen.
interact.look: Linen drying in the sun. Good for bandages, and torches.

interact.go_fail: We have no business in town yet. There is Carfax first, and the Professor's plan.
interact.look: A hansom waiting for hire at the lodge. London is only an hour away.
A lamp on a post, not yet lit.
The asylum gardener, with a billhook and a villager's longing to be somewhere else.
A cabman with a red nose and a talent for hearing what he shouldn't.
The gate we came by.
A great ugly house, shuttered, with a smell of damp stone. There is no light, and there should not be.

interact.go_fail: Locked. The great lock is rusted, but the Count's hand has oiled it. The key must be somewhere in the grounds.
interact.look: The old chapel door, iron-bound and rotten. It has been locked for years, and recently opened.
A leaning gatepost, green with moss.
A well-head, covered with a plank. It stinks of earth.
A cross, so old that no name remains.
Moss has eaten the seat. No one has sat here in decades.
Harker's lamp, set down on the path, a small yellow world.
Jonathan, white and silent, looking at the house as though it were the castle again.

do.say: Behind the wall: a wilderness. Carfax was always the Count's, and I held the paper that gave it to him. Now I hold the keys that may unmake him.

host.say: I laid a crumb of the Host upon each of the 6 boxes. The earth hissed and was clean.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host can make this earth unfit for the Count.
interact.look: The first stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.
The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

host.say: I laid a crumb of the Host upon each of the 6 boxes. The earth hissed and was clean.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host can make this earth unfit for the Count.
interact.look: The second stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.
The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

interact.look: The third stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.
The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

interact.look: The fourth stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.
The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

host.say: I laid a crumb of the Host upon each of the 5 boxes. The earth hissed and was clean.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host can make this earth unfit for the Count.
interact.look: The last stack: 5 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.
The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.
The altar-stone is cracked. Dust and earth cover it. The Count has made a jest of the place.
A pew, rotten with age. The saints on the wall are scarcely visible.
Strokes of chalk on the stone, in fives, crossed through. I count twenty-nine strokes. Someone has been counting what was brought, and not all of it came here.
One of Arthur's terriers, a small hard dog with a scarred nose and a conqueror's air.
Lamps held high are the best weapon against rats.
The door to the park.
Hundreds of rats in the nave, a rolling grey tide with eyes like coals.
The Professor, bag at his feet, a pyx of consecrated Host in one gloved hand.
Jonathan holding the lamp, counting under his breath.

do.say: The chapel door gives with a groan. The smell: earth, old and ripe, laced with a coppery sweetness. And from the nave, a soft rushing, like a river of small feet.

interact.look: The cab that brought us up from the asylum.
A gilt sign above a smoke-black door: 'CARTER, PATERSON & CO., CARRIERS'.

interact.go_fail: I have no reason to knock there yet. First I must learn where the boxes went.
interact.look: A brass plate: 'MITCHELL, SONS & CANDY, HOUSE AGENTS AND SURVEYORS'.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. We must be armed and in company, and Mina must be safe first.
interact.look: A stone-fronted house with a bow window, high steps, and a torn 'To Let' board. I have walked past it this morning.

interact.go_fail: I have a scrap of paper in Mr. Smollet's spelling, but I do not know where it points. I need someone to read it with me.
interact.look: A narrow alley leads south toward Walworth and its courts.

interact.go_fail: We do not have the keys for those houses yet; the Count's own bunch would open them.
interact.look: A hansom for hire. 'Mile End New Town, sir? Chicksand Street?'

interact.go_fail: We do not have the keys for those houses yet; the Count's own bunch would open them.
interact.look: A growler for hire. 'Jamaica Lane, sir? That be Bermondsey.'
'Bartel Street' points one way, 'Piccadilly' the other, and 'Walworth Road' somewhere beyond a hundred chimneys.
A gas-lamp, not yet lit.
A barrel of winkles, abandoned by a coster.
Jonathan in a plain travelling coat, notebook in hand. He has hardened since the castle.
A thin boy with quick eyes. He holds out a hand without shame.

do.say: London. The Count chose well: a city so large that fifty boxes of earth pass for ordinary freight. But boxes leave marks in ledgers, and ledgers are my trade.

interact.look: A scarred oak counter, laden with forms and string.
A heavy ledger, chained to the counter. Mr. Smollet keeps a hand on it. The page for last month is dog-eared.
Waybills by the hundredweight.
Parcels tied with string and labelled in four different hands.
A high stool for an unhappy clerk.
A smoky lamp, left lit all day.
A notice: 'Carriers are not responsible for boxes of earth, live eels, or the Devil.' A wag has added the last item.
The street.
Mr. Smollet, foreman of the carriers: a thick man with ink on his cuffs and a cautious eye for strangers.
Thomas Snelling, the carter, asleep upright on a sack and smelling of beer.
The mouth of the court, back to the alley.
A long hand-cart. The planks are dented with the corners of heavy boxes.
A rain barrel with a drowned cat's-tail floating.
Grey linen on a line across the court.
Corcoran's bench, where Bloxam drinks.
A lamp, left lit all night by the landlady.
Sam Bloxam, carter, in a greasy waistcoat with a clay pipe in his teeth. He eyes my coat for what it might hold.
A polished counter with a brass hand-bell.
A black safe, bolted to the floor. A discreet agent keeps keys of let property here.
Deed boxes labelled with the names of London squares.
A framed map of the West End. Piccadilly is underscored in red, with the numbers 341-349 outlined.
A potted fir, dusted twice daily.
A chair for clients who arrive with money.
The street.
A young clerk in a high collar, nervous behind his counter, anxious to be discreet.

do.say: A discreet office on a quiet street. The agents sold 347 Piccadilly for cash to a foreign nobleman, and cash buys silence. A good name may buy back what cash has bought.

interact.look: A wide bed, twisted sheets. It faces the window, and Mina has not slept in it.

garlic_wreath.say: I hung the garlic wreath over the window-frame. The reek of it fills the room.

crucifix.say: I set the crucifix upon the sill, facing outward. It is a small thing against so great an enemy.

interact.use_fail: That is no ward for a window.
interact.look: A thick yellow blind covers the window. On a night of full moon it glows like a lantern.
A Bible, a glass of water and Mina's hairpins.
The gaslight, turned low.
Mina's trunk: dresses, writing-case, and a locket from Lucy.
A chair where Mina sat with her mending, in the first days.
The door locks from within. It has a bolt.
Jonathan lies face upward in a deathlike lethargy, face flushed, breathing as a drowning man.
A tall thin man in black, face waxen, eyes red, a bloody scar upon his brow. Beside him, Mina on her knees, her mouth at his open breast.
Mina in her nightdress, white and bloodied, on her knees at the Count's breast. Her eyes are open and there is no Mina in them.
The Professor with the Host raised in an envelope, face like a judge's.
Arthur with his crucifix thrust forward, trembling.

do.say: Mina's door is locked. Van Helsing says: 'Break it.' Quincey and I put our shoulders to it. It gives on the third heave. The room is full of a white mist, and in the mist, a tall thin figure.

host.say: A crumb of the Host on each of the 4: the earth hisses, and the smell is gone.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host will unmake the Count's bed.
interact.look: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.
Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.

host.say: A crumb of the Host on each of the 4: the earth hisses, and the smell is gone.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host will unmake the Count's bed.
interact.look: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.
Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.
A neat desk. Bills, receipts, a bundle of letters addressed to 'Count de Ville'. He pays in cash and writes in a very clear hand.
House-agent receipts, a cab-hire slip, a receipt for a steam launch's passage... All in cash, all in the one hand.
Dust-sheets over everything. The Count lives here as a ghost lives in a house.
A hearth with ash that has no warmth in it.
A hall mirror. Something about it is wrong: it shows the room, and no figure that stands before it but ours.
A chair set facing the door, the way a man sets a chair who expects visitors.
Candles, burned down to the Count's liking: lit only for show.
The front door onto Piccadilly. Its lock is fresh.
Jonathan, white as paper, a knife in one hand and the Host's envelope in the other.
The Professor, calm, guiding.
At the front door: tall, thin, a pale aquiline face. The Count, in the daylight, in a good coat, with a look of cold fury.

do.say: The keys turned at the first attempt. The air inside is dead and sweet. This is the Count's town house and the Count is not at home. Not yet.

host.say: A crumb of the Host on each of the 6: the earth hisses, and the smell is gone.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host will unmake the Count's bed.
interact.look: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.
Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.
Steps down to the cellar. The smell comes up them.
An empty barrel. Straw within, hollowed into a nest.
A broken chair and a gas-bracket with no gas.
A dark lantern, lit and shuttered.
The tally on the wall: six strokes. Six boxes, all here.
The door back to Chicksand Street.
Lord Godalming, a lamp in one hand and the Count's keys in the other. He has not smiled since Lucy.

do.say: The Count's own key turned in a Mile End lock. A poor street, a cellar like a grave, and six pits of foul earth.

props.name: Boxes in the back room (6 boxes)

host.say: A crumb of the Host on each of the 6: the earth hisses, and the smell is gone.

interact.use_fail: Only the Sacred Host will unmake the Count's bed.
interact.look: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.
Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.
The window is boarded. River-damp comes through the cracks.
Sacking, the sort used to pack and muffle.
A stool left by the carters.
A lamp with no oil in it; I refilled it.
The door to Jamaica Lane.
Quincey, rifle in the crook of his arm. He keeps one eye on the stair and one on the door.

do.say: The last of the earth. Quincey Morris has put a bullet through worse in the Texas brush, but he has never been so careful about a door.

interact.look: The hotel where we wait, day after day, for a ship that does not come. Mina is within.
A brass plate: 'Agency. Shipping intelligence.' Lord Godalming has been in and out of it all week.

interact.go_fail: We cannot go yet. We need Lloyd's telegram, the shippers' paper, the train time from Mina, Jonathan's knife sharpened, and Mina's promise renewed.
interact.look: A closed cab waits to take us to the railway station. It will not go until every detail of our plan is settled.

interact.take_text: I pocketed the whetstone. I shall leave a coin on the barrel for the chandler.
interact.look: A grindstone at a ship-chandler's stall, with a flat whetstone left on the rim. The chandler has wandered off to his dinner.

interact.take_text: I took a coil of rope. It may prove a mercy.
interact.look: A seaman's chest. A good coil of rope is on top, tarred and strong.

interact.take_text: I pulled out a length of ash. It will make a stake or a fire.
interact.look: A crate burst by a dropped hook. One slat is a good length of seasoned ash.

interact.take_text: I drew off a little lamp oil into a flask.
interact.look: A ship's lamp on a post, burning oil against the fog. The reservoir is full.
HOTEL ODESSUS. LLOYD'S AGENCY. RAILWAY STATION. And in Greek beneath: 'Sailors, mind the fog.'
A stout Bulgarian harbour master in a salt-stained cap. He has been asked about one ship too often.
A weathered Greek sailor mending a net. He crosses himself whenever someone mentions the dead of the sea.
The door to the quay and the grey harbour.
A faded sofa where Mina rests. At every sunrise and sunset the Professor puts her in trance here, and she tells us what she hears.
Lloyd's slips, the shippers' cards, a map of the Black Sea held down with a coffee-cup. Mina's typewriter sits at one end.

interact.take_text: I took the Bradshaw. Mina will want to consult it.
interact.look: A thumbed railway guide, open at the Varna line. Mina has underlined a time in pencil.
A neat stack of typescript: every diary, every letter, every telegram. 'The facts, in order, are half the battle,' Mina says.
A tiled stove-fireplace, hot as a bakery. The Roumanian chambermaid keeps it at roaring.

interact.take_text: I took two more heads of garlic. They smell worse than any soup.
interact.look: The hotel cook is mystified by Van Helsing's demand for garlic, and has provided it by the basketful.
Roumanian novels, a German guide to the Black Sea, and a Greek psalter nobody has opened.
A paraffin lamp with a green shade. It burns long into the night while Jonathan sits up.
The Professor sits by Mina's sofa with his watch open, waiting for the sun to touch the horizon.
Mina, very pale, her red scar showing under her hair. She smiles to reassure us and it breaks my heart.
Jonathan sits by the window with the Ghoorka knife and a rag, doing what he can with a dull edge.

a6_whetstone.say: Jonathan bent over the stone, and the edge sang. In a few minutes the Ghoorka knife would take a hair from the air. 'Thank you, Doctor. It is a good tool now. It will be needed.'

interact.use_fail: Jonathan shakes his head. 'That will not put an edge on it.'

interact.look: Quincey lounges against the wall, as at ease in a hotel as on the prairie, with the Winchester within reach.
Arthur stands over the table with his hands clasped behind him, lines of sleeplessness at his eyes.
The porter loiters with a salver, hoping for a telegram to deliver and a coin to follow.
Back to the quay and the fog.
A tall desk with a blotter, a letter-press and a pigeonhole cabinet of telegraph forms.

interact.set_text: I traced the ship's entries with a finger. The last is in the Dardanelles on 4 October; since then, a blank.
interact.look: Lloyd's register of arrivals and sailings. Under 'C': Czarina Catherine, Roumanian-flagged, last reported off the Dardanelles on the fourth. No later entry.
Slips from every port from Odessa to Alexandria, all ordered, none about our ship.
A small iron stove with a kettle forever on the boil.
A brass lamp, polished to a mirror, on a hook by the door.
A neat young clerk with ink on his cuffs. He takes Lord Godalming's money for telegrams with great composure.
A heavy man who speaks four languages, all of them politely, and gives away nothing in any of them.

interact.go_fail: The mate at the foot of the gangway will let no stranger aboard. We need the shippers' paper.
interact.look: A battered brig with salt-white rigging, her sails furled tight. She came in on the night tide, and no one saw her pilot.

interact.go_fail: I do not yet know where the box was taken. The ship's papers should tell me the consignee.
interact.look: A narrow passage to Burgen-strasse, where the Jew Hildesheim keeps his office.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. We have barely begun to trace the box.
interact.look: The way back to the hotel where the others sleep.

interact.go_fail: I have no reason to go to the churchyard yet.
interact.look: A path leads up to the churchyard on the hill, where something has been found.

interact.take_text: I took a length of spare canvas. It may be needed to patch a boat.
interact.look: A sail-maker's bale of canvas, lying by his shop door.
Shipping marks: 'Mackenzie & Steinkoff, Galatz. Via Varna, per Czarina Catherine.' The office clerk stands next to it.
A smoky oil-lamp in the fog. The fog clings to the river like a living thing.

interact.take_text: I filled a flask with lamp oil.
interact.look: A barrel of lamp oil, bung loose. A tin cup hangs on a nail.
The Galatz harbour master, weighing us up as we ask about the Czarina Catherine. He has seen stranger cargoes, but not many.
A clerk from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, shipping agents, with a ledger under his arm and a nervous cough.
A plank gangway down to the quay.

interact.set_text: I stooped to the hatch. Earth, dry and foreign, and the faint mould of a vault.
interact.look: The hatch where the long box lay. The boards still smell of old earth, and a few dry crumbs of soil cling to the iron of the clasp.
Donelson's log, open at the last pages. The entries speak of fog, a silent man, and a long box. The last line is blotted.

interact.take_text: I took a yard of sail canvas.
interact.look: A locker of mended canvas. The mate will not miss a yard.

interact.take_text: I took a second coil of rope.
interact.look: A tub of coiled hemp, wet but sound.
The helm. The wheel spokes are dark with sweat. The Captain says no hand but his own turned it for nine days of fog.
A square Scot with a grey-flecked ginger beard. He grips a handspike as if the argument were still going.
A sailor who will not look at the hatch. He makes the sign against the evil eye when we pass.
A young deckhand scrubbing planking that is already clean. He mutters about a tall man at the dead of night.
Out to Burgen-strasse and the quay.
A desk fitted with a hundred little drawers, each with its own lock. A set of brass scales stands on the corner.
'De Ville, Carpathian earth: 12 boxes, consigned per rail from Bucharest.' The Count used a different alias for each leg of his journey.
An iron-bound box with a triple lock. Hildesheim glances at it every time we move.
Row on row of leather account books, spines marked in German and Hebrew.

interact.take_text: I took the forgotten coin. It might serve for a Slovak's hand later.
interact.look: A shallow dish of Roumanian silver. A small coin lies next to it, apparently forgotten.
A stove that has not been properly warm for years. Hildesheim does not like to spend.
A dark, narrow man in a rusty black coat, who looks at everything first as a price, and then as a risk.
The way back down to the harbour.

interact.set_text: I lifted the sheet. One wound, at the throat, as sharp and exact as a surgeon's. Wolves tear; they do not choose.
interact.look: A Slovak lies under a sheet by the wall. His throat is torn open, clean as by one bite, and nothing else is disturbed. It is not the work of wolves.
Roumanian and Greek script, a name worn away. Fresh flowers lie before it.
'Maria, wife of a Danubian pilot.' She has been dead seven years.
An iron cross with a sprig of garlic wired to the arm. The folk here know of the Un-Dead too.
A tin lantern left by the sexton, still lit.

interact.take_text: I cut a sprig of wild rose.
interact.look: A late wild rose, hips red among the thorns. Van Helsing swears by it.
A tired old priest in a black soutane, who says his office over the dead man in a low voice and will not speak ill of wolves.
A woman in a black headscarf, wringing her apron. She says she saw a very tall man in the lane.

do.say: The yard is quiet. A sheet covers what lies by the wall.

interact.look: The way down to the quay and the river.
Mina's typewriter, a lamp, a spread of maps and the whole case in order. She works quietly while the men sleep.

interact.take_text: I took the typescript; every fact we hold is in it.
interact.look: Mina's typescripts, tied with a ribbon.

interact.take_text: I folded the map into my coat.
interact.look: A large-scale map of the Sereth and the Bistritza. Mina has pencilled a thin line from Galatz to the Borgo Pass.
A stove with a copper kettle, still warm.
Jonathan lies on the bed in his boots, asleep at last.
The Professor, awake and alert, wearing the face he put on at the grave of Lucy.
A fat river-trader summoned by Lord Godalming. Money has already begun to speak.
Lord Godalming's launch, named for Mina. She is small, lean and fast, with a boiler that eats wood like a furnace.

wood.say: I stoked the grate. The gauge needle crept up, then began to shiver.

interact.use_fail: The boiler needs wood for fuel.
interact.look: The little boiler, cold at the grate. It wants wood, and plenty of it, before the gauge will rise.

oil.say: A few drops of oil on each bearing. The engine purred.

interact.use_fail: The engine needs oil.
interact.look: A compact little engine, its bearings dry as bone. A touch of oil will keep it from seizing.

interact.take_text: I carried an armful of logs aboard.
interact.look: A neat stack of split logs on the quay. We shall need all of it before Fundu.

a6_roumanian_flag.say: The little Roumanian flag snapped in the wind. Villagers on the bank will take us for officials.

interact.use_fail: A flag of the country would serve here.
interact.look: A bare flagstaff at the stern. A flag will give us the look of officials, and fewer questions on the river.

a6_lamp.say: The electric lamp threw its road of white across the water. Every boat ahead of us is now to be found.

interact.use_fail: A strong lamp would serve in this bracket.
interact.look: An iron bracket at the bow, built for a searchlight.

a6_map.say: Mina's map told its story. The Count's boat must leave the Sereth at the junction by Fundu and enter the Bistritza. We pencilled the turn.

interact.use_fail: Without Mina's map there is nothing to plot.
interact.look: A chart table under a tarpaulin. The sheet is blank, waiting for a map.

interact.go_fail: We are not ready. Fuel, oil, lamp, flag and chart must all be in order, and we must know which river the boat took.
interact.look: The wheel. Once all is ready, Lord Godalming will take us upstream at full steam.
Jonathan keeps watch at the bow, one hand on the kukri hilt. His eyes never leave the water.
A Slovak on a drifting skiff, his lantern held low and his face turned from the light. He looks at us as at a ghost.
A raftsman crouched over his poles. He crossed himself twice when the lamp struck him.
The Mina lies on a shingle spit with a plank sprung amidships. A seam has opened below the waterline.

wood.say: A length of ash across the break. It is a splint.

rope.say: Rope lashed tight, turn upon turn.

cloth.say: Canvas drawn under the seam. The leak slowed to a drip.

interact.use_fail: That will not mend the keel.
interact.look: The broken plank. It wants a timber splint, rope to lash it and canvas to stop the water. Three things, all of which we carry.

interact.take_text: I dragged the spar up the bank. It will serve as a splint.
interact.look: A good straight spar, washed up by the rapids.
A pole with a red rag, planted by raftsmen. Beyond it the river drops three feet at a time.
A farmer's cooking-fire, ringed with stones. His wife offers us tea in a tin cup.
A farmer with an acre of sheep above the falls, who has watched our launch grind itself on his rocks with something like sympathy.
Jonathan stands in the shallows with a sodden coat and a stubborn jaw, working the launch off the rocks.
Arthur rolls his sleeves, wet to the elbow, with the look of a man who would sooner fix the boat than think.
A roadside sign swinging in the wind: a crowned eagle, over the legend 'Fundu'. Behind it, the lights of the little inn.

interact.set_text: Fresh cuts in the post and a heap of straw packed under the arm: the Szgany boat put in here at dawn.
interact.look: FUNDU. The Sereth bridge. Bistritza. Someone has scored a fresh knife-mark under the last arm: the Szgany boat turned this way.
A low sledge on runners, for the road when the snow closes it. 'Russian fashion,' says Quincey.
A smoking fire at the roadside. The horses steam beside it.
A hay bale, with dry grass for the horses.
A woolly-bearded innkeeper at his doorstep, wrapped in sheepskin. He has news for those who sit down and pay.
Quincey, mud to his thighs, whittling a stick and watching the clouds. 'Snow by dark, Doc.'
A grey wolf at the edge of the pines, watching us with yellow eyes. There are more behind it.

interact.go_fail: We are not ready. The Professor must buy the carriage, we need provisions and furs, and I owe Jonathan a letter.
interact.look: The inn yard, where our carriage waits.
A great green-tiled stove that warms the whole room. The landlady's cat lives on top of it.

interact.take_text: I took the basket. It weighs a stone.
interact.look: A huge covered basket: black bread, smoked sausage, cheese, a flask of plum brandy and a pot of paprika stew in a cloth.

interact.take_text: I took two heavy furs and a rug. We shall be glad of them.
interact.look: Sheepskin coats, a bear rug and two travelling-furs, hanging on pegs.

interact.take_text: I took a plait of garlic; the Professor will be pleased.
interact.look: A long plait of garlic on the wall. The landlady says it keeps off 'things'.

interact.set_text: I wrote to Jonathan: 'We are truly in the hands of God.' I put it with the Professor's own dispatch for Lord Godalming.
interact.look: A table with a cracked inkwell, and paper. I have a letter to write to Jonathan, which he may never read.
A large, kind woman who will not look at my forehead and will not stop packing food into my arms.
The Professor, counting money onto the table, checking horses through the window.
The four-in-hand the Professor assembled from the farmers' horses and a farm cart's body. Not elegant, but it has brought us across half the Carpathians.
Left, a wide cart-road dropping to a valley. Not the way Jonathan described.
Right, a narrow track, climbing between rocks. It looks like a sheep-walk.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. I must name the road from Jonathan's journal, the wolves must be driven off, and the Professor wants a wild rose for the lid of every grave.
interact.look: A grass-grown road under the pines, rising towards a black notch in the mountains: the Borgo Pass, and beyond, the castle.

interact.take_text: I cut a sprig of wild rose.
interact.look: A dog-rose, scarlet with hips against the snow. The Professor says it keeps the Un-Dead in their coffins.

interact.take_text: I took an armful of dry logs for the night's fire.
interact.look: A woodpile at a shrine to the Virgin, left for travellers.
A wooden crucifix under a small tin roof, hung with ribbons and fresh garlic.
A woman with a basket of eggs. She makes the sign of the horns at my forehead and presses garlic into my palm.
The Professor, with a hand always near his satchel, watching me out of the corner of his eye.
A large grey wolf on the ridge, motionless. Its pack waits behind the rocks.
A black bulk against the stars. Somewhere inside it, three women sleep and wait for dark.

host.say: Van Helsing crumbled the Host into dust and strewed it round the ring. 'In this circle you are safe, Madam Mina.'

interact.use_fail: The circle must be drawn with the Sacred Wafer.
interact.look: A circle of trampled snow, wide enough for a woman to sit in with a fire. Here the Professor will make the holy circle.

wood.say: The fire caught. Sparks rose into the dark, and the snow around us glowed red.

interact.use_fail: The fire needs wood.
interact.look: A hollow in the snow ringed by stones, ready for a fire. It must burn all night.

interact.take_text: I broke a length of wood from the bough.
interact.look: A great bough of pine, dry as paper under the snow.

interact.take_text: I split off more wood. The fire must last till dawn.
interact.look: A dead pine, snapped by the wind. Its resin will burn for hours.

crucifix.say: I planted the crucifix at the ring's edge, facing the castle.

interact.look: A crucifix propped in the snow at the edge of the ring. It is not strictly needed, but the Professor says it does no harm.
The carriage stands with its horses tethered in the lee. The animals scream if I go near; they have smelt something.
Mina sits on a fur at the heart of the ring, her shawl drawn tight, her eyes on the black castle and her hands twisting in her lap.
A lovely, pale woman in white, her black hair streaming in the wind. She has no footprints in the snow.
A dark sister with red lips and a hungry smile.
The third sister, the fairest, reaches towards me. I know that face from Jonathan's journal.
A white wolf circles the ring at a distance, baring its teeth, but it will not cross the line.

interact.go_fail: The door is rusted shut. It will need a blacksmith's blows.

hammer.say: I struck the hinges and the rust flew like blood. At the fifth blow the door groaned and gave.

interact.use_fail: That will not move the door.
interact.look: A double door, eaten red with rust, the hinges frozen into the stone. It will not move for any hand.

host.say: I laid a portion of the Host in the gateway. Whatever returns here will find the door shut.

interact.use_fail: The gate can be sealed with the Wafer.
interact.look: The castle's main gate, a gaping arch of black stone. A little of the wafer on its sill will keep him from using it.

interact.go_fail: Not yet. The castle must be sealed first, so that nothing is left behind me.
interact.look: The track down the hill to the circle, where Mina waits. I must bring her away before the afternoon dies.
A wayside crucifix with its arm sheared off. Someone has pushed it over, and long ago.
A dry well, choked with snow. I will not look in.
The cart's axle is broken; it has lain here for years. A little straw is still damp underneath.
The broken door and the pale winter light beyond.

interact.go_fail: The sweetness of that air is a charm. I must ward myself against it first: garlic or the crucifix.

garlic_wreath.say: I hung the garlic wreath on my neck and the sweetness curdled. Only the stone cold remained.

crucifix.say: I held the crucifix before me and the charm shrank to a whisper.

interact.use_fail: That will not ward against the charm.
interact.look: An iron door, dark and cold, with a small grating. The air that comes through it is sweet and wrong, and tugs at my mind. I must be warded before I go in.

host.say: I laid a piece of the Sacred Wafer in the tomb. He will find no rest here, ever again.

interact.use_fail: Only the Wafer will sterilise this earth.
interact.look: A great tomb, higher than the rest, with the name 'DRACULA' cut in the stone. The lid is off; inside, only a long hollow and a few crumbs of earth. Empty, by day.
A bare stone-and-wood altar. Years of dust, a rat's nest, and one tarnished candlestick.

interact.take_text: I broke off the pew's leg, a stout length of oak.
interact.look: A broken pew. One leg is a fine length of oak that might make a stake.
A battered silver cross at the altar's rear. The stone beneath is clean, as though regularly scrubbed.

do.say: The chapel is silent as a held breath. I must remember: do not look too long at any face in this house.

interact.look: Back to the chapel and the daylight.
A tomb of white stone, its lid pushed aside. In it, a woman lies in white, her lips red and parted, her breast rising a little. Utterly beautiful, utterly still.
A second tomb, lidless. A dark woman sleeps within it, her hair wound over her shoulders like black rope.
A third tomb. The third woman is fair and flushed, her cheek resting on her hand like a girl asleep.

interact.take_text: I picked up the ash. It will make one more stake if I need it.
interact.look: A mason's chest left in the vault. One stout wooden mallet-head remains, and a lump of ash for a stake.
The fair sister, eyes shut. Day has made her helpless, and I must not hesitate.
The dark sister, eyes shut, lips curled in her sleep.
The third sister, as young-seeming as a girl, one hand under her cheek.
A boulder the size of a haystack. Together with its twin it makes a pocket out of the wind.
A second boulder, lichen-coated. Between the two, a hollow where a woman might shelter.

host.say: The Professor drew a new ring, crumb by crumb, around the hollow. 'The wolves will come, Madam Mina. Here they cannot touch you.'

interact.use_fail: The ring must be drawn with the Wafer.
interact.look: Level ground between the stones. The Professor will draw a ring of Host around it before we rest.

a6_field_glasses.say: Through the glasses: a dust-cloud, and in it a leiter-wagon, whipped horses, a ring of horsemen. And, wide on both flanks, four riders closing fast. 'They are racing for the sunset!'

interact.use_fail: I need a glass to see anything on that plain.
interact.look: A flat-topped rock with a long view over the plain and the road below. A man with a glass could see every wagon in the valley.
The ashes of our morning fire. A few coals still glow.

interact.take_text: I took a flask of brandy for the cold.
interact.look: A chest of bread and cold meat. We have eaten and drunk a little.
Mina sits wrapped in furs in the hollow, her face white, her eyes clear. Her scar is still red.
A black wolf on the skyline. It will come no closer than the ring.
A long ladder-wagon, drawn by four lathered horses. On its bed, bound with chains, rides the long box.
A long, iron-bound box. The Szgany ring it with knives. We cannot reach it yet.
The lid is loose. Under it, in the red light, a man's white face with open red eyes. The sun is a hand's breadth from the mountain.
A leaning wayside cross. The sun's last rays strike its arm and throw a long red shadow across the snow.

interact.take_text: I took another handful of cartridges.
interact.look: A satchel of Winchester cartridges. Arthur keeps handing them round.
Arthur, hair wild, rifle in hand, eyes fixed on the wagon. He has not slept for six days.
Seward steadies his horse with a hand on its neck and looks for the best angle for a shot.
Quincey grips the bowie knife in one hand and his Winchester in the other, grinning like a boy.
A hawk-faced Szgany in a red coat, knife in his fist, who has been paid in gold and fear to bring a box to a castle.
A Szgany rider with a long knife. His lips are white.
Another rider, with a rifle on his back and a bandage round his arm.
A Slovak carrier in sheepskin, standing at the wagon's tail.

interact.set_text: I looked at the dust until it was gone. It blew away over the snow, and nothing remained.
interact.look: A heap of dry grey dust where the Count fell, already lifting in the wind. His face, as it went, had a look of peace such as I never could have imagined there.
Quincey's bowie knife, lying where it fell in the snow. The blade is clean.

interact.go_fail: I cannot leave him. Not yet.
interact.look: The road home. A wind has begun to blow from the mountains, as if the whole range had drawn a breath.
Quincey sits against Jonathan's shoulder, one hand pressed to his side. The blood runs through his fingers. He smiles at me.
Jonathan kneels in the snow behind Quincey, supporting his head and weeping.
Arthur stands bareheaded, the Winchester lowered, the tears frozen on his face.
Van Helsing, on his knees, praying aloud. For once he has no word of learning.
Seward's hands move over Quincey's wound by habit. He knows how little it can do.

interact.end_text:
