n0.text: Jack. I came on the first train after your wire. Arthur said to come quick and not to ask questions, and I never do. Looks to me as if you fellows have been through a stampede.

choices.text: Quincey, Lucy needs blood, and the Professor says yours is the best we have.
Tell me about the bat on the Pampas.

n_blood.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_blood.text: A brave man's blood is the best thing on this earth when a woman's in trouble. I'm your man, Jack. And here, take my flask. Texan brandy. It will put a fire in anyone's veins.

n_bat.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_bat.text: Out on the Pampas, my mare, the best in the world, was found dead one morning with two little punctures in her throat and not a drop in her. One of those big bats that they call vampires had been at her. I've been thinking of her all night.

n0.speaker: Telegraph boy
n0.text: You want to send a wire, sir? I take 'em to the office at Hampstead. Office shuts at eight, sir, and the last Amsterdam collect goes out at half past seven. What's the message?

choices.text: 'Come tomorrow morning if convenient. Lucy unwell.'
'Come by the day train through Calais and Dover; two changes.'
'Come by the night boat from the Hook; boat-train reaches Liverpool Street 6.05; urgent, a matter of life.'
I am not ready to send it yet.

n_late.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_late.text: 'Tomorrow morning if convenient' is no message to send to a man who runs a hospital. Lucy may not have the day to spare. I tear it up.

n_slow.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_slow.text: Two changes and a long day. He would arrive tomorrow evening, if the Channel is kind. No. The night boat, surely.

n_ok.speaker: Telegraph boy
n_ok.text: 'Night boat, 6.05, urgent, a matter of life.' That'll fetch him, sir. Never saw a wire to Amsterdam with so few words. I'll run.

n0.speaker: Lucy
n0.text: Dr. Seward. How kind of you to come all this way. I hope you don't think I'm ill. I'm so sleepy, that's all. And Arthur's poor father... I wish he were here.

choices.text: May I look at your throat, Lucy?
Do you walk in your sleep?
Do you remember the flowers last night?
Lucy, Arthur is here. He has come to see you.

n_feel.speaker: Lucy
n_feel.text: Weak, and rather faint, and hungry for a thing I don't know the name of. I dream so vividly, Doctor. There is a flapping at the window, and a long thin shadow, and sometimes a pair of red eyes that I can't bring myself to dislike.

n_exam.speaker: Lucy
n_exam.text: If you must. (She lifts the lace at her collar, and I see them.) Two little punctures, white-edged, not deep, not angry. They will not heal. She says she must have pricked herself on a safety-pin.

n_walk.speaker: Lucy
n_walk.text: Mamma says I did at Whitby. I woke on the East Cliff once, with Mina beside me, and I was freezing. But I haven't, here. I'm sure I haven't.

n_flowers.speaker: Lucy
n_flowers.text: Flowers? I never liked garlic before, but last night it was delightful. I slept as I have not slept in weeks. In the morning... it was all gone from my neck? I don't remember. I don't remember taking it off.

d1.speaker: Lucy
d1.text: (Her eyes open, blue and clear, and a little flush has come into her cheeks.) Arthur. Dear Arthur. Is it really you? I dreamed you'd come, and now I can't tell the dream from the room.

d2.speaker: Arthur
d2.text: (He kneels by the bed and takes her hand. He cannot speak for a moment.) Lucy. My Lucy. I am here, and I shall not leave you.

d3.speaker: Lucy
d3.text: (Very softly, to him alone.) Kiss me, Arthur.

d_wrong.speaker: Van Helsing
d_wrong.text: (He is across the room before I can speak, and his hand is on Arthur's shoulder.) No! Not on your life! Not for your life, nor hers!  Arthur... the forehead, only the forehead, I implore you.

d_forehead.speaker: Arthur
d_forehead.text: (He kisses her on the forehead, and she smiles, and closes her eyes, and the smile does not change.) Lucy? Lucy?

d_end.speaker: Dr. Seward
d_end.text: She does not answer. The colour that fed her cheek stays there, and her lips are red and soft in the candle, and she looks more beautiful than I have ever seen her. I put my fingers to her wrist. Nothing. Van Helsing takes Arthur out gently; Quincey follows. I stay with her.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Friend John. You have the face of a man who has not slept, which is correct. You may speak.

choices.text: Professor, what do you make of her?
Show me again how to ward the room.
Professor, look at the petals and the slippers.
Mrs Westenra threw out the garlic and opened the window.
Professor, the wolf. What is it? Where did it come from?

q1.speaker: Van Helsing
q1.text: I have looked, friend John, but you have looked first. Tell me what you saw. Three questions, as a surgeon answers before a student. Where are the marks?

choices.text: On her wrist, like a bad vaccination.
On her throat, two small punctures, white-edged and torn.
On her ankle, where a bat might alight.

qw1.speaker: Van Helsing
qw1.text: No, friend John. Think. Look again with the candle. You are a physician and you have an eye. Use it.

q2.speaker: Van Helsing
q2.text: Good. And what does she do, in the evenings? What happens to her, in the night, that does not happen to other sick girls?

choices.text: She sleeps badly from nerves, nothing more.
She sleeps with the window open, walks in her sleep, and wakes weaker each morning.
She has consumption; the pallor shows it.

qw2.speaker: Van Helsing
qw2.text: No. A phthisis does not shift with the window. Think about her nights.

q3.speaker: Van Helsing
q3.text: Good. And now the hardest question. She has lost, I judge, a great deal of blood. We cannot do the most simple thing, give it back, with a single man. Whose blood first?

choices.text: Her mother's: she is of the same blood.
Arthur's: her betrothed, who loves her.

qw3.speaker: Van Helsing
qw3.text: No. Her mother's heart would stop. A stranger's... it is not wrong, but he is not the man whose blood is a gift. Think again, friend John. The man she loves.

q_done.speaker: Van Helsing
q_done.text: Exactly. Arthur's. And then yours, and then mine, and, when God sends him, a fourth. Fetch Arthur. And you shall prepare: the black bag with the tubing, the brandy, the chloral for her sleep; I will bring the flowers.

n_plan.speaker: Van Helsing
n_plan.text: Four things tonight. First, the black bag, your silver tubing and lancets. Second, brandy, for the donor, afterwards, and for you when you faint. Third, a sleeping draught, chloral; she must not be awake or the sight will frighten her. Fourth, her room: garlic at the window, at the door, in the chimney, and a wreath for her neck. And then, we pray.

n_ward.speaker: Van Helsing
n_ward.text: Window, door, chimney, neck. A chimney is a door to what is thin enough. And the neck: a wreath tied with white ribbon, so it does not fall. Rub the flowers, press them into the cracks. Leave nothing out, friend John. A ward with one hole is no ward at all.

sw1.speaker: Van Helsing
sw1.text: You have seen the petals. You have seen the slippers. They are a story. Tell me what happened in this room, in the night.

choices.text: Mrs Westenra came in meaning well, and took the garlic away.
The maid came in and cleared the room.
Lucy herself rose in her sleep, took off the wreath, swept the window, and lay down again.

sw_w1.speaker: Van Helsing
sw_w1.text: No. Her mother did not come near. The trail begins at the bed and ends at the window, and no hand but hers made it. Think again.

sw_w2.speaker: Van Helsing
sw_w2.text: The maid is here for the daylight, not the night. Her footprints do not wander. No.

sw_ok.speaker: Van Helsing
sw_ok.text: Yes. Asleep, walking, drawn by something that is not her, she undid what we did, and does not remember. The thing that hunts her has found a will that is weaker than the flowers. So: we lock her door and keep the key. We pin her window shut with iron. And we wake her, friend John, if we must. Find the key on the hall rack. The pin is in the garden somewhere; a cottage garden always has an iron pin.

n_mw.speaker: Van Helsing
n_mw.text: (He sits down on the edge of the bed with his hands between his knees. His shoulders shake, and he laughs, and it is not laughter.) Oh, God. God forgive me; I am a fool. That good, kind woman has killed her daughter, and she believes she was kind. Friend John, there is only one thing left. You are strong, and so is Arthur; I am older, but I am here. The third transfusion shall be mine. Speak to Mrs Westenra. Persuade her.

n_wolf.speaker: Van Helsing
n_wolf.text: A wolf from the Gardens, friend John. Escaped, by every account in the paper. That is the plain explanation, and I have not the heart to give you the other. Go. See to the servants. Something has gone through this house tonight that wanted all its doors open.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: Lucy lies white on the pillow, her breath no louder than a moth's. The black bag, the tubing, the lancets are ready, if I am; and a donor, and brandy for afterwards, and chloral to keep her from seeing what is done.

choices.text: Use Mrs Westenra's blood. She is her mother.
Ask Arthur to give again so soon.

n_mother.speaker: Van Helsing
n_mother.text: No! Her heart is a thing that will stop at a loud word. The blood would do no good, and the shock would be worse than the loss. Another donor, friend John.

n_again.speaker: Van Helsing
n_again.text: A man may give a little, once. Not twice in a day. We shall have to find other donors, and lose no time about it.

t1.speaker: Van Helsing
t1.text: Chloral in water, a cup, drink. Good, she sleeps. Now, Arthur, your arm. (He lays the cut vein to the silver tube; the blood goes in, and the colour comes to her cheek like dawn.) Good. Brandy for Arthur. Not a word to him of what we shall do hereafter, friend John. A lover is jealous of everything, even the gift.

t2.speaker: Van Helsing
t2.text: You, friend John. Roll the sleeve. (I lie back and he opens the vein. It does not hurt; it is merely cold. The room goes grey, then white; the brandy brings it back.) She has colour. Say nothing to Arthur. It is our secret, and a good one.

t3.speaker: Van Helsing
t3.text: Mine, then. (He is shaking, though not with fear.) I am not young. Do not stare, friend John; it is my arm, not yours, that I am wasting. (The tube is warm. His face is grey and his jaw is set. He says, quietly, 'We fight him all the same.')

t4.speaker: Quincey Morris
t4.text: (He peels off his coat, rolls his sleeve, and lies down on the sofa-bed with his boots on.) Do it quick, Doc. I never had a tooth drawn easier. (The tube hums. His colour holds. Van Helsing, white at the mouth, injects morphia under Lucy's skin to keep her still.) A brave man's blood is the best thing on earth.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: The chair by the bed. The candle. The ticking. A man can sit here and keep time against the dark. But only if everything else has been done first.

choices.text: Keep watch through the first night.

do.card: 8 September.  Morning.  The wreath is on the floor.

choices.text: Keep watch through the second night.

do.card: 12 September.  Morning.  The window is open, and Mrs Westenra is smiling.

choices.text: Keep watch for the days that follow.
Keep watch through the seventeenth night.

do.card: 17 September.  Midnight.  Something is at the glass.

v1.speaker: Dr. Seward
v1.text: I sit, and doze, and nod, and the candle sinks. Towards dawn something wakes me; I cannot say what. The wreath is on the floor, the garlic has been swept off the sill, and the window is ajar. Lucy has not moved. She is white as paper.

v2.speaker: Dr. Seward
v2.text: I slept at the Professor's order, in the next room, and for the first time in days I slept. When I woke, Mrs Westenra was in Lucy's room opening the shutters and singing, with a handful of garlic flowers in her apron. She had meant it kindly. The room was cold.

v3.speaker: Dr. Seward
v3.text: Four days. Every morning a box from Haarlem, and every evening the same quiet. Lucy eats a little and laughs a little, and Mrs Westenra, true to her promise, will not so much as touch the door. At night something taps, and flaps, and Van Helsing says it is a bat, and does not say it with a smile. On the fifth night the wind rises.

v4.speaker: Dr. Seward
v4.text: Outside, a long howl, and a thin one answering it, and the whole house cowers.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: She lies so quietly. The candles are lit at head and foot, and Van Helsing is standing at the window with his back to me, very straight.

choices.text: Search for the paper Van Helsing noticed at her breast.
Ask Van Helsing what we must do now.

n_teeth.speaker: Van Helsing
n_teeth.text: (He draws her lip back with a finger. The canine teeth are longer and sharper than any I have seen in a living mouth.) You have eyes, friend John. You see them? Remember this, and tell no one. I shall explain later, and you will not believe me, and that is as it should be.

n_memo.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_memo.text: It is folded small, in the fold of her nightgown over her heart. 'Hillingham, 12 September. Arthur, if you read this, forgive me; I am not myself. There is something in the night that is not a dream. I am so frightened of what I am becoming...' The handwriting fails near the end.

n_do.speaker: Van Helsing
n_do.text: The funeral, friend John. The undertaker comes in the morning. You will say nothing to Arthur of the teeth, nothing of the paper. We shall bury her as a Christian woman, in her own vault, and we shall watch, afterwards. The hearse is at the garden gate. Come.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Friend John. The others have gone to the carriages. Stay a moment. Look at the vault, and tell me what you see.

n_task.speaker: Mina Harker
n_task.text: Thank you. Here are my own papers: my Whitby diary and the cuttings from the Dailygraph. The rest I shall ask for as I need them. Bring them to the room off the library, and I will type each one. Then we shall see what they say together.

n_where.speaker: Mina Harker
n_where.text: Four things I need: Jonathan's journal, which he keeps; your phonograph cylinders, Doctor, which I think you keep locked; the Professor's memorandum; and my Whitby papers, which you have. And if Mr. Renfield keeps notes, I should like to see them too. The typewriter is in the little room west of the library.

n_why.speaker: Mina Harker
n_why.text: A story told in six voices is a story nobody has heard. Typed in order, it may speak.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Friend John! The mountain has come to Mahomet. The Harkers are here, and the work begins. Madam Mina has the eye of a lawyer and the heart of a nurse.

choices.text: Professor, Mrs. Harker asks for your memorandum.
What do you think of the case?
Is the Host safe in your bag?

n_memo.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_memo.text: Ah, yes! My memorandum. It tells of Miss Lucy, and of what I think, and of what I do not yet dare to think. Give it to her, and tell her to be gentle with my English.

n_think.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_think.text: There is a man, or a thing, in London. He has fifty boxes of earth, and we cannot kill him until we know where all of them lie. When Madam Mina has finished her typewriting, we shall be wiser. And then we hold the council.

n_host.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_host.text: Seven wafers, from my own priest in Amsterdam. Not a toy, not a charm. A thing to be used with care, and in faith. Do not waste a crumb.

n0.speaker: Mina Harker
n0.text: The whole story, in threads and pins. Each paper I have typed is pinned in its place, and I try to make them agree. What shall I ask the papers?

choices.text: Where does the Count lie in London?
How did he come from Transylvania?
What can be done against him?
[Say the Count sleeps in Whitby churchyard]

n_carfax.speaker: Mina Harker
n_carfax.text: Jonathan wrote that fifty boxes were brought from the castle chapel. The Doctor's cylinders say that Renfield screams loudest from the window that looks over the wall. And Mr. Hawkins sold the Count a house on the other side of that wall. He rests at Carfax, among his boxes, in the old chapel.

n_whitby.speaker: Mina Harker
n_whitby.text: The Demeter put into Whitby in the storm with a dead crew and a great dog that leapt ashore. Jonathan's boxes were aboard her, fifty of them. The dog was the Count. Then the boxes went to London by rail, consigned to Billington of Whitby and forwarded by the carriers.

n_renf.speaker: Mina Harker
n_renf.text: Doctor Seward noted that Renfield grows violent when the night is clear, and eats the flies and sparrows with an increasing greed, 'to take their life into his own'. Each turn corresponds to the Count's visits. He is the Count's pawn, and may be the Count's door.

n_rules.speaker: Mina Harker
n_rules.text: He needs his native earth to rest. He cannot enter a house unasked. He fears the crucifix, garlic, the Host. If every box of earth is made unfit for him, he will have nowhere to lie by day. That is what we must do: find every box, and sanctify every one.

n_wrong1.speaker: Mina Harker
n_wrong1.text: Whitby is where Lucy first met him, but he does not rest there. There is no box in that churchyard. Look again at Jonathan's pages.

n_wrong2.speaker: Mina Harker
n_wrong2.text: A madman, Doctor Seward calls him. But no madman keeps a record that matches the Count's movements. Look again at the cylinders.

n_done.speaker: Mina Harker
n_done.text: Yes. It is all one story, and now I can say it plainly: the Count lies at Carfax, in the fifty boxes, and the fifty boxes must be found and sanctified. I will take it to the Professor.

n0.speaker: Mina Harker
n0.text: I have given the Professor the typescript. He wishes us all to meet at the long table. I think it is a council, Doctor, and I think I am afraid that I shall be asked to leave it.

choices.text: You have earned a seat, Mrs. Harker.
Is there anything that troubles you?

n_seat.speaker: Mina Harker
n_seat.text: Thank you. I do not mean to be a burden. But if I am in the dark, I fear I shall be a greater one.

n_trouble.speaker: Mina Harker
n_trouble.text: A dream, only. A great white mist about the window. I woke, and the garlic wreath on the sill had curled, as though it, too, felt something. Pray set it at my window, Doctor, if you can find a reason.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Friends! Madam Mina has done what no man of us could do. She has made the story one. Now I must tell you what I know, which is what none of you wish to hear. Sit, and listen, and do not laugh.

n_menu.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_menu.text: Ask, and I will answer. You may ask in any order. When you know enough, we shall settle the matter of Madam Mina.

choices.text: What is it that we hunt?
Why does he need the boxes of earth?
[Propose that Mrs. Harker be one of us]

n_powers.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_powers.text: The Nosferatu does not die like other things. He has the strength of twenty men; he can command the wolf, the rat, the owl, the bat, the moth; he can come on moonlight as mist, as dust. He casts no shadow and no reflection. And he feeds on blood, and those who feed him become his.

n_weak.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_weak.text: In the daylight he is powerless. He cannot cross running water save at ebb or flow of the tide. The crucifix, the garlic, the wild rose, the Sacred Host: all these he must obey. And the stake through the heart and the sword to the head will give his body peace.

n_earth.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_earth.text: He is bound to his native earth. He must rest in it by day, or he withers. That is why he brought fifty boxes from Transylvania. If we can make each unfit for him, in sanctified ground he cannot lie. We find the boxes. We hallow the earth. It is a work of days, but it is a work we can do.

n_invite.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_invite.text: He may not enter unless he is invited. That is why he needs a door. That is why a man like Renfield is dangerous. A lunatic does not know what an invitation is, and the Count will give him a reason to say yes.

n_mina.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_mina.text: Madam Mina has read every paper we have. She has the best brain in the house. She is also the woman whose friend he took, and the woman whose husband he tormented. I think she has a right. But she is delicate. What do you say?

choices.text: Agreed. We keep no secrets from her.
Think of the danger to her.

n_danger.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_danger.text: I have thought of it. But a woman kept in the dark by love is a woman in greater danger than a woman who knows. Think again.

n_end.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_end.text: Then we are six, and God help us. Tomorrow, to Carfax, the chapel, the boxes. Mr. Harker has the keys. Take the Host, take the crucifix, take the lamps. Let Lord Godalming's dogs go before us. And let us all swear, here, on this table, to put an end to this thing.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Friend John. We stand on the edge of a long road. Ask me what you will.

choices.text: What do we do now, Professor?
How should the Host be used?
A ward for Mrs. Harker's room?
I am out of the Host, Professor.

n_next.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_next.text: First Carfax, the chapel. There lie twenty-nine boxes, or so I judge. Each must be sanctified with a crumb of the Host. Go with the keys from Harker. Beware the rats: the Count is a master of them. Then, when we have counted what we found, we shall know how many are elsewhere. Then the carriers, the ledgers, the agents.

n_host.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_host.text: A crumb upon the earth in each box, with the true intent of the heart. There are five stacks in the chapel; I count one wafer for each. Do not waste it on one box when a stack will do. And remember, we have use for it elsewhere.

n_ward.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_ward.text: Yes. The garlic wreath at the window, the crucifix on the sill. They are not proof against him, but they will tell us if he has come. Do it quietly. Madam Mina must not think we mistrust her sleep.

n_refill.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_refill.text: Then take another. There is one more in the pyx. Be careful with it: they are not easily come by.

n0.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n0.text: Seward. I have my terriers in the yard, a good rope, and a very bad conscience. I wish to end this thing, for Lucy's sake.

choices.text: Lord Godalming, might I have a length of rope?
How are you bearing up, Art?

n_rope.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n_rope.text: Take it. Good Sussex hemp. It has hauled many a fox from its earth.

n_bear.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n_bear.text: I think of her every day, and then I think of what she became, and I do not know which thought is worse. Mina is a fine woman. I shall protect her.

n_dogs.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n_dogs.text: Three terriers, hard as nails. If the Count's rats come, they will meet something that bites back.

n0.speaker: Quincey Morris
n0.text: Doc. I have a Winchester in my room and a bowie knife under my coat. Say the word, and I'll shoot at anything that moves after dark.

choices.text: Quincey, I am told you carry the purse.
What do you make of the Professor?
What do you make of this whole business?

n_purse.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_purse.text: Sure thing. Three sovereigns. Pay for a clerk's silence, a carter's thirst, and keep a spare. In this town gold talks louder than a judge.

n_vh.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_vh.text: He's the first man I met who looks at a ghost the way my father looked at a bear. Calm. Practical. I'd follow him anywhere.

n_biz.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_biz.text: I've seen more of the world than most. Never believed in witches. Now I believe in everything.

n0.speaker: Renfield
n0.text: Doctor! Dr. Seward! I must speak with you. Not of the flies, nor the spiders, but of myself. Of what is coming.

choices.text: Tell me again about the Master.

n_plea.speaker: Renfield
n_plea.text: Let me go, Doctor! Let me go home. I am not safe here. He is near, nearer than ever, and he will want something. I cannot refuse him and live. I cannot obey him and be saved.

choices.text: Tell me what you fear. I will listen.
I cannot release you. Quiet, or I will call the attendants.

n_refuse.speaker: Renfield
n_refuse.text: Then I am lost! Then I am his! No! NO!

n_calm.speaker: Renfield
n_calm.text: Thank you, Doctor. I am sorry. He promised me lives, thousands of them, if I would be his. He has come before, in the mist. He will come again. If he asks me in, I... I do not know what I shall do. Keep him from my window. Keep him from hers.

n_master.speaker: Renfield
n_master.text: He is no master of mine. He is a tyrant, a tempter. He showed me a swarm of rats. He said they would be mine, and I should have an endless supply of lives. All I had to do was say 'Come in.' I said nothing. Doctor, I said nothing.

choices.text: Swear that you will not invite him.
If he comes, will you call out?

n_swear.speaker: Renfield
n_swear.text: I swear it, Doctor. On the flies. On my own life, which is not much of a stake. But I am afraid I am a weak vessel.

n_signal.speaker: Renfield
n_signal.text: I will scream till the roof comes down. But I fear the roof is not the thing he needs. He needs a door, and I am one.

n_garlic.speaker: Renfield
n_garlic.text: Keep it off me, Doctor! Not for me. For her window. Garlic the lady's window and there is not a cloud that can cross it. But he may find another way.

n0.speaker: Renfield
n0.text: Doctor... Doctor, my back... I cannot... lips...

n_revive.speaker: Renfield
n_revive.text: That is better. Thank you, Doctor. I must tell you quickly. While I can.

n_who.speaker: Renfield
n_who.text: He came through the mist. I had not asked him in, but he came. And I knew what he meant to do, and I begged him to spare her. He laughed. Then he took me up and broke me against the floor like a child's toy. Doctor, he is going to the lady. Now. This minute.

n_end.speaker: Renfield
n_end.text: The room... of the Harkers. Go! GO! Tell her... tell her I was not wholly his...

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: He is dead. Poor Renfield. He tried to be a man at the end. I will see to it that he is buried with the dignity he never had in life.

n0.speaker: Simmons
n0.text: Evenin', Doctor. He's been quiet today. Quiet's worse. He writes in that book of his, columns of numbers, day and night.

n_num.speaker: Simmons
n_num.text: Flies, sir. Spiders. Sparrows. He ticks each one off. Says they're the 'lives', and he's collecting a hundred for the one big life.

n_vis.speaker: Simmons
n_vis.text: Not as I've seen, sir. But the window... I have heard a sound on it more than once. Like a bat at the glass.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: The tall clock stands at ten. The house is quiet, and quiet in this house is rarely rest.

choices.text: [Retire for the night. Let the Count come if he will.]
What have I yet to do?

n_todo.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_todo.text: Mina's records, the council, Carfax, the carriers, the trace to Piccadilly, and a word with Renfield. When all are done, we can rest for a night, and perhaps be wiser.

n_night.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_night.text: I locked the library, doused the lamps, and went to the wards. I do not know why. Something in the house had changed.

do.card:
Night of 3 October. Purfleet.

A scream in the dark. A pool of blood. The Count has come.

n0.speaker: Old gardener
n0.text: Evenin', sir. That wall's older than the house. Folks say Carfax was a monastery, once, and the chapel's older still. Nobody goes in. Nobody comes out.

choices.text: Has anyone been over the wall lately?
The chapel door. Is there a key?
I need oil, wood and cloth for torches.

n_wall.speaker: Old gardener
n_wall.text: I've seen lights, sir, at night. And I've seen a great dog sitting on the wall, with eyes like coals. I don't go that end any more.

n_key.speaker: Old gardener
n_key.text: The old caretaker, God rest him, was afeard of thieves. Hid the chapel key somewhere in the grounds where a dog could not dig and a child could not climb. Under a stone, or in a well, or maybe in a gatepost. Look about, sir.

n_supply.speaker: Old gardener
n_supply.text: Oil's in the barrel by the shed. Ash-wood stacked by the stove. And Mrs. Billing's washing, I daresay, has a spare strip or two.

n0.speaker: Cabman
n0.text: Cab, sir? Town in the hour. Anywhere you like, sir, and no questions, save the fare.

choices.text: Have you carried a foreign gentleman lately?

n_foreign.speaker: Cabman
n_foreign.text: Aye, a tall thin gent, ancient, with a white moustache and a fine black coat. Carried a box under his arm like a child's coffin. Paid me in gold, he did, and never so much as blinked. Bit of a cold fish. The horse near bolted.

n0.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n0.text: I sold him this place. Or helped to. I drew up the deed and sealed the packet that put the Count in the very house he dreamed of. Now I come as his enemy.

n_key.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_key.text: The deeds mention that the old caretaker hid it in the park, near a stone feature of some kind: a post, a cross, a well. I have looked at the house; I should not like to go further without the chapel key in hand.

n_go.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_go.text: Not before we have the key. And the Professor says rats may be abroad. Hold your lamps high, Doctor.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Here it is, friend John. Here is where he sleeps. The Count's house of dead earth. If we do this right, he will have no bed in England tonight.

choices.text: How shall we cleanse the boxes?
I am out of the Host, Professor.

n_rats.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_rats.text: The Count commands them. They will come when we move toward the earth. Hold your lamps, hold your ground, and keep the dogs close. They are only rats, friend John. Rats are afraid of men with lamps and resolve.

n_how.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_how.text: Five stacks, by my count. Six boxes in four of them, five in the last: twenty-nine in all. A crumb of the Host upon each stack, with the intent of the heart. It is enough. It will not be pleasant, and it will not be quick, but it is the work we came for.

n_refill.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_refill.text: There is one more in the pyx. Take it, and God forgive me if I have miscounted.

n0.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n0.text: The count is easy, if we are patient. I have kept the tally from the castle in my head: fifty boxes, I counted them sleeping and wakeful, and I will never be wrong.

choices.text: How many do we see here?

n_info.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_info.text: Five stacks. By the chalk on the wall, twenty-nine boxes. But there were fifty in the castle chapel, and fifty on the Demeter. So twenty-one are elsewhere.

n_count.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_count.text: Twenty-nine boxes, and all are clean. The Count can no more lie here. But where are the other twenty-one? He has scattered them across London, I am sure of it. The carriers, Doctor. There is a ledger somewhere in London that remembers every box.

n0.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n0.text: A trail is a chain: one link leads to the next. Carriers, then the man who carried, then the man who sold the house. Where shall we begin?

n_start.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_start.text: Carter, Paterson & Co. They are the carriers, and the Hawkins letter will open the office door even if it will not open the ledger. Then, whoever carried the boxes. And lastly the house-agents. A man who buys a house in cash leaves a name somewhere.

n_status.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_status.text: That depends what we have done. Smollet's ledger shows six boxes to Mile End and six to Bermondsey. Bloxam knows where the nine went, I suspect. And the house-agents must know whose house it is.

n_missing.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_missing.text: Keys, mostly. And patience. The Count paid cash for everything. A man who pays cash is a man who hates a written record, and I have never known one to leave none.

n0.speaker: Street boy
n0.text: Penny for a poor lad, sir? I know every court and alley between here and the river.

choices.text: Do you know a white-moustached old gentleman?

n_scrap.speaker: Street boy
n_scrap.text: Coo, sir. 'Sam Bloxam, Korkrans, 4, Poters Cort, Bartel Street, Walworth.' Who writes like that? It don't make sense. What's it supposed to say?

choices.text: Potter's Court, off Bartel Street, Walworth: Corcoran's, number four.
Sam Bloxam is a made-up name.

n_wrong.speaker: Street boy
n_wrong.text: Never heard of no Poter. Try again, guv.

n_wrong2.speaker: Street boy
n_wrong2.text: Sam Bloxam's real enough. Drinks at the 'Are and 'Ounds. It's the writing that's daft.

n_right.speaker: Street boy
n_right.text: That's it! Potter's Court, Corcoran's, down the alley by the barrel, sir. Sam Bloxam lodges there. Good luck, and a penny would not go amiss.

n_old.speaker: Street boy
n_old.text: A gent with a white moustache and a hat pulled low? Walked up to the big stone house with the bow window in Piccadilly, he did. Carried a box up the steps himself. One hand. Gave me a shiver.

n0.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n0.text: Business hours, sir. State your errand. I can't show our book to every gentleman who walks in off the street.

choices.text: I am inquiring after fifty boxes of earth, consigned to Carfax.

n_inq.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n_inq.text: Boxes of earth, is it? Aye, we carried the like. But it's a confidential book, sir. I'd need good reason.

n_letter.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n_letter.text: A letter's a handsome thing, sir. But a letter's not a ledger. My memory has been poor of late. A bit of grease might clear it.

n_police.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n_police.text: Constable? On what charge? Hauling boxes? Be off with you, sir, or I'll fetch him myself.

n_pay.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n_pay.text: Ah, well. Sovereign talks, sir. Here: I'll copy the entry for you. Six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town. Six more to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey. And the nine that went to a gentleman in Piccadilly, that's Sam Bloxam's work. Here's his direction. My own spelling is a little on the poor side, mind.

n_after.speaker: Mr. Smollet
n_after.text: I have told you all I know, sir. And I'd thank you not to mention my name outside.

n0.speaker: Thomas Snelling
n0.text: Zzz... Eh? Who? Boxes? Aye, boxes. Dirty. Heavy. Smelt like a churchyard. The old gent that bought 'em lifted one hisself. One-handed. I'm tellin' ye, sir, I'm a sober man.

n_where.speaker: Thomas Snelling
n_where.text: Chicksand Street, Mile End... and a place in Bermondsey... and that big stone house in Piccadilly. Ask Sam Bloxam. He had the cart. Zzz...

n0.speaker: Sam Bloxam
n0.text: Who wants Sam Bloxam? If it's about that Hackney debt...

choices.text: Tell me about the nine boxes.

n_cold.speaker: Sam Bloxam
n_cold.text: Nine boxes? Don't know what you mean, guv. Memory's gone a bit foggy. Might come back with a bit of coin.

n_tell.speaker: Sam Bloxam
n_tell.text: Well, now. Nine boxes of earth, heavy as sin. An old gent with a white moustache, strong as a horse, took us to a stone house with a bow window and high steps. Near a big white church, beyond the Junior Constitutional Club. A torn 'To Let' board. I forget the number, guv, but a groom in the mews will know it. Number 347, I'd say, but don't swear to it.

n_again.speaker: Sam Bloxam
n_again.text: I've told you all. Go careful. That old gent was no ordinary old gent.

n0.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n0.text: Good day, sir. How may we serve you?

n_picc.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n_picc.text: I am afraid our clients' affairs are strictly confidential, sir.

n_bribe.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n_bribe.text: Sir! This is a respectable house. Please put that away.

n_bluster.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n_bluster.text: I must ask you to leave, sir, or I shall call Mr. Candy.

n_letter.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n_letter.text: Lord Godalming? Of Ring? Oh, I beg your pardon, sir. The buyer was a Count de Ville, who paid in cash and wished the house kept quiet. A foreigner, very old, very strong. I would not have liked to cross him. Here are the keys, sir. And I would say, sir: if you do mean to enter, take company.

n_after.speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
n_after.text: You have the keys, sir. I hope you find what you seek.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: Jonathan lies on his back, face flushed, breathing heavily like one in a drugged sleep. I shake him. Nothing.

n0.speaker: Dr. Seward
n0.text: In the moonlight through the yellow blind: a tall, thin man in black, his face waxen, his eyes red. His left hand grips both of Mina's wrists. His right holds her head against his open breast, where a bleeding wound drips. Her mouth is at it. On the bed, Jonathan lies in a stupor.

n_wreath.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_wreath.text: The wreath lies trampled on the floor. It did not keep him out. Only an invitation could, and he had that already.

n_rush.speaker: Count Dracula
n_rush.text: Fools. Do you think you can strike me? I who have commanded armies when your fathers were babes?

n_cruc.speaker: Count Dracula
n_cruc.text: You think yourselves so wise, all of you. Your girls are mine, and through them you, and others, shall be mine. The sheep are in my hands. Yet before I go, I shall have her again; and again.

n_host.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_host.text: The Count drops the girl and turns on us. He is a hawk, a stoat, a wolf. Van Helsing steps forward with an envelope. 'Back!'

n_cower.speaker: Dr. Seward
n_cower.text: He cowers. Further and further we advance with crucifixes lifted. A bar of moonlight crosses his face and he grows grey, then thin, then a pale mist under the door. We hear the whining of the wind. He is gone.

n_mina.speaker: Mina Harker
n_mina.text: Unclean! Unclean! Even the Almighty shuns my polluted flesh! I must bear this shame upon my forehead until the Judgment Day!

n_brand.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_brand.text: Madam Mina. This is the Sacred Host. Forgive me.

do.say: The Wafer touched her forehead and burned like a hot iron. A red scar, where it touched. The Count has marked her; the Host has marked her too, and she bears both.

n0.speaker: Mina Harker
n0.text: Doctor Seward. I am awake, and I am whole, and I am afraid to look in a glass.

choices.text: How do you feel, Mrs. Harker?
Is there anything I can do?

n_bond.speaker: Mina Harker
n_bond.text: I feel him. Like a cold wind with a taste. When the sun rises or sets I seem able to follow him a little way, wherever he is. The Professor says it may be our only road to him. I pray God it is not also his to me.

n_mark.speaker: Mina Harker
n_mark.text: I would rather you did not. It is the size of a florin, red as a coal. Jonathan weeps when he looks at it. The Professor says it will fade when the Count dies, and not before.

n_help.speaker: Mina Harker
n_help.text: Finish the boxes. Every one you destroy is a day gained. And promise me that you will not keep me in the dark, whatever the Professor thinks best.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Friend John, he has tasted her, and she him. That is a link we cannot cut. But it may serve us. He is not omnipotent. He fears us, you have seen it.

choices.text: We need more of the Host.
I am out of the Host, Professor.

n_next.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_next.text: Piccadilly, with the keys that Harker got from the agents. Nine boxes, or eight, if he has taken one. Then, if the Count's keys come into our hands, the houses in Mile End and Bermondsey. We shall find him leaving, or arriving. Either way, we strike.

n_host.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_host.text: I wrote to Amsterdam as soon as I arrived. This morning my priest sent four more. Piccadilly will need two, Mile End one, Bermondsey one. Take them, friend John.

n_refill.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_refill.text: Then take another. There is one more in the pyx.

n_mina.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_mina.text: She is stronger than she knows. She asked me to keep nothing from her, and I shall obey, God help me. But she must rest, friend John. She must rest.

n0.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n0.text: Eight boxes, Professor says. The ninth the Count has taken, or perhaps he sleeps in it. We sanctify the two stacks, and we wait. If he comes, he must come through us.

n_feel.speaker: Jonathan Harker
n_feel.text: I have not slept since the night he took her. I do not mean to sleep until he is dead.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Two stacks, friend. A crumb on each. Then we wait at the door. He comes here to see to his property, and we shall be waiting.

choices.text: [Hang the garlic wreath on the front door]
I am out of the Host.

n_wreath.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_wreath.text: Good. He will think twice at the threshold. Perhaps once is enough for us.

n_refill.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_refill.text: Take another. We cannot be short of it.

n0.speaker: Count Dracula
n0.text: So. The sheep have found the wolf's lair. You are clever, you English, with your keys and your agents. But you came too late, and you leave too soon.

choices.text: [Stand in the doorway with the crucifix]

n_stand.speaker: Count Dracula
n_stand.text: Do you think a bauble stops me? I have lived when your fathers' fathers were dust. Stand aside!

n_rush.speaker: Count Dracula
n_rush.text: Ha! Hold him, men! I'll not fight in a doorway.

n0.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n0.text: The Count's key opened the Mile End lock like butter. Six boxes, in a coal-cellar. I thought I should feel triumphant. I only feel tired.

choices.text: A crumb on the stack, then?

n_how.speaker: Arthur Holmwood
n_how.text: One wafer, one stack. Do it with the right heart, the Professor says. I shall try to think of Lucy.

n0.speaker: Quincey Morris
n0.text: Last of the lot, Doc. Last house, last stack. Then there's only the one with the Count.

choices.text: [Report: the houses are clean and the Count has fled]

n_count.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_count.text: Twenty-nine at Carfax, eight at Piccadilly, six at Mile End, six here: forty-nine. One left. The Count's got it somewhere, and himself in it.

n_done.speaker: Quincey Morris
n_done.text: Forty-nine down, one to go. The sun is setting. Let's get back to Purfleet; Mrs. Harker will be waiting.

do.card:
Evening of 4 October. Purfleet.

Forty-nine boxes cleansed. One remains.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: Madam Mina, you said the link may serve us. Let us try it. At sunrise and at sunset the Count is at his weakest and his closest. Will you let me?

n_t1.speaker: Mina Harker
n_t1.text: Darkness. Everything is dark... lapping water... a creaking of wood... a rope drawn taut... above me, feet. Cold. So cold.

do.card: Sunrise, 5 October. Purfleet.

n_t2.speaker: Mina Harker
n_t2.text: A bell, dull and distant. Hawsers. Men calling, and a cry from the deck. 'We are going, we are going.' He is awake, Professor. He knows I am listening. He is so very near, and so very far.

do.card: Sunset, 5 October. Purfleet.

n_decode.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_decode.text: Think, friend. Water lapping. Wood creaking. A rope pulled taut. Feet above. A bell. 'We are going.' What is the Count's box? Where is he?

choices.text: He lies in the Bermondsey cellar still.
He is aboard a ship. We must learn her name: wire Lloyd's.
The Czarina Catherine, bound for Varna.

n_wrong1.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_wrong1.text: No. Bermondsey has no lapping water, and the box there is clean. Think of the sounds again.

n_name.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_name.text: Good. Lord Godalming has the ear of Lloyd's. A telegram will come. When it does, tell me.

n_ship.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_ship.text: Yes. The telegram says the Czarina Catherine cleared the Thames this morning for Varna. Water, wood, rope, the bell: a ship, and one eastbound. He is running home with his last box. Lord God, what a woman you are, Madam Mina.

n0.speaker: Mina Harker
n0.text: The Professor wants me to try the link. I am afraid, but I would rather be afraid and useful than safe and idle.

choices.text: You are braver than any of us, Mrs. Harker.

n_brave.speaker: Mina Harker
n_brave.text: I do not feel brave. But it helps to be told.

n_feel.speaker: Mina Harker
n_feel.text: Like standing at the edge of a dark river, with the other bank hidden. I can hear it, but I cannot see.

n0.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n0.text: The Czarina Catherine: a slow ship to Varna. We go by rail to Paris, thence the Orient Express to Varna, and wait on the quay for the ship to come in. We shall be there before her.

choices.text: I am out of the Host, Professor.

n_who.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_who.text: Lord Godalming, Mr. Morris, Dr. Seward, Mr. Harker, and myself. Five good men, and a ship's passage of rope, wood, and faith.

n_mina.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_mina.text: She is not to come. Not this time. She has done more than any of us, and the Count has her link. If she is near him, he has her. If she is far, she is free. We shall tell her this at the last, for her own peace.

choices.text: She will not agree to be left out.
It is a hard thing, but for her safety.

n_dissent.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_dissent.text: She has taken one wound for us. I will not let her take another. We say nothing of the plan, friend John. Nothing.

n_agree.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_agree.text: Good. Then it is settled. I will make out the passage. Let each man gather what he needs.

n_kit.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_kit.text: Crucifix, stake, hammer, Host. Without these we go to our graves. Do you have them all?

choices.text: Crucifix, Host, stake, hammer: all here.

n_packed.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_packed.text: Then we are ready. Go and speak with Madam Mina. She is waiting. And friend John, be kind.

n_refill.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_refill.text: Take another. We must not be short of it where we go.

n0.speaker: Mina Harker
n0.text: They have decided. I overheard the Professor with Lord Godalming. They mean to go without me. It is for my safety, they say, and I have not the heart to refuse. And I do not mean to stay behind.

choices.text: Let them go. I shall wait, and watch the link.

n_arg.speaker: Professor Van Helsing
n_arg.text: Madam Mina, I beg you. It is for your sake. The Count has the claim on your blood. We go to cut it. Stay safe here.

n_go.speaker: Mina Harker
n_go.text: They stand in the hall with their kits, the five of them: Jonathan, Arthur, Quincey, Dr. Seward, and the Professor in his shabby coat. I kiss Jonathan. I press the Professor's hand. They go. I watch the cab out of sight, and feel the line in my blood quiver, as though the Count himself were looking back.

do.card:
5 October, evening.

The party leaves Charing Cross for Paris, the Orient Express, and Varna, to wait for the Czarina Catherine. Mina remains behind.

n0.speaker: Harbour master
n0.text: Another Englishman, and another question about the Czarina Catherine. She is not in my book, sir, and no berth is kept for her.

choices.text: When was she last heard of?
What ships go astray between the Straits and Varna?

n1.speaker: Harbour master
n1.text: The Dardanelles, the fourth of October, by the telegraph. A slow brig, Roumanian flag, owners in Galatz. Eleven days is long, even for a slow brig.

n2.speaker: Harbour master
n2.text: Ships from the Straits make Varna by the cape, or, if the weather is foul and the captain a Roumanian, they run north for the Danube mouth and Galatz. Nobody tells a Roumanian where to go. If I wanted a ship that would not arrive, I should look at the Danube.

n0.speaker: Greek sailor
n0.text: You look for the Czarina? Ach, I would not wish to find her. A fog stood off Kaliakra three nights back, and it moved against the wind.

choices.text: What do you mean, against the wind?

n1.speaker: Greek sailor
n1.text: I mean a fog does not sail upstream, sir. This one did. My mate saw a ship go into it, and it closed behind her like a door. We made the sign and rowed for shore.

n2.speaker: Greek sailor
n2.text: God bless you. A man who offers brandy is a man who knows a bad sea. I tell you, sir: keep a wreath of garlic at the hatch and a candle in the cabin.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Madam Mina, the sun is near the horizon; this is the hour. Friend John has the watch, Jonathan the pencil. Are you willing?

choices.text: What do the trances tell us, Professor?

t0.speaker: Van Helsing
t0.text: Look into my hand. Sleep, Madam Mina. Where are you?

choices.text: What do you hear, Madam Mina?

t1.speaker: Mina
t1.text: I hear water. It is lapping, and rushing, and lapping again. Cool and dark.

t2.speaker: Mina
t2.text: Wood creaks. Rope strains. There are feet above me, going to and fro, and a bell. Everything is straining as if it wished to be free.

choices.text: Do you feel anything beneath you?

t3.speaker: Mina
t3.text: I am rising and falling. We are moving. The ship is moving, and I am not in her. I am somewhere dry and still, and I feel the motion of her as one feels a heart beat in another's chest.

t4.speaker: Van Helsing
t4.text: Enough, enough. Wake, Madam Mina. [Her eyes open. She remembers nothing, and I write everything down.]

d0.speaker: Van Helsing
d0.text: Consider it as the lawyer, the doctor, the metaphysician, all three. Water laps and rushes. A ship creaks and moves. Where is she, friend, and what must we do?

choices.text: She is in the harbour. We should wait on the quay.
She is out on the open sea and will reach Varna any day now.
He knows we are at Varna. He will not come where we wait; she may make for the Danube and Galatz, and we must watch the wires.

d1.speaker: Van Helsing
d1.text: No. In port a ship does not move. Madam Mina feels motion, hears rushing water. And the harbour master has no berth marked for her. Think again.

d2.speaker: Van Helsing
d2.text: Perhaps, perhaps. But Lloyd's had her at the Straits eleven days ago. A ship of that kind would be here already. Something else holds her. Read the Lloyd's report again and ask the harbour master where a ship may go besides Varna.

d3.speaker: Van Helsing
d3.text: Ah, friend John, that is thinking. He learned through her trance that we are here, and then he cut that thread. Any port but this will do him. We watch every wire, and when the news comes we move.

do.card: We waited. The days of October dragged by, a trance at every sunrise and sunset, and every day a telegram from Lloyd's: 'Czarina Catherine, not reported.' At last, on the twenty-eighth...

n0.speaker: Mina
n0.text: I am quite well. Do not look at me so. I have rested and eaten and I am sorry to be a burden.

choices.text: You asked us for a promise, Mina.
Mina, you know the railways. How do we reach Galatz?

o1.speaker: Mina
o1.text: I did, and I ask it again, with the sun high and my head clear. If I turn, Arthur, John, all of you: let me not live as that thing. Kill me. Jonathan shall read the Burial Service.

o2.speaker: Mina
o2.text: You must, dear friend, and soon. It is the one favour I ask. I will ask it every day of this journey until you say it.

o3.speaker: Mina
o3.text: Thank you. Now I am no longer afraid; or no more than I can bear. God keep you all.

r0.speaker: Mina
r0.text: You forget that I am the train fiend. I always keep the Bradshaw. At what hour does the one train for Galatz leave, do you think?

choices.text: Let me consult the Bradshaw. [Open it]

r1.speaker: Mina
r1.text: No, dear friend. Look it up before you guess. It is on the table.

r2.speaker: Mina
r2.text: Half-past six in the morning, there is only one train. It arrives in the afternoon. Tell the Professor, and tell Jonathan to sleep.

n0.speaker: Jonathan
n0.text: I have been at this knife an hour. It was good in Ghoorka hands; it is not good in mine. A dull blade is an insult to what it must do.

choices.text: What does it have to do, Jonathan?

n1.speaker: Jonathan
n1.text: Cut through the throat of a man who is not a man, and do it clean. I shall be nearest. I mean to be the one.

n2.speaker: Jonathan
n2.text: A fine stone would do wonders. There are chandlers on the quay. If you find one, put it in my hand. I cannot rest until this thing is right.

n0.speaker: Quincey
n0.text: Well, Doc. We're a long way from the Staked Plains, and the buffalo here wears horns and trousers. Anything on your mind?

n1.speaker: Quincey
n1.text: Because a Texan don't ask a lady twice. Because I loved Lucy, and have lost her, and here's a woman I'd lose my right arm for. Sit down, Doc; this country gets under the skin.

n2.speaker: Quincey
n2.text: Always. Here, take a handful. The Winchester wants feeding, and so do you.

n0.speaker: Arthur
n0.text: Lloyd's wires every morning: 'Czarina Catherine, not reported.' It makes me want to take a boat and meet her in the Bosphorus. Is there anything you need from me?

choices.text: What of the ship's owners? We cannot open the box without their consent.
Is there money for a long chase?

n1.speaker: Arthur
n1.text: The shippers' agent is at Lloyd's. Courteous, closed, a hard man to move. He'll not consent to open a case on the strength of a good face. You'll want a reason, not a truth. And, I suspect, a compensation.

n2.speaker: Arthur
n2.text: Whatever it takes. I have the purse. I'll not spare a sovereign for my own comfort, but anything that gets us to him faster, I'll buy.

n0.speaker: Porter
n0.text: Good day, sir. No post, sir. I only wait in case.

n1.speaker: Porter
n1.text: Yes, sir! Just this minute, from Lloyd's. 'Czarina Catherine reported entering Galatz at one o'clock to-day.'

n0.speaker: Lloyd's clerk
n0.text: Lord Godalming. The usual, sir? 'No news.' I am sorry. It is the same for every ship in the Black Sea. You may consult the register if you wish.

choices.text: What is the last entry for the Czarina Catherine?

n1.speaker: Lloyd's clerk
n1.text: Passing the Dardanelles, the fourth of October. Roumanian-flagged brig, hull and rigging sound. Since then, nothing; not a signal, not a sighting. If the sea had her we should have a report of wreckage by now.

n0.speaker: Shippers' agent
n0.text: Lord Godalming, is it? You have asked after a consignment aboard the Czarina Catherine. What, precisely, would you have of me?

choices.text: Open the box. It contains a dead man that is not dead.
A friend of mine has had a thing stolen, and I think it is in that ship.
Allow me to show my appreciation for the owners' trouble.
The owners will surely forgive some delay for the sake of a friend. Here is something for their trouble.

n_truth.speaker: Shippers' agent
n_truth.text: You will forgive me if I have the door held open. I have heard many reasons for opening cargo. That was the first to make me afraid for your health.

n_story.speaker: Shippers' agent
n_story.text: Stolen? That is a serious matter. If the thing is yours, a friend's, I should be glad to see it restored. But the owners will want assurance, and some consideration for delay. Return when you can promise both.

n_early.speaker: Shippers' agent
n_early.text: You mistake me, my lord. I do not take money for nothing. Give me a reason and then we shall discuss recompense.

n_permit.speaker: Shippers' agent
n_permit.text: Ah. Now we understand each other. I will give you a paper to the Captain and another to our man at Galatz. They will open the box in your presence, and any claim the owners have will be settled between gentlemen.

n0.speaker: Harbour master
n0.text: The Czarina Catherine? In last night on the tide without a pilot. Moored in the fog, and not a soul on deck till dawn. I have never seen a ship come up the Danube so still. What is your interest, gentlemen?

n1.speaker: Harbour master
n1.text: A long box, by the first light. Men from Hildesheim's lighter took it ashore. And a very tall thin man in a big coat watched from the wharf-head; I thought he was a foreigner. When I looked again he was gone.

n2.speaker: Harbour master
n2.text: Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, the agents. Their clerk is on the quay by the crates. But the Captain, Donelson, he has the papers. A Scot, and a rough one. You would do well to carry a letter from his owners.

n0.speaker: Clerk
n0.text: Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, gentlemen. What can I do for you? The Captain is aboard; I cannot say more than he allows.

choices.text: I have the Captain's bill of lading. Who is the consignee?
What can you tell me about the cargo?

n1.speaker: Clerk
n1.text: A bill, signed. Yes, I see; Hildesheim, Burgen-strasse 16. He is cautious, sir, and fond of coin. Take this note from my masters; he will see the name of Mackenzie & Steinkoff and perhaps be less difficult.

n2.speaker: Clerk
n2.text: A single long box, sir, consigned from Varna. Fifty pounds' worth of earth, they said. I thought it a joke. Hildesheim paid the carriage with an English note and signed for it in his own hand.

n0.speaker: Captain Donelson
n0.text: Ye'll be the gentlemen from Varna. I have the shippers' letter. Aye, I can see it. Well, ye may ask what ye like, but dinna expect me to tell ye a pretty story.

choices.text: Tell me about the voyage, Captain.
Show me the bill of lading.

n1.speaker: Captain Donelson
n1.text: From the day we cleared the Bosphorus the fog came on, and it stayed. Nine days, nae a breath of wind, but we made a sea-mile an hour more than any ship I've seen. The men would na touch the wheel; I stood it myself.

n2.speaker: Captain Donelson
n2.text: A long box brought aboard at Varna, by an old man in a great coat. The men crossed themselves at the sight of him. When we sailed they asked to throw it overboard, and I laid a handspike to the loudest. If the Deil did have any luggage aboord the ship, I'm thinkin' it was nane ither than that same!

n3.speaker: Captain Donelson
n3.text: Here it is. Hildesheim's the name, Burgen-strasse 16. And ye'll find a Slovak called Skinsky has the box now. Go canny, gentlemen. That old man was no man.

n0.speaker: Sailor
n0.text: [He makes the sign of the horns, and mutters in Roumanian.] Strigoi. We carried a strigoi. I would not have sailed if I had known.

choices.text: What did you see on the voyage?

n1.speaker: Sailor
n1.text: A man who was not there. A tall pale man at the rail at night. We found a mate gone one morning, with a neck like a torn flower. The Captain said he fell. I know what fell.

n0.speaker: Deckhand
n0.text: I scrub, sir, I scrub. It does not take out the smell. Not blood: earth. Earth from a grave. You smell it in the hold.

choices.text: Where did the man go when you docked?

n1.speaker: Deckhand
n1.text: He went into the box, sir. I was at the rail at dawn and I swear he went in like water in the sand. Then the lid shut. Then Hildesheim's men came.

n0.speaker: Hildesheim
n0.text: You are English gentlemen. I like English gentlemen; they are always in a hurry, and a hurry is a thing that has a price. What is it that you want?

choices.text: I come from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, with their letter.
The box taken ashore this morning. Where is it?
A Slovak called Skinsky has the box. Can you confirm it, in writing?

n1.speaker: Hildesheim
n1.text: Ah. They are good clients. That makes it easier, although not free. What information do you want?

n2.speaker: Hildesheim
n2.text: I had it of a gentleman who signed 'de Ville.' A letter, a fee, and delivery. If I tell, the gentleman is no longer a client. And for a man in my line, a client lost is a thing to be paid for.

n3.speaker: Hildesheim
n3.text: Skinsky is a Slovak, his men take cargo up the river by boat. I gave him the box. For a signature and thumbprint I would put it in writing, but the paper costs.

n4.speaker: Hildesheim
n4.text: Excellent. Here is my receipt, with the Slovak's mark. You will find him at the churchyard if he lives. I would not trouble to look in the taverns. Good day, sir. It was a pleasure doing business.

n0.speaker: Priest
n0.text: A poor Slovak, Petrof Skinsky. They found him at dawn at the churchyard wall. The people say wolves, but we have no wolves in the town. God have mercy on his soul.

choices.text: The wound is too clean for a wolf, Father.
Did he have anything on him?
May I see the coat, Father?

n1.speaker: Priest
n1.text: You have seen it, then, and you are not afraid to say it. A wolf tears. This was cut, as if by a single great tooth. I have said nothing to the police. They would think me mad. I laid the dead man's coat on the wall; no one has asked for it.

n2.speaker: Priest
n2.text: Only a coat. His widow came for it, but she has not the heart to wear it. I laid it by the wall until someone should ask.

n3.speaker: Priest
n3.text: Take it, my son. Something is sewn in the lining. A slip of paper. A boat, and Slovaks, and the river by night. I cannot read what it means. You may. God go with you.

n0.speaker: Neighbour
n0.text: He was a good man, Petrof, though he drank. He took money from a foreigner and a big box on a boat. Then in the night he came home white and he said: 'Do not open the door.' In the morning he was in the lane.

choices.text: What did the foreigner look like?

n1.speaker: Neighbour
n1.text: Tall. Thin. A long white moustache. A voice like honey. He lifted the great box alone, and Petrof, who could carry a barrel, could not help but stare.

n2.speaker: Neighbour
n2.text: Up the river, by night, with Slovaks at the oars. Petrof said they would not stop till the mountains.

n0.speaker: Mina
n0.text: Jonathan sleeps and the others rest, so I am putting all of it in order. Hildesheim, Skinsky, the Captain's tale; the facts want only a clear head. Help me think it through.

choices.text: We have not yet gathered everything. [Leave]

m0.speaker: Mina
m0.text: He cannot go by sea again; the ship is here, and watched. How would he carry his box from Galatz to the Borgo Pass? By road?

m_road.speaker: Mina
m_road.text: A cart takes days, and the horses will not abide him; I remember Jonathan's driver. And the receipt names a boat, Skinsky's slip says 'by night'. No, not the road.

m_rail.speaker: Mina
m_rail.text: Every station is a risk: clerks, officials, customs. The Count must be seen. The slip says a boat. It is not rail.

m_water.speaker: Mina
m_water.text: By water. Skinsky's slip, Hildesheim's receipt, the neighbour's account: all speak of a boat, a Slovak crew, and the river by night. It remains: which river?

choices.text: The Sereth, then a tributary to the mountains.

m_pruth.speaker: Mina
m_pruth.text: The Pruth leads away from the Pass. No, the Sereth has the Bistritza, and the Bistritza runs from the Borgo Pass itself, by Jonathan's journal. It must be that.

m_sereth.speaker: Mina
m_sereth.text: Yes. Up the Sereth, then into the Bistritza, near Fundu. It is the only river that ends at the Count's door. I shall pencil the route on a map.

m_done.speaker: Mina
m_done.text: The memorandum: Galatz, the Sereth, the Bistritza, the Borgo Pass. The map is on the table. Now Professor Van Helsing must hear it.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Friends, Madam Mina has given us the road. I think we must divide. A launch on the water, riders on the bank, and Madam Mina and myself by rail and carriage to the Pass. Let us make arrangements.

choices.text: Jonathan will not agree to his wife's going.
We are ready. Let us set out.

n1.speaker: Van Helsing
n1.text: Lord Godalming and Jonathan take the steam launch up the Sereth. Dr. Seward and Mr. Morris ride the bank. We go by the 6.30 and the carriage. At the Pass we meet. Each must have what he needs: the dealer in the hall has the launch, the horses, the flag, the lamp.

n2.speaker: Mina
n2.text: Jonathan, I am safest with the Professor. The Count's will no longer holds me, and it is I who can lead the Professor through the castle. You know it. Trust me.

n3.speaker: Van Helsing
n3.text: Then go, God keep you. Madam Mina will write. And, friends: remember that it is the sun that is our friend. He is helpless between sunrise and sunset. Let us not miss it.

do.card: 30 October, night. The party divides. Lord Godalming and Jonathan board the steam launch 'Mina' and head upstream into the dark. Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris ride the bank. Van Helsing and Mina take the morning train.

n0.speaker: Dealer
n0.text: Lord Godalming has told me you require a steam launch and good horses within three hours. It is possible. For a consideration.

choices.text: Buy the launch, a lamp and a flag.
Is there a map or chart I might have?

n1.speaker: Dealer
n1.text: A small steam launch with a boiler of English make, and an electric lamp such as the English navy uses. And here is a Roumanian flag. Fly it at Fundu and the village will think you officials. She is called, I believe, the Mina.

n2.speaker: Dealer
n2.text: The lady at the table has a map. She is the only one who has drawn the river as it is, not as the Roumanian government pretends.

n0.speaker: Jonathan
n0.text: I will not take my eyes off the water. We must overtake him before the mountains. Every boat on this river is a suspect.

n1.speaker: Jonathan
n1.text: She is with the Professor, and the Professor is a good man. And she has asked me to go. But I would give ten years to be in that carriage with her.

n2.speaker: Jonathan
n2.text: When I am working, yes. When I think of that castle, no. I escaped it once. I swore I would never see it again. Now I am running to it. Strange, is it not?

n0.speaker: Slovak boatman
n0.text: [He fell to his knees in the light of the lamp, and prayed.] Do not harm us, gentlemen. We have done nothing. We are poor men.

choices.text: Have you seen a boat with a great box and Szgany at the oars?
Stand up, man. Where is your boat bound?

n1.speaker: Slovak boatman
n1.text: Yes, gracious sir! Before dusk, a boat with eight men at the oars, a great box in the middle, and in the stern a tall dark man in a cloak. He did not look at us but I felt his eyes. They turned in at the river mouth on the left, up the Bistritza. They did not stop.

n2.speaker: Slovak boatman
n2.text: Downriver to Galatz with timber, sir. We saw lights and heard a shot and we hid. Please do not tell the Count's men we spoke.

n0.speaker: Raftsman
n0.text: [He crossed himself twice.] If you hunt what I think you hunt, you have courage. I have seen the lights of his boat at the fork, with wolves howling on the bank. They did not harm him.

n1.speaker: Raftsman
n1.text: Where the Bistritza comes into the Sereth, past Fundu. A man who knew the river would go there. And a man with wolves for guards would not need to ask.

n0.speaker: Farmer
n0.text: She struck the rock, your boat. I saw it from the field. Sit by the fire. You will need a night and a plank to mend that seam, and horses for the road.

choices.text: Can you spare two horses and a saddle?
How bad is the river ahead?

n1.speaker: Farmer
n1.text: For this gold, six. Take the grey and the bay. The road follows the river. Go with God, and do not stop when the wolves howl.

do.card: 2-3 November. The launch is mended, but the river will carry us no further. Lord Godalming buys horses; he and Jonathan will ride for the mountains. And on the bank, Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris have been in the saddle three days.

n2.speaker: Farmer
n2.text: Rapids for three versts. A rock in each, and the water black. A launch with a sound keel may pass. A launch with a broken one may not.

n0.speaker: Jonathan
n0.text: A plank sprung; no more. We need a splint, rope to bind it and canvas to stop the water. We must be on the river by nightfall.

n0.speaker: Arthur
n0.text: If we cannot mend her we shall ride. But the river is faster, and I'll not give up the Mina while she floats. A spar for the splint, a rope, some canvas; I know what to do.

n0.speaker: Innkeeper
n0.text: Gentlemen, you are not from here. News is a thing I sell. Bread and brandy first, and then we talk.

n1.speaker: Innkeeper
n1.text: Last night a launch passed, with an English lamp. And the day before, a boat with Szgany, a box, and wolves following on the bank. Both turned up the Bistritza.

n2.speaker: Innkeeper
n2.text: A sledge? There will be snow by dark. Take mine. Two horses, a bearskin and sleigh-bells I won't take back. For gold.

n0.speaker: Quincey
n0.text: Doc, I've followed a trail in sleet for three days and I never felt so tired or so awake. Mina is ahead, God willing. What's the good word?

choices.text: We must hurry. The sun sets at five.
I fear for Arthur and Jonathan on the river.

n1.speaker: Quincey
n1.text: Then we hurry, and Mina does what she has to. I told her once that I'd see the thing through, and I will. Tell the horses.

n2.speaker: Quincey
n2.text: The launch has a lamp and a flag; Arthur's no fool. Let's keep our heads and we'll all meet at the Pass.

n0.speaker: Landlady
n0.text: [She makes the sign of the horns at my forehead, then flushes and pats my hand.] Forgive an old fool, little lady. Here, a bite for the road. Garlic in the soup, and garlic at the door.

choices.text: Is the road to the Pass safe?

n1.speaker: Landlady
n1.text: Because of what lives up there, lady. In the old castle. You are young, and your husband's journal is no answer. Wear it. Carry it.

n2.speaker: Landlady
n2.text: The road to the Pass is safe by day. By night it belongs to wolves, and to him who calls them. Be across the Pass before dark, or camp in a ring.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Madam Mina, we must have a carriage, horses, and furs. The road above Veresti is rough and the nights are cold. I have gold; let me use it.

choices.text: What do you fear most on this road?

n1.speaker: Van Helsing
n1.text: Done, and well done. Four horses, a stout carriage, and a driver who will take us to the last village and not a yard further. Now furs and provisions, and your letter to Jonathan.

n2.speaker: Van Helsing
n2.text: Not the wolves, Madam Mina, nor even the Un-Dead. I fear that you will be tired, and the Count will find the thread he has lost in you. We must be careful of your sleep.

n0.speaker: Peasant woman
n0.text: [She crosses herself and thrusts garlic into my hand.] Go home, lady. Not past the cross. Dracula's wolves do not eat; they only wait.

choices.text: Which road leads to the castle?

n1.speaker: Peasant woman
n1.text: None you want. The wide road goes to the valley; the narrow road to the shepherd's hut; the old by-road goes to the Pass, and from there to the devil's house. Your man's book knows it better than I.

n2.speaker: Peasant woman
n2.text: Wear it at your throat, and when you sleep, keep your hands crossed. God keep you.

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: Madam Mina, we come to three roads. I know that you have read Jonathan's journal many times. Which of these is the one he took?

choices.text: The wide cart-road, to the left.
The narrow track, to the right.

n1.speaker: Van Helsing
n1.text: That one goes down into the valley, Madam Mina. Jonathan's coach went up. Read again.

n2.speaker: Van Helsing
n2.text: That goes to a shepherd's hut. Jonathan did not meet a shepherd. Think of the cross and the bend.

n3.speaker: Mina
n3.text: Here: 'the road went up, then down, then up again under tall pines, past a cross at the bend.' It is the old by-road, the grass-grown one beyond the shrine. I know it. Have not my Jonathan travelled it, and wrote of his travel?

n4.speaker: Van Helsing
n4.text: Then it is that road. Madam Mina, I must ask you to stay close and to take sleep when you can. Something is changing in you, and I do not want it to take you unawares. First, the wolves; they are waiting.

n0.speaker: Mina
n0.text: Professor, I feel the snow under me but I do not feel the cold. I only feel that I am drawn to that castle, as a bird to a snake. I am so tired.

choices.text: The night is coming. Let us wait.

n1.speaker: Mina
n1.text: I am in. I did not think I could be so glad of a few handfuls of dust. Keep the fire high, Professor. Keep it high.

n2.speaker: Mina
n2.text: Then we wait. Whatever comes, I shall not leave this circle; I give you my word, and I give it with all the strength I have left.

do.card: The sun went down behind the mountain. The cold deepened. The horses began to scream, and from the mist beyond the firelight came a whisper of women's laughter...

n3.speaker: Mina
n3.text: I feel him in the distance, as one feels a draught under a door. He is not far, and he is not alone. Do not leave me, Professor.

n0.speaker: The sisters
n0.text: Come, sister. Come to us. Come! Come! Why will you not come? We are so cold and the snow is so soft. He sent us, as he sends all his lovelies. Come!

choices.text: [Mina] I will not leave this circle.

n1.speaker: The sisters
n1.text: Brave sister! You are not afraid of us? We are not afraid of you. Give us your hand, only your hand, through the line. One kiss. One only.

n2.speaker: The sisters
n2.text: The Master, our dear Master. He is close. He is racing the sun. Come, and be one with us, and he will be so glad.

n3.speaker: Van Helsing
n3.text: [He raised the Host between her hand and the line.] Madam Mina! You cannot. The circle will hold, but not if you will it open. Look at me, look at the Host.

n4.speaker: Mina
n4.text: [I draw my hand back. The sisters laugh, and wolves begin to howl all around the ring. They cannot enter; but they will try until dawn.]

n0.speaker: Van Helsing
n0.text: [She is lovely beyond description. She seems to breathe, and the colour of her lips is the colour of life. A thing in me longs to kneel and kiss her, and I know what that is: not love, but a trap.]

choices.text: Think of Mina, waiting in the circle.

n1.speaker: Van Helsing
n1.text: [I hold the crucifix before my eyes. The spell shrinks. She is a thing, not a woman; a beautiful corpse that has fed on the living.]

n2.speaker: Van Helsing
n2.text: [Somewhere across the snow, Mina cries out my name, and I know the cry is real, or I have imagined it. It cuts the charm like a knife. My hand steadies, my eyes clear.]

n3.speaker: Van Helsing
n3.text: [I am a hair's breadth from her lips when something in my mind screams: 'You are drowning!' I wrench myself back, shaking, drenched in sweat. I must not look so long.]

n0.speaker: Mina
n0.text: Professor, the castle is behind us, the three are at peace, and I am myself again, or nearly. But I feel the Count draw near, as the tide draws in. Can you see anything?

choices.text: Stay in the ring. I shall look from the rock.
They come. We shall see the end of it, Madam Mina.

n1.speaker: Mina
n1.text: Yes. I shall be quiet. But be careful not to fall; the sun is almost down, and I would not have you late.

n2.speaker: Van Helsing
n2.text: [The glass shakes in my hand.] They are racing for the sunset. We may be too late. God's will be done!

do.card: 6 November, an hour before sunset. Four men ride on the plain: Jonathan, Lord Godalming, Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris. Before them, a wagon flogged by Szgany whips, and the dying sun.

n0.speaker: Arthur
n0.text: Jonathan, we have them. I will take the right flank with Seward and rifles at the ready. We pick the first man who raises a knife.

choices.text: Hold the right, Arthur. Cover the escort with the rifle.

n1.speaker: Arthur
n1.text: Right flank, rifle on the escort. For Lucy, and for Mina. Go.

n2.speaker: Arthur
n2.text: I am steady. I have never been steadier. God forgive me if I miss.

n0.speaker: Seward
n0.text: Jonathan, I take the left, wide of the wagon, to keep their horsemen from circling. If I fire at the wolves, they are the lesser danger.

choices.text: Hold the left, Jack. Break the circle if you must.
How much ammunition do you have?

n1.speaker: Seward
n1.text: Left flank, understood. I shall fire over their heads if I can, and between their eyes if I cannot.

n2.speaker: Seward
n2.text: Plenty, and a prayer for each cartridge. We do not need many.

n0.speaker: Quincey
n0.text: Jonathan, we two go for the box. You get the throat, I'll get the heart. If either's down, the other does the job. Shake on it.

choices.text: We go together, Quincey. The kukri first, the bowie after.

n1.speaker: Quincey
n1.text: That's a deal, Jonathan. For Lucy, and for the little lady up there. Let's go.

n2.speaker: Quincey
n2.text: Only a scratch. Don't fuss, Jonathan.

n0.speaker: Szgany captain
n0.text: [He looks at us, at the sun, and back at the box.] Gentlemen, the road is closed. This is a poor man's load and a poor man's journey. I am paid by the day.

choices.text: Stand aside. We have no quarrel with you.
Who is the master you serve?

n1.speaker: Szgany captain
n1.text: [He spits.] A man who pays in gold and watches me with eyes I do not like. I do not stand aside, English. He made us swear. He will make us die before he lets his box be touched.

n2.speaker: Szgany captain
n2.text: I do not know his name. The Count of the castle, they say. If you come between the Count and his house, you will not see another day.

n0.speaker: Quincey
n0.text: I am only too happy to have been of any service. Don't cry, little lady. It was a fair fight.

n1.speaker: Quincey
n1.text: [He took my hand in his feeble one, and smiled.] Oh, God! It was worth for this to die! Look! look!

n2.speaker: Mina
n2.text: [The sun was now right down upon the mountain top, and the red gleams fell upon my face so that it was bathed in rosy light. The men sank on their knees; a deep and earnest 'Amen' broke from all.]

n3.speaker: Quincey
n3.text: Now God be thanked that all has not been in vain! See! The snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!

n4.speaker: Mina
n4.text: [And to our bitter grief, with a smile and in silence, he died, a gallant gentleman. I touched my forehead: there was no mark.]

n0.speaker: Jonathan
n0.text: He was braver than any of us, Mina. He was our friend. And I never said so.

n1.speaker: Jonathan
n1.text: Let us carry him down together. Wherever we go, whatever we call our children, he will be remembered.

n0.speaker: Mina
n0.text: He is a lovely boy, Jonathan. He has Quincey's name and, I think, Quincey's laugh. The scar is gone, and so is the fear. Come and read what you have written.

n0.speaker: Lord Godalming
n0.text: Arthur. Is that the light, or is it the evening?

choices.text: Evening, sir. Dr. Lenox says you must rest.
Your spectacles, sir. I found them under the Bible.
The cordial, sir. Dr. Lenox's evening dose.
There is a telegram from Hillingham, sir.
There is a telegram from Hillingham, sir.
Tell me about the Ring, sir.

n_rest.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_rest.text: Rest? I have rested for forty years in that chair downstairs, and look what it has done to my eyes. Talk to me.

n_specs.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_specs.text: Ah. Now there is a thing. A man cannot be a Lord without his spectacles; the tenants would see right through him.

n_cordial.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_cordial.text: Foul stuff. Lenox swears by it. Well, I shall be brave for you.

do.say: The colour comes back into his face, a little. His voice is stronger.

n_tele_not.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_tele_not.text: I cannot read it, Arthur, with the whole room swimming. Come back when I can see.

n_tele.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_tele.text: '...do not stay away for fear of us.' Then go, boy. Go to her. A Holmwood who waits for a death before he lives has not understood the family business.

n_tele2.speaker: Lord Godalming
n_tele2.text: There is a ring in my desk. Your mother's. And a letter to Mrs. Westenra, in case her heart needs persuading. The key is somewhere in the hall; I hid it from myself years ago and I have been ashamed ever since.

n_ring.speaker: Lord Godalming
